papers.title: Karhunen-Loève Expansion of Time-Rescaled Brownian Bridge and Inference of Unit Distribution
papers.abstract: We study the Karhunen-Loève (KL) basis of the time-rescaled Brownian bridge (TRBB) with time rescales of the form $t\mapsto\int_0^t f^2(s)\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}s$. For testing unit distributions, we construct a new statistic based on the projection of empirical process onto the KL basis functions of the TRBB and derive its asymptotic distribution. Moreover, using this statistic, we develop a goodness-of-fit test for uniformity and study its power against a specific non-uniform alternative. Numerical experiments indicate that, in the settings considered, the proposed test can have higher power than classical alternatives such as the Kolmogorov-Smirnov and Cramér-von Mises tests. Furthermore, we propose a two-parameter family of TRBBs and derive the closed-form KL expansion for this new deterministically time-changed process. The family includes a diverse class of monotone rate time rescales, both increasing and decreasing, while retaining a tractable eigenstructure. Finally, an analysis with real data reveals greater flexibility of the proposed parametric family for modelling monotone densities on $[0,1]$.

papers.title: Bohr inequalities and Landau-type estimates for harmonic Poisson extensions of $L^p$ boundary functions
papers.abstract: This paper establishes sharp quantitative bounds governing the Bohr phenomenon, Landau-type distortion, and geometric univalence for complex-valued harmonic mappings on the unit disk $\mathbb{D}$ parameterized by boundary data in the Lebesgue spaces $L^{p}(\mathbb{T})$ for $1 \le p \le \infty$, where $\mathbb{T} = \partial\mathbb{D}$. First, we resolve the classical coefficient problem for bounded harmonic mappings by incorporating an integral Parseval constraint rather than crude individual bounds, establishing the sharp Bohr radius as $r_H(a) = \sqrt{(1-a)/(3+a)}$ for a fixed initial term $\vert{}a_0\vert{} = aM$. Second, this framework is extended to the $L^p$ setting under the vanishing normalization $f(0)=0$, explicitly characterizing the sharp Bohr radius as $r_{p} = (2C_{q}+1)^{-1}$, where the structural constant $C_{q}$ is intrinsically linked to the conjugate exponent $q$. Finally, under standard normalization, we determine explicit formulations for both the radius of univalence $r_{0}$ and the corresponding radius of the inscribed Schlicht disk $R_{0}$. The sharpness of all analytical constants and radii is verified through the construction of concrete extremal configurations derived from the Poisson kernel.

papers.title: A Coupled Thermomechanical Model with Volterra Memory: Influence of the Kernel Class on Relaxation Asymptotics
papers.abstract: The aim of this study is to determine how the class and asymptotic behaviour of a Volterra memory kernel influence relaxation in a coupled thermomechanical model. The model describes the mutual interaction between an internal mechanical variable and temperature through temperature-dependent material properties and mechanical dissipation. The analysis combines a Volterra integral formulation, a spectral representation of the memory mechanism, thermodynamic decomposition of the hereditary power, local well-posedness analysis, linearization near equilibrium, and Laplace-transform asymptotic arguments. The spectral representation separates the energy stored in the relaxation modes from irreversible hereditary dissipation and establishes the thermodynamic consistency of the memory contribution. Under minimal assumptions on the constitutive functions and the kernel, local existence and uniqueness of solutions are obtained; for thermodynamically dissipative memory and a non-negative external heat source, positivity of the absolute temperature is preserved. The main result concerns the linearized dynamics near equilibrium: with the thermomechanical coupling kept unchanged, an exponential kernel produces exponential relaxation, whereas a power-law kernel with a long tail produces algebraic relaxation. A numerical comparison performed for the same set of dimensionless thermomechanical parameters illustrates these two asymptotic regimes. The results show that changing the class of the memory kernel alone can change the qualitative long-time relaxation law of the coupled system.

papers.title: Time-reflection nonlocal equations from $\mathcal{P}\mathcal{T}$-symmetric oscillator pairs: physical origin and variational formulation
papers.abstract: We show that every second-order differential equation with time reflection describes the $\mathcal{P}\mathcal{T}$-symmetric solutions of a local pair of oscillators that is invariant under exchange combined with time reversal. For linear equations the pair is built from springs, balanced gain and loss, and a gyroscopic coupling. We determine when such a pair has a regular first-order Lagrangian, and when the solutions of the equation fix its coefficients. As the main example, we consider a recently studied equation whose solutions do not depend on its velocity coupling. In the corresponding pair this coupling acts only on the conserved total momentum, which vanishes for $\mathcal{P}\mathcal{T}$-symmetric solutions, and each of the two conditions that single out the model places the pair at an exceptional point. When the spring and velocity couplings are both nonzero, the pair has no regular first-order Lagrangian, while the equation has one with second derivatives. We also propose an electronic realization and construct a Bateman-type Hamiltonian, from which the velocity coupling is removed by a canonical transformation.

papers.title: On a Problem of Erdős and Graham Related to Restricted Order
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be a set of nonnegative integers. We prove that if $A\setminus F$ has a finite order for every finite subset $F\subseteq A$, then $A$ has finite restricted order. This resolves a problem posed by Erdős and Graham in 1980. We also establish a local to global principle to characterize restricted asymptotic bases of finite order.

papers.title: Multiplicativity of Vertex Energy Under the Kronecker Product
papers.abstract: We prove that vertex energy is multiplicative under the Kronecker product. Using this core property, we introduce a unified theorem to compute vertex energies for any graph operation obtained through the Kronecker product. As direct applications, we derive exact vertex energy formulas for semishadow, generalized splitting, and shadow-splitting graphs. Furthermore, we completely classify all blueprint matrices that preserve vertex energies.

papers.title: A $q$-analogue of an inverse problem leading to second-order linear functionals
papers.abstract: R. Sfaxi studied the linear functional $L_ε$ determined by the equation $L_ε-εL_ε'=L$. We replace the derivative by the Hahn operator $H_q$ and study the solution $L_ε$ of $L_ε-εH_q L_ε=L$. For $0<q<1$ we solve the equation explicitly when $L$ is a Dirac mass, and we deduce that $L_ε$ is positive-definite whenever $ε>0$ and $L$ is positive-definite on $[0,+\infty)$. We show that $L_ε$ is $H_q$-semiclassical if and only if $EL=FL_ε$ for two non-zero polynomials $E$ and $F$, and we work out the $q$-analogues of the Hermite and Laguerre examples. Finally we treat the $H_q$-classical functional $K_q$ whose moments are the $q$-factorials: here $L_ε=(1+ε)^{-1}(K_q+ε\,h_{-ε}K_q)$, and for $ε<0$ the functional $L_ε$ is positive-definite if and only if

papers.title: A computer-assisted proof of one-cell snaking and lattice trapping for a nonlinear square lattice
papers.abstract: We establish a computer-assisted proof of lattice trapping in an infinite nonlinear square lattice with interaction potential $φ(t)=(1-e^{-3t^2})/6$ and an antiplane crack far field $K\sqrt{r}\sin(θ/2)$. We construct a connected branch of equilibria whose single-cell segment contains exactly two nondegenerate quadratic folds, with a stability sequence of stable, Morse index one, and stable in the full energy space. The fold loads satisfy $0.45897<K_-<0.45923$ and $0.46219<K_+<0.46242$, establishing a strictly positive lattice-trapping width $K_+-K_->0.00296$. A uniqueness argument establishes exact translation closure and smooth continuation across lattice cells. The proof combines renormalized energy, Schur complement estimates, analytic infinite-tail bounds, interval arithmetic, and exact integer positivity certificates. All finite input data, verification programs, and recorded certificate outputs are provided in the accompanying certificate archive.

papers.title: Besicovitch Pseudo Almost Periodic Stochastic Processes and Their Applications to Delayed Stochastic Neural Networks
papers.abstract: The Besicovitch almost periodic concept is a generalization of the Bohr, Stepanov, and Weyl almost periodic concepts and, in a certain sense, has broader coverage and weaker conditions. However, the concept of pseudo almost periodic stochastic processes in the Besicovitch sense has not yet been systematically proposed, which limits the characterization of the complex oscillatory behavior of a broader class of stochastic non-autonomous systems. This paper proposes the concept of Besicovitch pseudo almost periodic stochastic processes. As an application of this concept, we study the existence of Besicovitch pseudo almost periodic solutions in distribution for a class of stochastic delayed neural networks in which all parameters except the time delays are pseudo almost periodic and establish stability criteria for such solutions in the $p$-th mean sense. The work of this paper fills the gap caused by the lack of the concept of Besicovitch pseudo almost periodic stochastic processes and provides a new conceptual tool and analytical approach for characterizing the complex oscillatory behavior of stochastic differential equations and stochastic neural network systems.

papers.title: Crossed homomorphisms on Leibniz superalgebras
papers.abstract: In this article, we give characterisation of crossed homomorphisms of Leibniz superalgebras as Maurer-Cartan elements of an associated graded Lie algebra. This characterization enables us to develop a cohomology theory for crossed homomorphisms and to apply it to their formal deformation theory. We show that the infinitesimal of a deformation is a 1-cocycle and that linear deformations are classified by such cocycles. Furthermore, we introduce the category of crossed homomorphisms between two fixed Leibniz superalgebras.

papers.title: Constructions and Upper Bounds for Trifferent Codes
papers.abstract: A ternary code of blocklength $n$ is trifferent if every three distinct codewords have a coordinate at which they take all three values. Let $T(n)$ be the largest size of such a code. We prove that $T(n)=Ω(1.162579^n)$ and $T(n)=O(n^{-1/2}(3/2)^n)$. The lower bound improves the exponential base $(9/5)^{1/4}=1.15829\ldots$ of Körner and Marton. It comes from a random system of overlapping local constraints, in which every position is read two or three times, followed by thinning and the deletion of nearby pairs and of the remaining triples that violate trifference. The required estimates reduce to finitely many inequalities, which we verify rigorously by computer. The upper bound improves our earlier bound $O(n^{-2/5}(3/2)^n)$.

papers.title: Why $(4x(1-x))^{3/4}$ approximates the binary entropy so well: a proof of Topsøe's convexity conjecture
papers.abstract: Write the binary entropy as $h(x) = u^{g(x)}$ with $u = 4x(1-x)$. Topsoe (2001) proved the sharp bounds $1/\ln 4 \le g \le 1$, i.e. $u \le h \le u^{1/\ln 4}$, and conjectured that the effective exponent $g$ is convex. We prove this conjecture. In the variable $s = (1-2x)^2$, $g$ extends to a Pick function on $\mathbb{C} \setminus [1,\infty)$ with an explicit positive density on the cut, so that $g(x) = \sum_n γ_n (1-2x)^{2n}$ with $γ_n > 0$ and $(γ_n)_{n \ge 1}$ a moment sequence. Pinelis's monotonicity theorem, Topsoe's power-type bounds and the optimality of their exponents follow as corollaries, together with a classification of all exponents $α$ for which $u^α$ bounds $h$. The proof is by hand except for one inequality in one real variable on a bounded interval, certified by interval arithmetic. As an application we give sharp, certified constants for the approximation $h \approx u^{3/4}$: $-0.0065493 \le u^{3/4} - h \le 0.0080004$ on $[0,1]$.
papers.comments: 13 pages, 4 figures. Verification scripts included as ancillary files

papers.title: Why $2$, $3$, and $5$? Lambert Series, Prime Logarithms, and a $48$-Step Octave for Musical Tuning
papers.abstract: The primes $2$, $3$, and $5$ generate many familiar frequency ratios in musical tuning. We identify three mathematical properties that distinguish these primes in a construction based on modular transformations of Lambert series. We derive an exact identity for $\log p$ for every odd prime $p$, together with a separate identity for $\log2$. Within this construction, all transformed Lambert-series arguments can be chosen real precisely for $p=2,3,5$. In the identities obtained for these three primes, every series argument has magnitude at most $e^{-2π}$, whereas the identity for $\log7$ requires complex arguments and contains a more slowly converging series. The leading $π$-terms for $\log2$, $\log3$, and $\log5$ generate a $48$-step octave grid and recover its conventional prime mapping $(48,76,111)$ exactly, without rounding, while including the leading $π$-term for $\log7$ enlarges the grid to $1680$ steps. The identity for $\log7$ introduces no auxiliary logarithms of larger primes, whereas for every prime $11\le p<20000$, an exact computation identifies such logarithms in the construction. The Lambert-series remainders provide exact corrections for just intervals and musical commas. For a published theoretical model of $22$ Hindustani shrutis, the additive $48$-step mapping assigns all $22$ ratios to distinct positions, with corrections no greater than $15.3$ cents in magnitude. These results establish precise arithmetic distinctions that parallel the prominence of $5$-limit tuning, without implying that number theory determines musical practice.

papers.title: hp-Adaptive Finite Element Modeling of Static Cracks in Density-Dependent Media
papers.abstract: The elastostatic crack-tip fields within a density-dependent continuum are numerically investigated under several macroscopic loading configurations. The governing nonlinear boundary value problem is formulated using an algebraically nonlinear hyperelastic constitutive relationship in which the material moduli are intrinsically coupled to volumetric strain. Existence and uniqueness of the weak solution to the nonlinear displacement-based variational formulation are rigorously established at the continuous level via the Minty-Browder theorem. The variational formulation is then linearized at the partial differential equation level to construct a continuous damped Newton-Raphson scheme. To accurately capture the severe field gradients and internal singularities inherent to this model, the resulting sequence of linear operator equations is discretized and solved via a conforming finite element method within an $hp$-adaptive framework. A comparative analysis is conducted across five distinct boundary loading profiles (encompassing uniform, piecewise-slope, and concentrated point loads) applied to a stationary cracked geometry. Within each configuration, the density-dependent constitutive parameter is systematically varied to assess its regulatory impact on the fracture process zone, focusing on the spatial evolution of normal stress, normal strain, and strain energy density near the crack tip. Numerical results demonstrate that local kinematic deformability is strictly bounded by the strain-limiting nature of the continuum, whereby static equilibrium is sustained through severe, localized stress amplifications. Furthermore, the mechanical influence of the modeling parameter is fundamentally dictated by the topological interplay between internal crack geometry and the spatial distribution of applied macroscopic loads.

papers.title: Bistable waves and propagation success on hexagonal lattice
papers.abstract: Inspired by propagation phenomena occurring on media with hexagonal structures, we propose an idealized system of bistable reaction-diffusion equations posed on a hexagonal lattice, and investigate the existence and speed of traveling wave solutions. We establish a sharp criterion for propagation success (nonzero wave speed) and failure (zero wave speed), where the criterion is determined by an angle-dependent periodic threshold function and the ratio of two parameters in the nonlinearity. Moreover, the sign of the wave speeds is governed by the angle and the parameter ratio. Our results imply that the hexagonal structure and bistability significantly affect the propagation dynamics.

papers.title: Cyclicity of period annuli of quadratic codimension four centers
papers.abstract: Quadratic systems with a center fall into four classes: Hamiltonian $Q_3^H$, reversible $Q_3^R$, generalized Lotka--Volterra $Q_3^{LV}$, and codimension-four $Q_4$. Before this work, the cyclicity of period annuli under quadratic perturbations had been completely determined for $Q_3^H$, whereas only certain special cases had been resolved for $Q_3^R$, $Q_3^{LV}$ and $Q_4$. In this paper, we establish that the period annulus of every center in $Q_4$ has cyclicity three under quadratic perturbations, thereby proving Żoł{ą}dek's 1994 conjecture for this class. The proof combines Picard--Fuchs equations with a Chebyshev criterion. Its key step is a strict Wronskian inequality for two ratios of elliptic integrals on their entire interval of definition. We establish this inequality by constructing a comparison function and excluding a first zero of the Wronskian. The Chebyshev property avoids the two additional zeros allowed by the second-order differential reduction used in earlier proofs.

papers.title: The smallest vertex triangle in a fixed polygon
papers.abstract: Among the triangles determined by $n$ points in convex position in the unit square, one has area at most $32/n^3$. Equality is possible exactly when $4$ divides $n$, and then the maximizing point set is unique. We prove a fixed-container theorem for a class of convex $s$-gons that includes affinely regular polygons and a one-parameter family of pairwise affinely inequivalent hexagons without a centre of symmetry. If the container has equal ears of area $a$ and the tips of its directed side vectors are in convex position, the sharp bound at $n=sk$ is $a/k^3$. Its equality conditions determine every side vector of the maximizing polygon. The proof uses the area enclosed by the normalized side directions. We compare the result with the area-normalized smallest-ear theorem of Gronchi and Longinetti and give consequences for unrestricted Heilbronn configurations with 13 and 15 points.
papers.comments: 7 pages, 2 figures. Supplementary note, Lean formalization, and reproducibility files: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24497708

papers.title: Optimal bounds for the length and number of unit fraction representations
papers.abstract: This paper gives a human-written exposition and simplification of proofs that were recently posted by OpenAI. We prove that every $a/b \in (0, 1)$ can be written as the sum of $O(\log\log b)$ many distinct unit fractions. We also prove that the number of representations of $1$ as the sum of $k$ distinct unit fractions grows doubly exponentially in $k$.

papers.title: On the index of positivity of linear functionals: a complement to the Hermite case and new examples
papers.abstract: We prove that the Dirac functional $δ$ is the only normalized linear functional on the space of real polynomials whose index of positivity is infinite. This complements the recent study of the Hermite case by R. Sfaxi and F. Marcellán [Bull. Malays. Math. Sci. Soc. 48 (2025) 138]: the index of the Hermite functional $\mathcal{H}$ is finite, and so are those of $\mathcal{L}(-1/2)$, $e^{\mathcal{H}}$ and $e^{\mathcal{L}(-1/2)}$, for which the value $+\infty$ was stated there. The key observation is that real Cauchy powers act on log-moments by scaling. This yields explicit upper bounds for the index in terms of the first four moments. In particular $\mathcal{H}^n$ is not even positive for any integer $n\ge 3$, and $2\le \mathrm{Ind}_p(\mathcal{H})\le 5$. We identify the point of the original argument that needs to be modified, a free integration constant in the construction of the weights of $\mathcal{H}^n$, and we give the adjusted statements. Finally, we compute the positivity sets exactly for two new families: the real powers of $δ_c$, which are Jacobi functionals on $[0,c]$, and the real powers of $δ_cδ_{-c}$, which are generalized Gegenbauer functionals containing the Chebyshev functional $\mathcal{T}$. For the latter, $\mathrm{Ind}_p(\mathcal{T})=2$. These examples show that our bounds are sharp and that every value in $[0,+\infty]$ is the index of some functional.

papers.title: The regular polygon maximizes the first positive Steklov eigenvalue among simple polygons at fixed area
papers.abstract: For $N\ge5$ and every simple planar polygon $P$ with at most $N$ sides, $\sqrt{|P|}\,σ_1(P)\le\sqrt{|R_N|}\,σ_1(R_N)$, where $σ_1$ is the first positive Steklov eigenvalue and $R_N$ is a regular $N$-gon. Equality holds precisely for polygons similar to $R_N$. This answers Oudet's fixed-area open problem \cite{AIM} for all $N\ge5$.

papers.title: Simultaneous coordinate-wise Wasserstein central limit theorem in high dimensions
papers.abstract: For independent centered random vectors $(X_i)_{i=1}^n$ of finite fourth moments, we obtain dimension free Wasserstein bound between its normalized sum $W_n = n^{-1/2}\sum X_i$ and a Gaussian whose covariance equals that of $W_n$. The coupling between $W_n$ and the Gaussian is strong in the sense that a single coupling controls controls every projection onto a subset of those eigen coordinates. The proof combines stochastic localization, Hermite expansion on a Gaussian prior with exchangeable pairing. This proves the Conjecture surmised in \cite{fang2026sharp} and improves the coefficient on the fourth-moment term from $2$ to $197/108$. The same Wasserstein error bound extends to real separable Hilbert space. For Hilbert-valued i.i.d. observations, the $L^2$ prediction error bound has an order of $O(n^{-1/2})$, with no dimension factor or restriction on covariance eigenvalue decay, and the same coupling retains bounds for every spectral projection. In an $\ell^2$ example, we demonstrate that the coordinate-wise error gives sharp error order of $n^{-1/2}$.

papers.title: Separable models of an NIP Banach space theory
papers.abstract: Let $Y$ be the renorming of $\ell_2(\mathbb N)\oplus_2\ell_2(\mathbb N)$ with norm $(h^2+q^2)^{1/2}$, where $h$ is the Hilbert norm and $q(u,v)=\sup_{i<j}|u_i+v_j|$. We prove that the unstable theory $\operatorname{Th}(Y)$ is NIP in the pure Banach language. We recover the index order from the Banach norm and classify the continuum many separable models up to surjective linear isometry. The invariants are the order type of a countable model of $\operatorname{Th}(\mathbb N,<)$ and the dimension of a separable Hilbert summand. Every such pair occurs. We describe all elementary embeddings between these models. The bounded norm types over a separable model are separable in the uniform metric exactly when its index order contains no copy of $(\mathbb Q,<)$.

papers.title: Nonzero central quotients of the Virasoro enveloping algebra are simple
papers.abstract: We prove a conjecture of Petukhov and Sierra that the central quotient $\mathrm{U}(\mathrm{Vir})/(z-c)$ of the universal enveloping algebra of the Virasoro algebra is simple for all $c \neq 0$. We extend the result to the $N=1$ super-Virasoro algebras. Our proof reveals a new connection between enveloping algebras and polynomial identity algebras. Although the enveloping algebra itself does not satisfy a polynomial identity, the adjoint action on each filtered piece does satisfy a standard identity. In particular, the Witt algebra $W$, as an adjoint module over itself, satisfies the standard identity $\mathrm{St}_4$, whereas $\mathrm{Vir}$ fails by a nonzero multiple of the central charge. Propagating this gap through the PBW filtration of $\mathrm{U}(\mathrm{Vir})/(z-c)$, for every nonscalar element, we construct an alternating adjoint operator that lowers its order by exactly one. As applications, we compute the annihilators of all representations with nonzero central character, prove a strengthened form of Etingof's conjecture on nonsplit extensions of $W$-modules, and reduce the classification of prime ideals of $\mathrm{U}(\mathrm{Vir})$ to those of $\mathrm{U}(W)$.

papers.title: The Transverse Finiteness Conjecture for pseudo-Anosov flows via universal circles
papers.abstract: We prove Mosher's Transverse Finiteness Conjecture, posed in 1996. This states that every taut, finite depth foliation $\mathcal F$ of an atoroidal 3-manifold is almost transverse to at most finitely many pseudo-Anosov flows, up to orbit equivalence. Our strategy is to organize the flows that are almost transverse to $\mathcal F$ using their associated universal circles. This technique also establishes the following rigidity result: if a finite depth foliation $\mathcal F$ is almost transverse to a pseudo-Anosov flow $\varphi$ without perfect fits, then $\varphi$ is the unique pseudo-Anosov flow that is almost transverse to $\mathcal F$, up to orbit equivalence. In fact, in this setting, $\mathcal F$ has only one minimal universal circle.
papers.comments: The mathematics in this article was developed by the authors without the use of AI

papers.title: Kovács Vanishing for Excellent Log Canonical Threefolds
papers.abstract: We prove a vanishing theorem of S. Kovács for excellent log canonical threefolds whose closed points have perfect residue fields of sufficiently large characteristic. This vanishing theorem roughly says that LC threefold pairs are not far from being rational pairs (in the sense of Kollár \& Kovács and Schwede \& Takagi) if one includes a correction term. We apply this vanishing to prove a depth relation of Chou and resolution-invariance of cohomologies of ``essential divisors" for isolated log canonical threefolds in large characteristic, extending works of Ishii and Fujino. Using examples constructed by Bernasconi and Cascini-Tanaka, we show that these results fail in low characteristic. Finally, we show Kovács and Alexeev-Hacon's result (in char 0) that ``Irrational centers are LC centers" fails in every positive characteristic.

papers.title: Horseshoe-Type Shrinkage from Ratio-Generated Priors
papers.abstract: We develop a class of horseshoe-type shrinkage priors generated by ratios of independent numerator and denominator random variables. Large denominator values produce concentration near zero, small denominator values generate heavy tails, and the numerator determines scale and geometry and may also influence tail behavior. We establish general origin and tail asymptotics, including power and logarithmic singularities. Under a Gaussian likelihood and regularly varying prior tails, the posterior mean approaches the observation for large signals, with risk approaching that of the unshrunk observation. The denominator also induces a latent shrinkage factor. For a Cauchy denominator, this factor has exactly the ${\rm Beta}(1/2,1/2)$ distribution, whatever the numerator. With a Gaussian numerator and appropriate scale calibration, it recovers the classical horseshoe shrinkage coefficient, whereas non-Gaussian numerators can change the effective posterior shrinkage, even in its asymptotic rate. The Cauchy/Cauchy prior illustrates the theory, with a logarithmic singularity at the origin in one dimension, power singularities in higher dimensions, and logarithmically modified Cauchy-order tails. Its posterior mean shrinks smoothly, whereas its spatial median behaves nearly as a threshold rule. We also compare the Cauchy/Cauchy posterior mean with fifteen established shrinkage procedures on the four standard Donoho-Johnstone test functions, finding competitive, though not uniformly superior, wavelet-denoising performance. The ratio construction generalizes several published shrinkage priors and offers a flexible framework for sparse estimation, with natural applications to wavelet shrinkage, variable selection, and structured multivariate shrinkage.

papers.title: Pohozaev identity, nonexistence and existence for mixed local-nonlocal $(p,q)$-Laplacian
papers.abstract: We study the mixed local-nonlocal operator $\mathcal{L}_{p,q}=-Δ_p+(-Δ)^s_q$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$. First, we prove a Pohozaev identity for bounded, continuous weak solutions of $\mathcal{L}_{p,q} u=f(u)$, where $f$ is any continuous function. We impose no growth condition on $f$. Combined with the Nehari identity, this gives nonexistence of nontrivial solutions for nonlinearities that are supercritical, or subcritical, with respect to both operators. For $f(t)=|t|^{r-2}t$, this rules out all $r$ outside the interval between $p^*$ and $q^*_s$. Second, we show that this interval is exactly where solutions exist. When $p^*\neq q^*_s$ and $r \in \left(\min\{p^*,q^*_s\}, \;\max\{p^*,q^*_s\}\right)$, we obtain a nonnegative radial solution by constrained minimization and a ground state by using the Pohozaev identity as a constraint. Finally, we show that the two solutions have the same energy.

papers.title: A Sequent Calculus for the Quantified Reflection Calculus $\mathrm{QRC}_1$: Cut-Elimination, Interpolation, and NP-Completeness
papers.abstract: We introduce $\mathrm{G3QRC}_1$, the first Gentzen-style sequent calculus for Borges and Joosten's Quantified Reflection Calculus ($\mathrm{QRC}_1$). As a strictly positive, first-order modal logic, $\mathrm{QRC}_1$ crucially escapes Vardanyan's $Π^0_2$-completeness theorem for quantified provability logic, while remaining arithmetically complete with respect to Peano and Heyting Arithmetic. The central innovation of $\mathrm{G3QRC}_1$ is a pair of context-erasing modal rules that simultaneously account for the monotonicity and transitivity axioms by deliberately discarding parametric context across modal boundaries. This structural bottleneck allows for a clean proof of cut-admissibility via a standard lexicographic induction, circumventing the complex loop-checking typically required for provability logics. Cut admissibility yields an instantiated subformula property and supports a direct canonical proof of the finite model property. We streamline the adequate Kripke semantics by interpreting constants globally. We also establish a split-context Craig interpolation theorem and a contextual form of left uniform interpolation, uniformly eliminating private predicate symbols, constants, and free parameters. Finally, by leveraging the rigid structural constraints of the context-erasing rules and the absence of left-branching connectives, we prove that, over the standard fixed countable signatures specified in the paper, the decision problem for $\mathrm{QRC}_1$ is $\mathbf{NP}$-complete, situating this quantified modal logic in a comparatively low nondeterministic complexity class.
papers.comments: Originally submitted to the Notre Dame Journal of Formal Logic on 2 June 2026

papers.title: Error estimates for a structure-preserving finite-element scheme of quasi-incompressible Navier-Stokes-Maxwell-Stefan systems
papers.abstract: A conforming finite-element scheme for quasi-incompressible Navier-Stokes-Maxwell-Stefan systems in a bounded domain with periodic boundary conditions is presented. The system consists of the Navier-Stokes equations, together with a quasi-incompressibility constraint, coupled with the cross-diffusion Maxwell--Stefan equations. The numerical scheme preserves the partial masses and the quasi-incompressibility constraint and dissipates the discrete energy. First-order error estimates in space and time are shown for a diffusion-augmented mobility matrix by using the relative energy method and suitable projection error estimates. Numerical experiments in two space dimensions illustrate the convergence of the scheme and indicate second-order convergence in space in the $L^2$ norm.

papers.title: Stark units and cyclotomic Iwasawa theory over complex cubic fields
papers.abstract: For cyclotomic extensions of complex cubic fields, we prove the integral rank-$1$ and rational rank-$2$ abelian Stark conjectures. More generally, we prove a relative theorem on the higher-rank Rubin--Stark conjectures for cubic extensions of number fields. We then apply our Stark unit constructions to the Bergeron--Charollois--García conjectures on elliptic gamma values. Finally, we prove an Iwasawa main conjecture relating norm-compatible systems of Stark units to ideal class groups in cyclotomic towers over complex cubic fields.

papers.title: Graphs with the largest chainable index and their properties
papers.abstract: This paper provides a complete characterization of the set of graphs with the largest chainable index. In particular, it is shown that the number of arcs and vertex degrees of such graphs satisfy strong restrictions. Moreover, graphs with the largest chainable index form five parametric families, and exactly one of them consists of graphs that are not strongly connected. As a consequence, the number of graphs on $n$ vertices with the largest chainable index is computed, and the values of the primitive exponent for these graphs are calculated.

papers.title: Effective bounds for adjoint Bloch-Kato Selmer groups of Hilbert modular forms
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a totally real field and let $Π$ be a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb A_F)$. Under the usual Taylor-Wiles residual irreducibility hypothesis, we prove the vanishing of the adjoint Bloch-Kato Selmer group with characteristic-zero coefficients and give an explicit upper bound for a corresponding Selmer group with divisible coefficients. The argument revisits Wiles's use of level raising at Taylor-Wiles primes. In place of freeness or almost freeness of automorphic cohomology over a Hecke algebra, we compare congruence modules at the original and auxiliary levels and control the part of the Hecke cotangent space detected by the automorphic module. This produces Galois cohomology classes with prescribed ramification at the auxiliary primes. The resulting bounds depend explicitly on congruence data at the original automorphic level and on torsion in cotangent spaces of local deformation rings.

papers.title: Nash-Williams' Orientation Theorems for Infinite Graphs
papers.abstract: Nash-Williams proved in 1960 that every finite multigraph has a \emph{well-balanced} orientation: for all vertices $x$ and $y$, the maximum number of arc-disjoint directed paths from $x$ to $y$ is at least half, rounded down, of the maximum number of edge-disjoint $x$--$y$ paths. In particular every finite $2k$-edge-connected multigraph has a $k$-arc-connected orientation. He announced an extension to infinite graphs whose details, as far as is known, never appeared, and the two statements for infinite graphs have since been known as the strong and the weak orientation conjecture of Nash-Williams. We prove both, for multigraphs of arbitrary cardinality. For multigraphs with countably many edges we obtain more: a well-balanced orientation that is smooth (in-degree and out-degree differ by at most one at every vertex of finite degree) and, if the multigraph is $2$-edge-connected, has infinitely many arcs in each direction across every infinite cut. Such an orientation is obtained by Kőnig's lemma from a sequence of finite orientation problems, each solved by the theorem of Király and Szigeti on simultaneous well-balanced orientations. The infinite cuts are controlled by a canonical tree of $2$-edge-connected pieces with finite cores: once the cores are strongly connected and every finite cut is crossed in both directions, every arc lies on a directed cycle that uses only edges owned by one piece and edges of the cores of its children, and a counting argument of Thomassen does the rest. Neither local finiteness nor ends play any role.

papers.title: Mortgage Backed Securities with p-Laplacian Diffusion and Random Prepayment
papers.abstract: In this note we consider deterministic and stochastic versions of a PDE pricing model for mortgage backed securities, driven by p-Laplacian motion. We show the existence of weak solutions in the $1<p<2$ case, for sufficiently small initial data. In the stochastic case, we consider a random prepayment function, when $p=2$. Herein we derive results concerning the uniform first order sensitivity and mean squared sensitivity of the solution, to the pricing model.

papers.title: The generalized Segal conjecture and the coalgebraic Frobenius
papers.abstract: We prove the generalized Segal conjecture, extending work of Bergsaker and Rognes and confirming a conjecture by the author: for every finite group $G$ and every bounded-below spectrum $X$, the Hill--Hopkins--Ravenel norm $N_e^G X$ becomes Borel-complete after completion at the augmentation ideal of the Burnside ring. Equivalently, for every non-trivial finite $p$-group $G$, the proper Tate diagonal $X\to(X^{\otimes G})^{\varphi G}$ is a $p$-completion. The proof reduces to the case $X=\Fp$, established by Bergsaker and Rognes, and removes the finiteness hypotheses from their theorem by abstract manipulations. As an application of this result, we refine the coalgebraic Frobenius to an oriented circle action (i.e. an action of the monoidal category $B\mathbb N$) on the category of bounded-below, $p$-complete $\mathbb{E}_\infty$-coalgebras, confirming another conjecture by the author. The construction is based on Yuan's approach to Frobenius actions via partial algebraic $K$-theory.

papers.title: The Traveling Salesman Problem with non-convex polygonal neighborhoods: A hybrid Iterated Local Search--Block Coordinate Descent approach
papers.abstract: The Traveling Salesman Problem with Neighborhoods (TSPN) generalizes the classical TSP by requiring a tour to visit a set of regions in the Euclidean plane rather than fixed point coordinates. It has applications in last-mile delivery, surveillance, and remote sensing in precision agriculture. In this paper, we address the Euclidean TSPN with arbitrary, non-convex polygonal neighborhoods---a highly complex setting due to the joint continuous and combinatorial optimization challenges. To solve the continuous subproblem of determining optimal visit points for a given visiting sequence, we propose a Block Coordinate Descent (BCD) method based on solving fast one-dimensional geometric subproblems. Computational experiments demonstrate that BCD computes optimal visit points for a fixed sequence in almost all instances in which optimality is certified, more than six orders of magnitude faster than a commercial solver solving the equivalent Mixed-Integer Quadratically Constrained Programming (MIQCP) formulation. This efficiency enables an effective hybrid Iterated Local Search metaheuristic (ILS-BCD) that thoroughly explores the combinatorial search space at low computational cost. Extensive computational tests on 235 benchmark instances derived from the Generalized TSP (GTSP), with up to 100 neighborhoods, show that ILS-BCD matched or improved upon the best-known GTSP tours in all cases, obtaining strictly shorter tours in 234 instances. On the 80 instances for which optimality is proven, ILS-BCD attains the optimal tour length in all of them, within a relative difference below 0.001%. On 60 larger instances, with as many as 6,325 neighborhoods, ILS-BCD remains competitive up to about 220.
papers.comments: 40 pages, 10 figures, 7 tables. Supplementary material available as an ancillary file

papers.title: Inverse Radiative Transport on Non-Convex Domains
papers.abstract: This paper addresses an inverse source problem for the radiative transport equation in non-convex domains with a single "corner", generated by the union of two convex domains, asking whether an observer restricted to one part of the boundary of such a domain can "see around the corner" and recover a boundary source restricted to a part of the boundary hidden from the observer. The main result shows that with a condition on the geometry of the corner, an analyticity condition on the coefficients of the equation, and a finiteness condition on the scattering kernel, an isotropic boundary source hidden around the corner from the location of the observations can be recovered by measurements of the scattered light.

papers.title: A Perturbative Two-Eigenvalue Faber-Krahn Problem for the Gaussian Short-Time Fourier Transform
papers.abstract: We prove that, for every fixed s\in (0,\infty), the set of area s maximizing the weighted sum of the first two eigenvalues of the associated Toeplitz operators on the Fock space must be a disc, up to translations and sets of measure zero. To do so, we first prove the existence of maximizer sets. Then we show that every maximizer set must be a perturbation of a disc when the weight is sufficiently small. Finally, we use the vector-valued version of the analytic implicit function theorem and the inverse function theorem to conclude that the perturbation must vanish when the weight tends to zero.

papers.title: Gerbe-corrected stringy E-functions
papers.abstract: We define an invariant of $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein complex varieties with at worst log-terminal singularities equipped with a rational Brauer class $α$ that generalizes existing versions of the $α$-corrected stringy $E$-polynomial, which are defined only for quotients of quasi-projective varieties by finite groups. Using recent results from $p$-adic integration, this new invariant can be shown to behave well for degenerate dual abelian fibrations and to agree with the intersection or BPS $E$-polynomial for certain moduli problems.

papers.title: From random intersection to spatial graphs: a unified asymptotic framework
papers.abstract: Random intersection graphs and spatial random graphs provide different mechanisms for generating edges and clustering. We investigate their interplay through geometric random intersection graphs, where vertices are adjacent whenever they share a spatially located group. First, a Poisson decomposition by attachment sets yields exact subgraph probabilities and laws of large numbers for connected subgraph densities. It distinguishes triangles supported by a common group from those requiring three distinct groups. Second, explicit representations of global and average local clustering reveal their different dependence on model parameters and the role of shared groups in edge correlations. Finally, by varying the strength and spatial range of group memberships, we establish convergence to random connection, random geometric, random intersection, Erdős--Rényi, and complete graphs. We characterize the corresponding clustering limits and show that clustering need not converge to that of the limiting graph, highlighting the distinction between spatially local convergence and global graph statistics.

papers.title: Graceful Colorings for Random Graphs
papers.abstract: Given a vertex coloring $c:V(G)\to [k]$, the graceful induced edge labeling is the induced edge coloring $c'(uv):=|c(u)-c(v)|$. A vertex coloring $c$ is a \textbf{graceful coloring} if $c$ is a proper vertex coloring and $c'$ is a proper edge coloring. The graceful coloring number $χ_g(G)$ is the least $k$ such that there exists a graceful coloring $c:V(G)\to [k]$. We study the graceful coloring number for the Erdős-Renyi random graph, $G_{n,p}$. In the diameter $2$ regime, we find the $χ_g(G_{n,p})=n^{1+o(1)}$ using a connection between graceful colorings and Salem-Spenser sets. In the regime where $G_{n,p}$ is connected, but not diameter 2, we find that $χ_g(G_{n,p})=Θ\left(\frac{n^2p^2}{\log np}\right)$, using the forbidden submatching method and a connection between graceful coloring and the chromatic number of the square of $G_{n,p}$. Finally, in the regime where $G_{n,p}$ has constant average degree, we find that $χ_g(G_{n,p})=Δ(G_{n,p})+1$, by exploring the cycle structure of $G_{n,p}$.

papers.title: Non-Amenability of Small Overlap Semigroups
papers.abstract: We prove that every semigroup admitting a presentation satisfying the small overlap condition $C(3)$ is neither left nor right reversible, unless it is the free semigroup on one generator. Consequently, all such semigroups outside this exception are both left and right non-amenable. We also show the optimality of this result, giving examples of $C(2)$ semigroups that are left and right amenable. Our proof makes use of semigroup diagrams, extending the results of Remmers who first introduced the methods as a means of studying small overlap semigroups. We also compare this to the known result that the $C(7)$ condition in groups implies hyperbolicity which then implies non-amenability (excluding the elementary cases). We establish that, for $m\geq 4$, a strongly $C(m)$ semigroup presentation induces an enveloping group presentation satisfying the small cancellation condition $C(2m-6)$, and show that this bound is sharp.

papers.title: Differentiability of the shape function in the planar corner growth model
papers.abstract: We prove that the shape function of planar directed last-passage percolation with general i.i.d.\ real-valued weights is differentiable on the open first quadrant, under a moment assumption of order $p''>4$ on the positive part of the weight and a nearly optimal order $p'>1$ on the negative part. Due to known results, only directions outside a percolation cone need be considered. The proof is a multiscale path-counting argument that uses the shape theorem, oriented percolation on a coarse-grained lattice, a simple change of measure in a finite region, and the van den Berg--Kesten inequality. Our Lean-formalized proof is an AI-assisted adaptation and improvement of the OpenAI proof of differentiability in planar first-passage percolation.

papers.title: Quantitative Convergence of the Nodal Length of Random Trigonometric Polynomials
papers.abstract: We establish quantitative convergence results for the distribution of the nodal length of two-dimensional random trigonometric polynomials with independent and identically distributed centered coefficients towards that of the corresponding Gaussian limiting field. More precisely, we obtain an explicit polynomial rate of convergence. The proof combines probabilistic and geometric arguments. First, we establish quantitative convergence estimates for the underlying random fields. Using a suitable functional representation, this problem is reduced to the quantitative convergence of an empirical field towards a Brownian sheet in a Wasserstein-type distance. Second, Crofton's formula allows us to express the nodal length in terms of the zeros of the restrictions of the random trigonometric polynomials to parametrized affine lines. This reduction makes it possible to adapt one-dimensional arguments based on Kac's counting formula and transfer the convergence estimates for the random fields to the associated nodal lengths.

papers.title: A block coordinate descent method for nonconvex multiobjective optimization under Hölder continuity
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a block coordinate descent method for unconstrained multiobjective optimization problems with possibly nonconvex objectives and Hölder continuous gradients, intended for large-scale instances, in which updating all the variables simultaneously is expensive. In each iteration, only one block is updated along a descent direction common to all objectives, obtained by minimizing the maximum of their regularized quadratic models. We show that, unlike the single-objective case, stationarity on each block does not imply Pareto stationarity, and that no method that updates only the blocks of a partition of the variables and is monotone in all the objectives reaches, in general, an $ε$-Pareto stationary point. Therefore, when none of the blockwise stationarity measures exceeds the tolerance, the algorithm performs a joint step across all coordinates and terminates only at $ε$-Pareto stationary points. We establish a complexity bound of $O(ε^{-(β+1)/β})$ iterations, where $β$ is the smallest Hölder exponent, the same order as that of methods that update all the variables, as well as bounds on the numbers of function and gradient evaluations, which also hold with one regularization parameter per block.

papers.title: Turing instability for periodic reaction-diffusion systems
papers.abstract: This paper is devoted to the study of Turing instability of spatially homogeneous periodic solutions for time-periodic reaction--diffusion systems with Neumann boundary conditions. We first identify three classes of such periodic systems for which the Turing instability does not occur. Then we analyze a class of periodic Riccati equations and give a complete classification of their global dynamics. This result enables us to establish a new criterion for Turing instability in periodic reaction-diffusion systems of predator-prey type. A further comparison with the autonomous case shows that our Turing instability criterion is equivalent to the classical one for spatially homogeneous equilibria, while it is complementary to a criterion for the Hopf-Turing instability.

papers.title: Height function covariance and point-to-line coalescence in the directed landscape
papers.abstract: We prove an integration-by-parts formula for the KPZ fixed point with a deterministic $C_b^1$ terminal reward. For flat data, let $C(x)$ denote the spatial height covariance at time one. For almost every $x>0$, we show that $-C'(x)$ is the probability that the point-to-line geodesics started at $0$ and $x$ coalesce by time one. The proof uses Gaussian integration by parts for the O'Connell--Yor polymer, followed by the zero-temperature and directed-landscape limits.

papers.title: Constructing Large Euler Pseudoprimes through Carmichael Products
papers.abstract: Inspired by recent work on Carmichael numbers and by the construction of Sanchez, et al., we revisit the subset product construction of Alford, et al. We state a theoretical parallel variant of the pushdown algorithm and extend computational records in two ways. First, we construct a Carmichael number that is an Euler pseudoprime to every base up to $1172819$, which includes the first $90968$ prime numbers. Second, we extend the known list of Carmichael numbers with exactly $d$ prime factors from $d \leq 19565220$ to $d \leq 340210163$.

papers.title: Using block coordinate descent for solving the close enough traveling salesman problem
papers.abstract: The Close Enough Traveling Salesman Problem (CETSP) is a variant of the Euclidean Traveling Salesman Problem in which the salesperson must visit some point within a disk associated with each customer. Evaluating a visiting sequence requires determining an optimal visit point within each disk. This building block of virtually every CETSP algorithm is typically computed either by solving a second-order cone programming (SOCP) problem with a general-purpose solver, which can be expensive, or by discretizing the disks, which sacrifices optimality. We propose a block coordinate descent (BCD) method that computes these visit points exactly, without discretization, optimizing one visit point at a time. We show that the resulting single-disk subproblem reduces to a one-dimensional minimization, and we characterize its stationary points through the roots of a quartic polynomial. Of the three resulting solution strategies, which agree up to machine precision, Newton's method is the most efficient. Compared with an off-the-shelf SOCP solver, BCD evaluates fixed tours more than an order of magnitude faster. Embedded in an iterated local search (ILS-BCD), it finds the known optimal solutions of 720 small benchmark instances and, on 62 large ones, outperforms all heuristics of their original study in 47 and matches the best of them in 11 others. Within the memetic algorithm MA-CETSP, replacing the general-purpose SOCP solver with BCD and adding an exact local search based on the single-disk solver yields a method that, over the best of 20 runs, is better than the original algorithm in 20 of the 62 large instances and equal in the others, and improves on its best published values in 21. BCD is a fast and exact building block for evaluating visiting sequences that can replace general-purpose SOCP solvers within CETSP algorithms and enables searches that would otherwise be computationally prohibitive.
papers.comments: 38 pages, 2 figures, 12 tables. Source code available at https://github.com/rsmatos11/berma2026-cetsp

papers.title: Quantifying combined rate- and noise-induced transitions in a multiscale system
papers.abstract: Excitations in multiscale dynamical systems produce persistent but impermanent excursions away from a quiescent state. A novel mechanism for inducing excitations, through a combination of rate-dependent parametric and stochastic forcing, is discussed using the FitzHugh-Nagumo model as an example. In the absence of noise, a quasithreshold separating the state space between supercritical and subcritical behaviour is defined with respect to slow manifolds associated with the metastable excited state. This is formulated in an autonomous system framework, which can be obtained via a compactification of time. Techniques from singular perturbation theory elucidate how canard trajectories shape the geometric structure of the quasithreshold as the system's pullback attractor moves through it. The probability with which weakly stochastically driven sample paths travel through the quasithreshold and undertake (i) solely noise-induced and (ii) combined rate- and noise-induced excitations is estimated numerically for each of the corresponding forcing scenarios, using the adaptive multilevel splitting algorithm. The probability of weak stochastic forcing preventing a rate-induced excitation, which occurs deterministically, is likewise estimated. This quantifies the different rates at which the probability of each transition scenario scales exponentially with the noise strength, in accordance with sample path large deviation principles. It is revealed that a combination of (deterministically subcritical) parametric and stochastic forcing is exponentially more likely to induce excitations than stochastic forcing alone, which is attributed to the pullback attractor and quasithreshold converging towards one another.

papers.title: Vector Quantized Information Bottleneck Mitigation of Adversarial Attacks on Modulation Classifiers
papers.abstract: Radio-frequency (RF) signal processing based on machine learning, including Automatic Modulation Classification (AMC), plays a critical role in Next Generation (NextG) intelligent communications but remains highly vulnerable to adversarial attacks. Prior work explored Variational Information Bottleneck (VIB) as a means to improve robustness, but only in continuous spaces and never for RF classifiers. We investigate the impact of discrete-space information bottlenecks on the adversarial robustness of AMC models. Classification accuracy of attacked modulated RF waveforms is evaluated in two frameworks designed to leverage VIB for adversarial robustness: (i) a two-stage framework where VIB is applied in the preprocessing step using a Vector Quantized Variational Autoencoder (VQVAE) to suppress adversarial perturbations in the process of input signal reconstruction and (ii) a Vector Quantized Classifier (VQC) that leverages VIB inside the classifier proper. The architectures of VQVAE and VQC are identical up to the bottleneck where the VQVAE adds a decoder while VQC utilizes a classification head. We train both VQVAE and VQC with loss functions that we derive from the VIB information-theoretic model. Both frameworks incorporate vector quantization and KL regularization to enforce discrete bottlenecks that filter out adversarial noise. Evaluations under white-box attacks demonstrate that discrete bottlenecks significantly enhance robustness: VQVAE outperforms its continuous VAE (Variational Autoencoder) counterpart, while VQC achieves strong robustness without requiring signal reconstruction.
papers.comments: Presented at the 2026 IEEE International Conference on Machine Learning for Communication and Networking (ICMLCN). To appear in IEEE Xplore. \c{opyright} 2026 IEEE

papers.title: Global dynamics of impulsive reaction-diffusion systems with asymptotically unbounded domain
papers.abstract: This paper is devoted to the study of the global dynamics of continuous-discrete hybrid population models with an asymptotically unbounded domain. We first prove a global attractivity result for a class of impulsive reaction-diffusion equations whose diffusion coefficients vanish asymptotically. A cut-off function is combined with an auxiliary impulsive kinetic system to construct a subsolution that is compatible with the birth update at every cycle. We then use comparison arguments to establish threshold-type dynamics for the original model when the birth function is either monotone or nonmonotone. It turns out that the threshold value for extinction and persistence is explicitly determined by the birth pulse, the within-cycle growth, and the asymptotic expansion rate of the habitat.

papers.title: Stochastic Optimization with Network Distribution Dynamics via Local Jacobian Approximation
papers.abstract: Network systems feature complex interactions among agents, whereby local decisions can influence the state distributions observed by other agents through coupled network dynamics. Such endogenous distribution shifts across large-scale networks pose significant challenges and call for distributed and adaptive decision-making pipelines. To address these challenges and collectively optimize a steady-state performance objective, we propose a distributed network-aware decision-response (D-NAD) gradient algorithm. This algorithm enables each agent to approximate network-response sensitivity using only local information (i.e., the Jacobians of local dynamics and objectives) and neighborhood communication. We establish a non-asymptotic closed-loop convergence guarantee and quantify the impact of the Jacobian approximation errors therein. Numerical experiments on a semi-synthetic networked electric-vehicle price--demand problem demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

papers.title: Nonlocal approximation of stable minimal surfaces with prescribed number of connected components
papers.abstract: We show that every strictly stable classical minimal hypersurface in a Euclidean ball can be approximated, for $s$ sufficiently close to $1$, by a stable $s$-minimal surface in a smaller ball. We also give an explicit lower bound on the size of the interval of admissible values of $s$. As a consequence, we construct stable nonlocal minimal surfaces with an arbitrarily large number $k$ of connected components in a bounded region, under the quantitative condition $k \leq \frac{C}{\sqrt{1-s}}$, attaining an optimal result (at least in dimensions $2$ and $3$). As part of the proof of our main result, we obtain an auxiliary result of independent interest, providing quantitative estimates for foliations of constant mean curvature embedded hypersurfaces near a stable minimal surface. The resulting foliation supplies nonlocal barriers thanks to known results of uniform convergence of the nonlocal mean curvature to the classical one when $s \to 1$.

papers.title: On the non existence of minimal non-uniquely ergodic 4-IETs with flips
papers.abstract: The existence of minimal non uniquely ergodic oriented IETs of n intervals requires that n>= 4 by Th. 2.12 from (W. A. Veech, Interval exchange transformations, J. Anal. Math., 1978); moreover, for n=4 there exist examples of minimal non uniquely ergodic 4-IETs with two independent invariant measures, see (M. Keane, Non-ergodic interval exchange transformations, Israel J. Math., 1977). For the non oriented case, also called IETs with flips, the first examples of minimal non uniquely ergodic IETs were built in (A. Linero Bas and G. Soler López, Minimal non uniquely ergodic IETs with flips, J. Differential Equations, 2023). However, the examples are (10,k)-IETs (k is the number of flips, 1<= k<= 10). Since there are no minimal (n,k)-IETs for n<= 3, it is interesting to decide if, as in the orientable case, there exist minimal non uniquely ergodic IETs with flips and four intervals. Our Main Theorem answers this question in the negative.

papers.title: Estimation for High-Dimensional Hawkes Processes with Inhibition via CIR Approximation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a parametric estimation method for a high-dimensional Hawkes processes with inhibition. The proposed approach relies on a quantitative approximation of the Hawkes process by a Cox-Ingersoll-Ross (CIR) process. In particular, we establish an explicit convergence rate in the joint large-population and long-time regime. This result requires specific techniques to handle the non-Lipschitz diffusion coefficient of the limiting CIR process.Based on this approximation, we construct explicit and easily implementable estimators of the model parameters. We establish their consistency and asymptotic normality. We also conduct numerical experiments to illustrate our findings.

papers.title: Primitive Collections for Klyachko Varieties
papers.abstract: Klyachko introduced a family of $S_m\times S_n$-invariant toric Gorenstein Fano varieties, $X_{mn}$, with connections to representation theory, algebraic groups, and graph theory. He focused on the case in which $m$ and $n$ are coprime, for which $X_{mn}$ are smooth, and hence Fano. Klyachko and Voskresenskii later proved that all forms of $X_{mn}$ are stably rational when $m, n$ are coprime, and that all forms of $X_{mn}$ are rational when $n$ is congruent to 1 modulo $m$. In the same paper, they classified centrally symmetric toric Fano varieties as products of projective lines and generalized del Pezzo varieties, $X_{2,2k+1}$. For this reason, the special case of generalized del Pezzo varieties are frequently studied. For example, Ballard, Duncan, and McFadden proved that the bounded derived category of generalized del Pezzo varieties has a full exceptional collection of line bundles. An understanding of the maximal cones and primitive collections of the fan associated to $X_{2,2k+1}$ is crucial in their construction. In this paper, we focus on the Klyachko varieties $X_{mn}$ in the case in which $n$ is congruent to 1 modulo $m$. We determine a description of the maximal cones and primitive collections for the associated fan. We also determine a description of their cohomology ring and some stability results on the $S_m\times S_n$-orbits of maximal cones and primitive collections for $X_{mn}$.

papers.title: On the Cluster Duration Distribution of the Markovian Hawkes Process
papers.abstract: The duration of a Hawkes process cluster, meaning the time from first point to last point in an entirely endogenously generated progeny stream, has been stubbornly resistant to analysis; even the mean has not been known in closed form. Recently, uniformly random parking functions have been found to be hidden spines of these history-driven clusters, offering a probabilistic combinatorial structure within self-excitement that has opened new avenues for analysis. Here, we leverage and refine this decomposition to provide a closed-form expression for the mean cluster duration in the case of an exponential excitation kernel. Specifically, we reduce from uniformly random parking functions to non-uniform preference counts. This change of probabilistic combinatorial structure in the decomposition leads us to both a Borel-based identity and an explicit integral-based expression for the mean duration.

papers.title: A singular Lawson cone minimizing the fractional perimeter in dimension seven
papers.abstract: We prove that the nonlocal Lawson cone constructed by Davila, del Pino, and Wei (J. Differential Geom. 2018) in $N=7$ minimizes the fractional perimeter for all sufficiently small orders $s$. Thus nonlocal minimal surfaces can have singularities already in dimension $7$. This contrasts both with the classical theory, where the first singular example occurs in dimension $8$ (Bombieri-De Giorgi-Giusti, Invent. Math. 1969), and with the fractional theory for orders $s$ close to $1$ (Caffarelli-Valdinoci, Adv. Math. 2013).

papers.title: Tori without contractible closed geodesics
papers.abstract: We show that a Riemannian 2-dimensional torus has no contractible closed geodesics if and only if it admits a geodesic foliation.

papers.title: A proof of the Nevo-Peeva conjecture: Exact regularity and linear powers of gap-free edge ideals
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph with at least one edge, and let $I(G)$ be its edge ideal over a field $K$. We prove that if $G$ is gap-free, then $\mathrm{reg}\, I(G)^q=\max\{2q,\mathrm{reg}\, I(G)+q-1\}$ for all $q\geq 1$. This answers both open problems of Nevo and Peeva on ordinary powers: $I(G)^q$ has a linear resolution exactly when $q\geq \mathrm{reg}\, I(G)-1$, and their proposed regularity recurrence holds with equality. As consequences, the upper bound $\mathrm{reg}\, I(G)^q\leq 2q+\mathrm{reg}\, I(G)-2$ conjectured by Alilooee, Banerjee, Beyarslan, Hà, Jayanthan and Selvaraja holds for gap-free graphs; every power $I(G)^q$ with $q\geq 2$ has a linear resolution when $\mathrm{reg}\, I(G)=3$; and the stabilization index equals $\mathrm{reg}\, I(G)-1$, which is unbounded on this class. The proof rests on a combinatorial result of independent interest: a parity-sensitive homology vanishing theorem for a filtration of the independence complex by a weighted Hall defect. An internalization lemma and sublevel complexes of submodular functions control the local terms, and Hall's theorem together with an implication-digraph argument classifies the zero level. A capacitated form of the Tutte-Berge formula and Takayama's formula identify the filtration with the degree complexes of ordinary powers. The algebraic statements hold over every field, and the topological vanishing holds with arbitrary abelian coefficients.

papers.title: Normalized ground states for the nonlinear Born--Infeld problem with Sobolev-critical and supercritical growth
papers.abstract: We study normalized solutions to the nonlinear Born--Infeld problem \begin{equation*} -{\rm div}\left(\frac{\nabla u}{\sqrt{1-|\nabla u|^2}}\right) +μu=f(u) \quad\hbox{in }\mathbb{R}^N,\qquad \int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|u|^2\,dx=2m^2, \end{equation*} where $N\ge3$, the mass is prescribed, the frequency $μ>0$ is unknown, and $f$ has Sobolev-critical or supercritical growth at the origin, with no upper growth bound at infinity. We find three thresholds $c_*\leρ_0<\widetilde r_e$ for $m^2$. Normalized action ground states exist for $m^2>c_*$ and do not exist for $m^2<c_*$. Least energy normalized solutions exist for $m^2>ρ_0$, and the energy attains its minimum on the mass sphere if and only if $m^2\ge\widetilde r_e$. In dimensions $3\le N\le6$, we prove that $c_*<ρ_0$ and that the first two existence results hold also for $m^2=c_*$ and $m^2=ρ_0$, respectively. The Lagrange multiplier of the energy minimizers is obtained from an abstract multiplier rule for constrained local minima of functionals with a convex nonsmooth part.

papers.title: The Whitney sphere and tori as self-shrinkers
papers.abstract: We prove that the Whitney sphere in $\C^n$ is a self-shrinker for the Hamiltonian gradient flow of volume. We construct an explicit family of Lagrangian self-shrinking tori in $\C^2$ containing infinitely many pairwise noncongruent examples. We also characterize closed connected Lagrangian immersions whose Legendrian lifts lie in a Korányi sphere by showing that, up to scaling and a unitary transformation, they factor through the Whitney immersion via a diffeomorphism for $n\geq2$ and a finite covering for $n=1$.

papers.title: The squared antipode of a twisted function algebra is locally unipotent
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a proalgebraic group over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic zero, and let $F:{\rm Rep}(G)\to {\rm Vect}(k)$ be a dimension-preserving tensor functor, possibly nonsymmetric. We prove that a tensor automorphism $T$ of $F$ is locally unipotent if and only if its trace on $F(V)$ equals ${\rm dim} V$ for every $V\in {\rm Rep}(G)$. Applied to the Drinfeld element of a dual twisted function algebra $(\mathcal{O}(G)^J)^*$, this proves our conjecture from 2000 that the square of the antipode in $\mathcal{O}(G)^J$ is locally unipotent (arXiv:0002128). Without the trace assumption, we show that for any $V\in {\rm Rep}(G)$ the eigenvalues of $T$ on $F(V)$ determine, modulo roots of unity, its eigenvalues on $F(\mathbb{S}^νV)$ for every Schur functor $\mathbb{S}^ν$. The proof combines the Koszul identity, polynomial growth of symmetric powers, Fourier inversion, and congruences for Newton sums.
papers.comments: 7 pages, latex; the main argument is due to ChatGPT 6 Astra

papers.title: Linear images of graphs of vector-valued affine fractal interpolation functions
papers.abstract: We determine the Hausdorff and box dimensions of every linear image of the graph of a vector-valued affine fractal interpolation function with positive vertical factors. The same formula holds for signed factors under a rank condition on the active branches. Outside an explicit finite union of hyperplanes in the space of vertical factors it holds simultaneously for all choices of interpolation knots and all linear images. The dimension is determined by the branch contractions, the rank of the projected deviations from the endpoint line, and the affine dimension of the projected knots. The proof gives uniform entropy estimates over bounded slopes for tilted projections of homogeneous triangular systems. Permutations of words with prescribed symbol frequencies then transfer the dimension estimates to unequal branch contractions. For the homogeneous systems covered by the entropy estimate, we also compute the exact dimensions of Bernoulli measures and their tilted projections. Examples with exceptional factors exhibit distinct Hausdorff and box dimensions.

papers.title: Singular rational S-functions of second-order ODEs: structure, degree bounds and a Kovacic-type search
authors: L. A. C. P. da Mota
papers.abstract: For a rational second-order ODE $y''=phi(x,y,y')$, the $S$-function method reduces the search for a first integral to finding a rational solution $S$ of the Riccati-type equation $X(S)=S^2+phi_z S-phi_y$ along the total-derivative field $X$. The standard ansatz $S=P/N^k$, with $N=den(phi)$, misses every $S$ with poles outside $N=0$. Such singular solutions cannot be avoided: for point transforms of linear equations without hyperexponential solutions we describe every quasi-regular $S$ explicitly, and for a generic transformation none exists. We then determine the structure of singular solutions. Outside $N$ every pole is simple, with residue $-1$, and is not a Darboux surface; along non-characteristic factors of $N$ the leading polar coefficient is free Cauchy data; and the only unknown denominator is a squarefree polynomial $D$, which enters a linear equation. A Newton-polygon analysis at infinity gives the polynomial part up to a correction of bounded weight. The weighted degree of $D$ is determined exactly when the excess is zero and the top Riccati equation has no algebraic solution, and is bounded by residues of the top field otherwise, conditionally on the vanishing of that correction. The dependence of $D$ on $x$ is obtained, without a degree bound, from the rational solutions of a linear differential system. These results give a certified search procedure, implemented twice, which finds the singular $S$ of nine non-Liouvillian pull-backs of the Airy and Bessel equations. In one regime it is a decision procedure; for instance, it proves that $y''=xy+1$ has no rational $S$.

papers.title: Adaptive Blockwise Tensor Trains for Stochastic Finite-Volume Methods with Uncertain Geometry
papers.abstract: Stochastic finite-volume (SFV) methods extend conservative, shock-capturing discretizations to hyperbolic systems with uncertain inputs by partitioning the parameter domain into finite-volume cells. However, their memory and computational cost grow exponentially with the number of uncertain parameters. Tensor-train (TT) formats can remove this exponential dependence, provided the ranks of the discrete solution remain small throughout the simulation. This requirement is frequently violated when the uncertainty is geometric. Mapping each realization onto a common reference domain introduces parameter-dependent metric factors, so that shocks and contacts propagate at different reference speeds and come to occupy different cells across realizations. The resulting rank growth is spatially localized - a structure that neither a single global TT nor a separate TT for each physical cell is able to exploit. We propose an adaptive blockwise TT representation in which the SFV solution is partitioned along its physical mode into contiguous blocks, each stored as an independent TT for every conserved variable. Blocks are split near discontinuities and in regions of large variance or rank, and merged where the solution is smooth. The mesh itself is never changed; only the grouping of cells into trains adapts. We embed this representation in a TT-based SFV solver combining WENO3 reconstruction in the physical and stochastic directions, positivity-preserving limiters, and strong-stability-preserving Runge-Kutta time integration, with nonlinear steps evaluated via cross approximation. A mean-conservative rounding that adds no rank, together with single-valued interface fluxes, conserves the parameter-mean mass and energy to round-off for any partition. The approach is demonstrated on a Sod shock-tube problem with uncertain wall positions.

papers.title: Stability in abstract classes via set theoretic techniques
papers.abstract: We prove that all abstract classes equipped with an independence relation satisfying a mild local character condition are stable. We obtain the result by using methods from model theory and set theory. We have several applications in the context of abstract classes of modules. In particular, we prove that if $K$ is a class of $R$-modules closed under isomorphisms and pure submodules and $λ^{\operatorname{card}(R) + \aleph_0} = λ$, then $K$ equipped with pure embeddings is stable in $λ$.
papers.comments: 24 pages. Key words and phrases: Abstract Classes; Stability; Abstract Elementary Classes of Modules; Independence Relations; Categories of Models

papers.title: Improving the efficiency of the ratio-of-uniforms method
papers.abstract: In 1977, Kinderman and Monahan showed that under certain conditions, a random variable can be expressed as the ratio $V/U$, where $(U,V)$ is uniformly distributed over a bounded region $S\subset{\mathds R}^2$. Thus, by generating values of $(U,V)$ and computing the indicated ratio, samples from the random variable can be obtained. This procedure is now known as the ratio-of-uniforms method and relies heavily on our ability to produce uniform samples from $S$, for which an acceptance-rejection method is customarily used. In this paper, we propose three sampling schemes based on the polar representation of $S$. The first uses a covering consisting of triangles, the second uses a covering based on circular sectors, while the third employs rectangular coverings of an associated angular density. Numerical examples illustrate that these schemes can achieve acceptance rates close to $100\%$.

papers.title: Inverses of split graphs via Ferrers diagrams and degree sequences
papers.abstract: A graph is a split graph if its vertex set can be partitioned into a clique and a stable set and is a partitioned split graph if the partition is also specified. The inverse of a partitioned split graph is formed by removing all edges within the clique and adding all edges between vertices in the stable set, while preserving the edges between the two parts. In this paper we compare two forms of the degree sequence of a graph: the conventional form and the block representation. We show the effect on the block representation of taking complements of graphs and inverses of split graphs, the latter of which is complicated by the fact that some split graphs have two different inverses. When there are two distinct inverses, we show how the degree sequences of these inverses are related to each other in both the conventional and block representations. We also demonstrate geometric interpretations of these results using Ferrers diagrams.

papers.title: Graphon hitting times: connectivity and minimum degree
papers.abstract: A classical result in random graphs states that the Erdős--Rényi random graph process becomes connected at exactly the moment its last isolated vertex disappears. The main goal of this paper is to establish a graphon analogue of this result. Let $G(n,W)$ be the inhomogeneous random graph sampled from a graphon $W$, and reveal its edges one by one in a uniformly random order. We prove that if $W$ is connected and the lower tail of its degree distribution satisfies $g_W(t)/t\to 0$ as $t\to 0$, which is needed for the connectivity of $G(n,W)$, then the connectivity and minimum-degree-one hitting times coincide asymptotically almost surely. We also determine when this hitting time occurs at scale $Θ(n\log n)$, as in the binomial random graph model. Moreover, we give a simple analytic criterion for the transition to be localized in a $(1+o(1))$-multiplicative window, and construct graphons with minimum degrees arbitrarily close to zero whose transition is nevertheless sharp. Our approach uses Laplace transforms and vague convergence of rescaled graphon degree measures to provide a unified framework for analyzing low-degree vertices and connectivity transitions. Along the way, we revisit the minimum degree of~$G(n,W)$, giving simplified proofs of results of Hladký and Viswanathan~\cite{HV} and establishing the limiting distribution of $δ(G(n,W))$ under a second-order decorrelation condition.

papers.title: Stochastic Optimization for Switch-System Identification under Errors-in-Variables
papers.abstract: In this paper, we address the identification of switched dynamical systems under errors-in-variables, where both input and output measurements are corrupted by noise, and the number of operating modes and subsystem orders are unknown. We propose a unified identification framework that simultaneously estimates the subsystem parameters, latent switching sequence, and model structure. The proposed formulation combines a variance-normalized data-fitting criterion with temporally regularized soft mode assignments and sparsity-inducing penalties for selecting the active modes and relevant input-output lags. To solve the resulting nonconvex optimization problem, we develop an alternating algorithm that incorporates convex mode-assignment updates and proximal stochastic variance-reduced gradient optimization for parameter estimation.
