In the Faddeev-Jackiw framework, a symplectic tensor is constructed from which the fundamental brackets are identified. The HJ and FJ brackets coincide, and from the symplectic tensor, the measure for the quantum path integral is calculated. The differences between the cases $λ\neq \frac{1}{3}$ and $λ= \frac{1}{3}$ at the quantum path integral are discussed.

papers.title: Stability of 3D Stratified Plane Couette Flow: A New Lift-up Mechanism and Potential Vorticity
papers.abstract: Since the pioneering work of Taylor and Goldstein in 1931 laid the foundation for the study of parallel stratified shear flows, non-parallel configurations have received comparatively little attention. We study the stability of the 3D Boussinesq system near the plane Couette flow $V^*=(y,0,0)$ under the vertically stratified background $η^*=αz$. The shear and stratification directions are perpendicular. This geometry produces two structural effects that are absent in the parallel configuration: an additional nonlocal coupling in the non-zero-mode system, which obstructs a directly useful symmetrization, and a wave-shear coupled lift-up mechanism for the zero modes. The transient growth due to the lift-up effect can be suppressed either by sufficiently strong stratification or under suitable assumptions on the initial data. To study the nonzero-mode system, we introduce a reformulation based on the linearized potential vorticity (PV), a fundamental quantity in geophysical fluid dynamics, to recover a better energy structure. We establish the inviscid damping of $u_{1,\neq}$ and $u_{2,\neq}$. We further apply the linearized PV formulation to study the linear stability of the tilted Couette flow. Finally, we use this formulation to prove the nonlinear stability for perturbations on $\mathbb{T}\times\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{T}$ and show that strong stratification can enhance the stability.
papers.comments: Rewrote Section 2.2 and improved Lemma 2.4. Revised the Introduction and split the nonlinear stability theorem into two parts

papers.title: Multiple Zeta Values in Positive Characteristic: A Kaneko-Zagier-Type Conjecture
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study a comparison between $\infty$-adic and finite multiple zeta values in positive characteristic. We construct a surjective comparison map from the algebra of $\infty$-adic multiple zeta values to a quotient of the algebra of finite multiple zeta values. This map factors through the quotient by $ζ_A(q-1)$, thereby establishing the well-definedness of a Kaneko-Zagier-type conjectural map. We further show that the comparison map is compatible with special values of Carlitz multiple polylogarithms, as well as with the corresponding $\star$-inverse values. As an application, we prove the upper bound predicted by Shi's dimension conjecture for finite multiple zeta values.

papers.title: Einstein manifolds and extended Poincaré algebras
papers.abstract: For any pseudo-Euclidean space $V \simeq \mathbb{R}^{p, q}, p \geq 3$, module $W$ over the even Clifford algebra $\text{Cl}^{0}(V)$ and $V$-valued skew-symmetric bilinear $\mathfrak{so}(V)$-equivariant form $Π$ on $W$, V. Córtes constructed noncompact quaternion-pseudo-Kähler homogeneous space. In particular, such homogeneous space is always Einstein and for $p=3$ it is Riemannian. The current paper is devoted to the generalization of this construction for $p = 3$ to the case $p \equiv 3 \pmod{4}$ and an irreducible $\text{Cl}^{0}(V)$-module. As a result we construct the new series of Riemannian Einstein homogoneous spaces $M_{p, q}$ with negative scalar curvature.

papers.title: Sectional category versus module sectional category for retractive maps
papers.abstract: We construct a map between simply connected rational spaces of finite rational type which admits a homotopy retraction and satisfies $msecat(p)=2<secat(p)=3$. The target is the rationalization of a simply connected twelve-dimensional CW complex with eleven cells, and is rationally hyperbolic. This disproves Carrasquel--Vera's conjecture for retractive maps.

papers.title: Hessian manifolds of positive constant Hessian sectional curvature
papers.abstract: Hessian structure on a manifold is a geometric structure consisting of a pair $(\nabla,g)$ of an affine connection $\nabla$ and a Riemannian metric $g$ satisfying certain compatibility conditions. It is also known as a dually flat structure in information geometry. Hessian geometry is considered to be a real analogue of Kähler geometry; in particular, Hessian sectional curvature corresponds to holomorphic sectional curvature in Kähler geometry. The standard models of Hessian manifolds with constant Hessian sectional curvature were classified by Furuhata and Kurose (2013) in the nonpositive curvature case, whereas the positive curvature case is open. In this paper, we classify the standard models in the positive curvature case. For this end, we introduce Hessian structure on quotient manifolds of Kähler manifolds equipped with suitable Hamiltonian actions of abelian Lie groups and realizing the standard models as such quotient manifolds.
papers.comments: 37 pages; corrected Definition 2.7(1), revised the argument in Section 3.5 (with no change to the results), and made several minor revisions

papers.title: Closing the Accuracy Gap in Stochastic First-Order Bilevel Optimization
papers.abstract: We study the stochastic first-order complexity of smooth nonconvex-strongly-convex bilevel optimization with fresh, conditionally unbiased gradient samples of bounded variance. We assume globally $L$-Lipschitz gradients, bounded $f_y$, $μ$-strong convexity of the lower objective, and $ρ$-Lipschitz lower Hessian blocks. Let $κ=L/μ$, $\vartheta=ρ/μ$, and $χ=1+\vartheta$. For $κ\ge2$, $1\le\vartheta\leκ^2$, every initial-gap budget $Δ>0$, and $0<ε\le c\min\{L,\sqrt{LΔ}\}$, we establish $\mathsf{T}_{\mathrm{SFO}}(ε)=\widetildeΘ(Lχκ^{5/2}Δε^{-2}+Lκ^4σ_f^2Δε^{-4}+L^3\vartheta^2χκ^8σ_g^2Δε^{-6})$, where $σ_f^2$ and $σ_g^2$ are the upper- and lower-level variance budgets. The comparison assumes a finite lower-initialization certificate, holds uniformly over both nonnegative noise budgets, and uses an accuracy constant $c$ independent of conditioning. Three lower-bound families capture the deterministic, upper-noise, and lower-noise contributions. The bounds cover arbitrary randomized adaptive queries and terminal outputs under worst-case expected costs, even for conservative sample gradients. The upper bound combines accelerated frozen-linear-tilt solves with displacement-based reuse of the full upper gradient. An independently chosen base-chain length yields the uniform accuracy range, while a projection and homotopy argument separates undisclosed coordinates from a newly disclosed source, allowing $\vartheta/κ$ to grow without bound. The bounds match polynomial orders and noise transitions; exact logarithmic exponents and coarser accuracies remain open.

papers.title: Generalized Gelfand-Cetlin data and abelianization
papers.abstract: The Hamiltonian-geometric analogue of restricting a complex representation of a compact connected Lie group $G$ to a maximal torus $T\subset G$ is symplectic implosion, as developed by Guillemin-Jeffrey-Sjamaar. The first author and Weitsman studied the effect on this analogy of replacing $T$ with a Gelfand-Cetlin torus. In particular, they identified symplectic quotients by $G$ at generic levels in $\mathfrak{g}^*_{\mathrm{reg}}$ with symplectic quotients by a Gelfand-Cetlin torus. On the other hand, the applicability of this result is limited to Hamiltonian $G$-spaces whose moment images intersect $\mathfrak{g}^*_{\mathrm{reg}}$. The purpose of the present work is to remove that constraint altogether. We construct generalized Gelfand-Cetlin data for each orbit-type stratum $Σ\subset\mathfrak{g}^*$. Each datum determines a Gelfand-Cetlin torus and a Hamiltonian action of that torus on an open subset of every connected Hamiltonian $G$-space whose principal orbit-type stratum is $Σ$. Our generalized abelianization theorem gives canonical isomorphisms of stratified symplectic spaces between reductions by $G$ at generic levels in $Σ$ and corresponding reductions by the Gelfand-Cetlin torus. Using symplectic implosion, we extend the Gelfand-Cetlin abelianizations of the first author and Weitsman to non-regular elements of $\mathfrak{g}^*$. We subsequently illustrate this theorem by using the first author and Mayrand's theory of symplectic reduction along a submanifold to construct a canonical family of Hamiltonian $G$-spaces whose moment images lie entirely outside the regular locus. The positive-dimensional reductions of these spaces are realized as reductions by Gelfand-Cetlin tori.

papers.title: Descartes' rule of signs for polynomial systems
papers.abstract: The classical Descartes' rule of signs bounds the number of positive roots of a real polynomial in one variable by the number of sign changes of its coefficients. This bound only depends on the order of the exponents and on the signs of the coefficients, that is, on the oriented matroids of the exponent and coefficient matrices. We generalize this rule to fewnomial systems with any number of monomials: for systems of $n$ real polynomial equations in $n$ variables with $n+k+1$ monomials, we obtain upper bounds for the number of nondegenerate positive solutions which only depend on sign conditions on the maximal minors of the coefficient matrix and of the exponent matrix and its liftings. For $k=1$ they are the Descartes' rules of signs for circuits of Bihan--Dickenstein and Bihan--Dickenstein--Forsgård. Our approach starts from the Gale duality and the Khovanskii--Rolle argument of Bihan and Sottile, which reduce the problem to counting common zeros of iterated Jacobians in a chamber $Δ$ of a hyperplane arrangement determined by the coefficients. We bound this number by the Bézout number minus the zeros forced in the other chambers by a topological degree, which we compute by a facet-count formula involving signs of minors of a Gale dual matrix of the exponent matrix. This leads to a recursion over the flats of the arrangement, which ends with the Descartes' rules for circuits. Restricting the recursion to coherent chambers, in which no cancellation occurs in the facet-count formula, gives weaker bounds in closed form.
papers.comments: 47 pages. v4: revised and reorganized version, with a new title (previously "Descartes' rule of signs for arbitrary fewnomial systems"); the more technical proofs are now gathered in an appendix

papers.title: Differential operator approach to the $\imath$Howe duality
papers.abstract: The iHowe duality for iquantum groups of type AIII/IV was established in \cite{LX22} via two approaches, based on partial flag varieties and quantum coordinate coalgebras respectively. In this paper, we provide a new construction of this iHowe duality via quantum differential operators. Moreover, by deriving explicit action formulas, we prove that our construction coincides with the two constructions given in \cite{LX22}.

papers.title: Galois coinvariants and fundamental groups of arithmetic schemes
papers.abstract: We investigate the structure of étale fundamental groups of arithmetic schemes over rings of integers of number fields. We show that the image of the geometric étale fundamental group is FAb, while the kernel of the map to the fundamental group of the base need not be FAb or finitely generated. Our results rely on finiteness theorems for Galois coinvariants of geometric étale fundamental groups and étale cohomology over finitely generated fields. These apply to Galois extensions $L/k$ for which $\mathrm{Gal}(L/k)^{\mathrm{ab}}$ has finite exponent. As a further application, we establish finiteness of prime-to-characteristic $L$-rational torsion on abelian varieties over $k$.

papers.title: A characterization of central extensions relative to n-nilpotent objects
papers.abstract: We characterize the central extensions, in the sense of the categorical theory of central extensions of Janelidze and Kelly, relative to the Birkhoff subcategory of $n$-nilpotent objects of a semi-abelian and algebraically coherent category. An extension $f \colon A \to B$ with kernel $K$ turns out to be central precisely when the iterated Huq commutator $[A,[A,\dots,[A,K]\dots]]$, with $n$ occurrences of $A$, vanishes. For $n=2$ this condition reads $[A,[K,A]] = 0$, that is, $[K,A]$ is a central subobject of $A$. In the special case of groups this description was obtained by Everaert and the first author. The present proof is categorical, and applies in particular to Lie algebras, to crossed modules, to cocommutative Hopf algebras over a field, and to any category of interest. We also show that, in an arbitrary semi-abelian category, an extension $f \colon A \to B$ with kernel $K$ is central relative to the Birkhoff subcategory of two-nilpotent objects, defined by means of the ternary Higgins commutator, precisely when the ternary Higgins commutator $[K,A,A]_{\mathsf{Hig}}$ vanishes; a similar characterization holds in the $n$-nilpotent case.
papers.comments: 23 pages. Section 6 has been added: it contains some new results concerning the Higgins commutator

papers.title: Restriction estimates using multilinear Kakeya
papers.abstract: We use multilinear Kakeya estimates to establish restriction estimates for the paraboloid in dimensions $n\ge5$. The proof inserts Zahl's multilinear Kakeya estimate for direction-separated tubes into the two-ends method of Wang and Wu by means of a broad--narrow argument. In several dimensions, including $n=9$, the resulting exponents were the best known before the recent proof of the local smoothing conjecture by OpenAI.

papers.title: Nearly sharp $W^{1,\infty}$ stability of polynomial spectral Ritz projections
papers.abstract: For the first time, we establish nearly sharp $W^{1,\infty}$ stability estimates for the Legendre spectral Ritz projection associated with the Laplacian on a square domain. The $W^{1,\infty}$ operator norm of this projection is of order $N^{1/2}$, up to logarithmic factors, where $N$ is the polynomial degree. The upper bound uses a resolvent representation of the discrete gradient projection and a rank-two comparison controlled by terminal-column energy estimates. The lower bound follows from an explicit zero-trace polynomial whose Ritz projection is computed exactly. As an application, we derive sharp maximum-norm error estimates for the Poisson and heat equations.

papers.title: SL(n)-covariant symmetric tensor valuations on polytopes
papers.abstract: All $\operatorname{SL}(n)$-covariant symmetric tensor valuations on convex polytopes in $\mathbb R^n$ are completely classified without any continuity assumptions. It is shown that the only such valuation is the moment tensor.

papers.title: The geometric exceptional set for Fano threefolds
papers.abstract: We study the geometric exceptional set in Manin's conjecture for smooth Fano threefolds. We prove that every adjoint rigid surface with $a$-invariant one on a non-product smooth Fano threefold is normal. This yields a description of the geometric exceptional set in terms of the higher-$a$ locus, anticanonical conics, and del Pezzo fibrations. Zariski density arises only from the latter two contributions. For del Pezzo fibrations, we construct a finite collection of parameter covers which control the associated breaking maps. We classify their low-genus components for general smooth Fano threefolds, yielding examples with potentially Zariski dense geometric exceptional sets in $22$ of the $105$ deformation families. Extending the construction of Batyrev and Tschinkel, we give examples of Fano fourfolds with quartic del Pezzo fibrations and an explicit Fano threefold with two del Pezzo fibrations of degree six. All these varieties have Zariski dense geometric exceptional sets. For the threefold, the original form of Manin's conjecture fails on every nonempty open subset for every anticanonical height.

papers.title: Graded Structures of $v$-adic Carlitz Multiple Polylogarithms and $v$-adic Multiple Zeta Values
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study $v$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms and $v$-adic multiple zeta values. We prove that, for every finite place $v$ of $\mathbb{F}_q(θ)$, the natural weight gives a graded structure on the algebras generated by these values. Moreover, we show that every $\overline{\mathbb{F}_q(θ)}$-linear relation among these values arises from an $\mathbb{F}_q(θ)$-linear relation. In particular, our results establish a function field analogue of the Furusho-Yamashita direct sum conjecture and extend Chen's work from finite places of degree one to arbitrary finite places.

papers.title: Functional limit theorems for self-interacting random walks
papers.abstract: We consider a wide class of nearest neighbor self-interacting random walks on $\mathbb{Z}$ and show that, under mild conditions, their scaling limits at the process level can be uniquely identified and constructed directly from the augmented joint Ray-Knight theorem for their local times, i.e., the joint convergence of rescaled local time ``curves'' of the walks stopped at certain stopping times together with the merge and absorption times of these ``curves'' to a concatenation of coalescing reflected-absorbed diffusions and their merge and absorption times. We apply our results to polynomially self-repelling walks introduced and studied in the mid-90s by B. Tóth, and to ``true'' self-avoiding walks with bond repulsion. The first application solves a problem that has been open since Tóth's work: it gives a construction and first properties of a new family of processes, polynomially self-repelling motions, as scaling limits of polynomially self-repelling walks. These processes were simultaneously and independently constructed from flows of correlated powers of Bessel processes by Y. Yu. The second application strengthens an earlier result on convergence of rescaled ``true'' self-avoiding walks to the ``true'' self-repelling motion of B. Tóth and W. Werner, and streamlines its proof. Our results can be thought of as an ``inversion'' of the augmented joint Ray-Knight theorem to get a functional limit theorem for self-interacting random walks.

papers.title: Topological degree of sparse polynomial maps
papers.abstract: We consider maps $F\colon\R^n_{>0}\to\R^n$ whose components are real polynomials, possibly with real exponents, with the same support $\A$, and we study the topological degree of $F$. We prove a real analogue of the Bernstein--Kushnirenko--Khovanskii theorem, which says that the number of solutions in the complex torus is the normalized volume of the Newton polytope when there is no solution at infinity. Our main assumption is a half-space condition on the columns of the coefficient matrix indexed by the faces of the Newton polytope. It is a positive analogue of the absence of solutions at infinity, and it is satisfied for generic exponents and coefficients. Under this condition, we show that the topological degree only depends on the oriented matroids of the exponent and coefficient matrices restricted to the vertices of the Newton polytope. We give two closed formulas for it: a sum over the facets of the Newton polytope, and a Viro formula, which is a signed count of the positively decorated simplices of a regular triangulation of $\A$. As a consequence, we get sign conditions for the existence of positive solutions, as well as parity results for their number.
papers.comments: 18 pages. v2: the paper has been split into two papers.The Gale dual formula, the Descartes' rule of signs, the fewnomial bounds and the symmetry results are now in a companion paper, "Descartes' rule of signs for the topological degree". Title changed (previously "Topological degree of fewnomial maps")

papers.title: Failure of noncommutative Rota's theorem with $L(\log L)^α$ endpoint
papers.abstract: For every $1\leα<2$, we construct a factorizable Markov map $T$ on a hyperfinite finite von Neumann algebra and a positive element $x\in L(\log L)^α$ for which the sequence $T^n(T^*)^n x$ does not converge bilaterally almost uniformly. In particular, this answers a question of Anantharaman-Delaroche \cite{AD2006} concerning the $L\log L$ endpoint.
papers.comments: 18 pages, Title change, results strengthened to $L(\log L)^α$ counter-example

papers.title: Off-diagonal Ramsey numbers of $3$-graphs
papers.abstract: A $3$-graph (meaning a $3$-uniform hypergraph) $H$ is iteratively $3$-partite if $H$ is isomorphic to a subgraph of some lexicographic power of a single hyperedge. We prove a conjecture of Conlon, Fox, Gunby, He, Mubayi, Suk, Verstraëte, and Yu, that for a $3$-graph $H$, the off-diagonal Ramsey number $R(H,n)$ is polynomial in $n$ if and only if $H$ is iteratively $3$-partite. As an immediate corollary, we also obtain a resolution of a 2009 problem of Bohman, Frieze and Mubayi, asking for a characterization of all $3$-graphs $H$ for which the minimum number of hyperedges in an $H$-free $3$-graph with chromatic number greater than $k$ is $k^{3+o(1)}$ as $k\to\infty$. We prove a $3$-graph $H$ has the latter property if and only if $H$ is not iteratively $3$-partite.
papers.comments: This version largely reverts to v1, with minor adjustments. It also resolves, as an immediate consequence of the main result, a problem posed by Bohman, Frieze and Mubayi in 2009. Version 2 is obsolete

papers.title: Hodge--Deligne polynomials and $S_n$-representations on the cohomology of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n}$
papers.abstract: We compute the Hodge-Deligne polynomials of the moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n}$ of stable $n$-pointed curves of genus two, together with the action of the symmetric group $S_n$ on their cohomology, for all $n$. Using Hassett's moduli spaces of weighted pointed curves, we first show that the generating function of the $S_n$-equivariant Hodge-Deligne polynomials of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$ is obtained from that of the moduli spaces of minimally weighted pointed curves by plethysm with the explicit symmetric function $Z=h_1-\sum_{k\ge3}(x+x^2+\dots+x^{k-2})h_k$; numerically, this is an explicit change of variables. The latter spaces map to $\overline{\mathcal M}_g$, and over each boundary stratum they are built from punctured universal curves and Losev-Manin spaces. Combining the stratification by stable graphs with Burnside's formula and twisted characteristics, we obtain in genus two a closed formula whose only non-elementary input is the cohomology of symplectic local systems on $\mathcal M_{1,1}$ and $\mathscr A_2$, known by work of Eichler-Shimura and Petersen. This determines the $S_n$-representations on all $H^{p,q}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n})$ for $n\le 19$ and on all even degree $H^{p,q}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n})$ for every $n$. We carry out the computation in all degrees for $n\le 18$, where it agrees with an independent computation by point counts, and in even degrees for $n\le 30$. As an application, we find that the even degree cohomology of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n}$ is of Hodge-Tate type if and only if $n\le 20$: the space $H^{23,1}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,21})$ is the multiplicity free $S_{21}$-representation with Frobenius characteristic $s_1\cdot h_2[e_{10}]$, of dimension $1939938$, so that $H^{24}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,21})$ is not spanned by algebraic cycle classes.
papers.comments: 29 pages, Remark 4.3 about a related work is added

papers.title: A simple construction of smooth counterexamples to the Loewner and Carathéodory conjectures
papers.abstract: In a recent announcement, Alpöge presented smooth counterexamples to the Loewner and Carathéodory conjectures and credited John-Paul Smith. We present a simpler construction of a seed by using trigonometric functions. Using this, for every positive integer $k$, we construct a smooth real-valued function on the plane, flat at the origin, whose Hessian eigenline fields share the origin as an isolated singularity of index $1+k/2$. A support-function parametrization realizes this index as an umbilic index of a non-real-analytic $C^\infty$-regular surface germ in Euclidean $3$-space. The same framework, applied to a rapidly decreasing function on the whole plane, gives a strictly convex closed regular surface with exactly one umbilic, of index $2$. This paper is self-contained with regard to the existence of an isolated umbilic of index $2$ and the construction of a counterexample to the Carathéodory conjecture.

papers.title: Initialization Stability and Convergence of Projected Langevin Dynamics
papers.abstract: The entropic regularized optimal transport (EOT) plays a fundamental role in the computation of optimal transport. In \cite{CLP}, the authors proposed a gradient flow approach to EOT, and derived a projected Langevin diffusion that converges in distribution to the solution of EOT when initialized with a coupling between the two given marginals. In this paper, motivated by samplings of optimal couplings for EOT, we analyze the projected Langevin dynamics with arbitrary initial distribution, and prove that its long time behavior is the same as if it was initialized from a coupling.

papers.title: An $L^p$ Version of Raeburn's Symmetric Imprimitivity Theorem
papers.abstract: Let $1\leq p<\infty$. We prove an $L^p$-operator analogue of Raeburn's symmetric imprimitivity theorem for countable discrete groups. Let $A$ be an $L^p$-operator algebra with a contractive two-sided approximate identity, admitting a nondegenerate isometric representation on a $σ$-finite $L^p$-space. Given commuting free and proper actions of groups $G$ and $H$ on a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff space $Z$, together with commuting isometric actions on $A$, we show that the two corresponding full crossed products, and likewise the two reduced crossed products, are Morita equivalent as Banach algebras. The proof is organized through the linking groupoid. Its main analytic ingredient is a coefficient-valued spatial matrix dilation; in the reduced case we prove that this dilation preserves regularity after a Borel reindexing of the opposite corner. A pairing-valued approximate identity yields fullness and nondegeneracy.
papers.comments: 29 pages, 1 figure. Substantially revised with simplified proofs of both the full and reduced symmetric imprimitivity theorems. Several technical arguments have been clarified. The main results remain unchanged

papers.title: Bulk gap stability and spectral flow for fermions with weak long-range interactions
papers.abstract: We prove that weak long-range many-body interactions preserve the bulk gap of a free fermion system and that a quasi-local spectral flow transports the free ground state to ground states of the interacting system. Let $Φ_h$ be a free fermionic interaction, possibly including pairing terms, whose infinite-volume Majorana coefficient operator $h$ has no spectrum in $(-g,g)$, and let $\mathcal V$ be an even self-adjoint many-body interaction. For sufficiently small $|λ|$, we construct pure ground states $ω_λ$ of the interacting bulk system $Φ_λ=Φ_h+λ\mathcal V$ and quasi-local automorphisms $β_{0,λ}$ such that $ω_λ=ω_0\circβ_{0,λ}$, where $ω_0$ is the free ground state of $Φ_h$. Each $ω_λ$ has a GNS Hamiltonian with gap at least $g-C_*|λ| \|\mathcal V\|_*$, where $\|\cdot\|_*$ is the relevant interaction norm. Our result allows polynomial decay of both the free coefficients and the many-body interaction. For two-site interactions on a uniformly discrete point set $Γ\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, a sufficient condition is decay as $(1+|x-y|)^{-\varpi}$ with $\varpi>2d$, for both the hopping and pairing coefficients and the interaction terms. The spectral-flow generator preserves the spatial exponent of the polynomial interaction norm, and its automorphisms satisfy locality bounds at that exponent. If $h$ and $\mathcal V$ have stretched-exponential decay, so does the spectral-flow generator. The proof constructs the spectral flow and establishes the gap through an excitation-number comparison, using polynomial propagation bounds for evolved interactions proved in a companion paper.
papers.comments: v2: updated arXiv references to companion papers

papers.title: Cycles and Symmetries of Non-Transitive Dice with Minimal and Uniform Winning Advantages
papers.abstract: We consider non-transitivity among dice with \(n\) sides restricted to taking face values in the set \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\). We investigate properties of the directed graphs arising from minimal and uniform winning advantages, including embeddings, isolated vertices and an involutive antiautomorphism. For every \(n\geq9\), we construct a non-transitive triple admitting no pairwise ties with uniform and minimal winning advantage. Moreover, for every \(n\geq7\), we construct a non-transitive triple which is invariant under the involutive antiautomorphism. We consider a two-player game utilizing these constructions and investigate the winning probabilities as \(n\) increases. We give a computer-assisted proof that \(n=6\) is the smallest \(n\geq3\) which admits a non-transitive cycle of maximum length \(n\) with uniform and minimal winning advantage, and identify the two unique such cycles. Finally, we present computational evidence supporting a conjecture that \(n=6\) is also the largest such \(n\).
papers.comments: 21 pages, added results that was meant to be a second preprint but now combined into one for more cohesive presentation. 21 pages, 2 figures

papers.title: Integral permutation twisted cohomology: one auspicious twist is all you need
papers.abstract: We introduce a reduced form of permutation twisted cohomology for the derived category of permutation modules over any commutative ring. Unlike the twisted cohomology rings previously constructed by Balmer--Gallauer and Miller, this reduced twisted cohomology ring is only bigraded, twisted by a single, well-chosen endotrivial complex corresponding to the representation sphere arising from the (doubled) regular real representation of a group. We prove that over any commutative ring, the Balmer spectrum of the derived category of permutation modules is homeomorphic to the projectivization of the spectrum of the reduced twisted cohomology ring. Moreover, we show that if the base ring is Noetherian, this ring is finite over the finitely generated subalgebra generated by the forerunners, certain $p$-local isomorphisms, of the twist. We apply these results to further analyze the geometry of permutation modules, determine the local Picard group of the geometric open of the Balmer spectrum, and resolve other questions posed by Miller. We include an appendix giving a general criterion for finite generation of twisted cohomology rings in tensor-triangular geometry.
papers.comments: v2: Major update with stronger results. We show the Balmer spectrum of the derived category of permutation modules over any commutative ring is homeomorphic to the projectivization of a bigraded permutation twisted cohomology ring. We also prove Noetherianity of the ring and a general criterion for finite generation of twisted cohomology. 45 pages, comments welcome

papers.title: Nondegeneracy of low-energy nodal solutions to the Yamabe equation
papers.abstract: We study the linearized Yamabe equation in $\R^n$, or equivalently on $\s^n$, at a low-energy sign-changing solution with two nodal domains. We consider odd dimensions $n=2k-1$ and a solution invariant under $Γ=O(k)\times O(k)$. Its regular level sets are isoparametric hypersurfaces, which foliate the sphere away from the two focal submanifolds. This symmetry reduces the equation for the solution to a singular ODE. In the balanced case, we choose a single-node profile that is odd under reflection across the midpoint. We prove nondegeneracy in the $Γ$-invariant subspace for every $k\ge2$, and in the full space $H^1(\s^n)$ for sufficiently large $k$: every kernel element is generated by a conformal invariance of the equation. The proof uses separation of variables, Wronskian identities and comparison functions adapted to the singular equations for the angular modes.

papers.title: The virial--Kato method and the asymptotic stability of solitons of the generalized Benjamin, Bona and Mahony equation
papers.abstract: We prove that every orbitally stable soliton of the pure-power generalized Benjamin--Bona--Mahony (gBBM) equation is locally asymptotically stable. For both nonlinearities $f(u)=|u|^{p-1}u$ and $f(u)=|u|^p$, the result holds for every exponent $p>1$ throughout the orbital stability range $c>c^*(p)$. Solutions starting sufficiently close to one of these solitons in the energy space converge locally in a moving frame to a nearby soliton and the limiting soliton has a speed close to that of the initial soliton. This establishes, for pure-power gBBM, the local convergence predicted by Bona and Soyeur's asymptotic stability conjecture and addresses an open problem raised by Martel. The proof uses Kato smoothing to close the high-energy virial estimates. The required smoothing estimates rely on the absence of nonzero embedded eigenvalues of the linearized operator. We establish this spectral property for every $p>1$ and every soliton speed $c>1$, including speeds for which the soliton is orbitally unstable. This settles a Pego--Weinstein spectral conjecture in the pure-power gBBM case.

papers.title: Separation points and pressure gradients for the nonstationary Stokes system with localized boundary data in the half-space
papers.abstract: We study separation points of the nonstationary Stokes system in a half-space with zero initial data and nonnegative, space-time separable boundary data supported in the unit ball and in $[0,1]$, respectively. A separation point is a pair $(x',t)$, with $x'$ outside the spatial support, arbitrarily near which a velocity component takes both signs. The main ingredient is an explicit representation of the velocity and pressure via confluent hypergeometric functions. For normal boundary data, if the temporal boundary data are regular and unimodal, log-concavity yields a unique separation time for the $i$th tangential component at every boundary point with $|x_i|>1$, and exactly two for the normal component at distant points, one before and one after the boundary data vanish. The later one, a simple zero of the second normal derivative of the normal component at the boundary, is unique even without unimodality. We obtain monotonicity and asymptotics of separation times and vanishing rates of normal derivatives. For tangential boundary data with $n\geq3$, under the same assumptions, a separation time for the velocity component in their direction exists at $x'$ with $|x'|>1$ precisely when the corresponding Riesz transform of the spatial boundary data has a positive derivative in that direction at $x'$, and log-concavity makes it unique. For the remaining components, we prove existence and uniqueness of separation points on distant lines parallel to the axes, with asymptotics in terms of spatial moments and support geometry. For radial spatial boundary data, we determine the signs and zero sets of tangential pressure derivatives.

papers.title: A linear edge bound for k-quasi-planar graphs
papers.abstract: We prove the $k$-quasi-planar graph conjecture for topological drawings. For every integer $k\ge 2$, a simple graph on $n\ge 3$ vertices admitting a drawing with no $k$ pairwise crossing edges has at most $1056(k-1)^2(n-2)$ edges. Thus the number of edges is linear in $n$, with an explicit quadratic dependence on $k$. The result allows multiple crossings between the same pair of edges, including edges with a common endpoint. The proof uses the double of a sphere with boundary to represent graph edges by closed geodesics on a hyperbolic surface. The endpoints of geodesic lifts induce partial orders of width at most $k-1$. A stability bound for greedy chain partitions, together with a counting argument over a triangulation, gives the stated edge bound.
papers.comments: 12 pages, 6 figures. Superseded by the joint paper "Polynomial bounds for quasiplanar graphs" (arXiv:2611.21416)

papers.title: The proof of the Harary--Hill conjecture: a detailed exposition and an extension to rotation systems
papers.abstract: The Harary--Hill conjecture states that the crossing number $\ucr{K_n}$ of the complete graph $K_n$ is $Z(n):=\frac{1}{4}\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\rfloor\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\rfloor\lfloor\frac{n-2}{2}\rfloor\lfloor\frac{n-3}{2}\rfloor$ for all $n\ge 3$. In October 2026 OpenAI uploaded to GitHub a proof of this conjecture. The proof is very short, but it relies on polynomial methods that are not part of the standard techniques used by many combinatorialists, and it is written with very little motivation or explanation. Since we found the proof very hard to follow, we decided to write this paper, which contains a complete proof of the conjecture written for mathematicians who are more familiar with combinatorics than with polynomial methods. In fact we prove a more general result on rotation systems of $K_n$, from which the Harary--Hill conjecture easily follows. Namely, we show that for every rotation system $Π$ of $K_n$ the number of $4$-vertex subsystems of $Π$ realizable as drawings of $K_4$ with one crossing, plus three times the number of non-realizable $4$-vertex subsystems of $Π$, is at least $Z(n)$. The statement and proof of our result are purely combinatorial and do not involve drawings at all.
papers.comments: In this revised version we update parts of the background section, update and add some references, and correct some typos

papers.title: Uniform Sampling of Linear Codes with Prescribed Hull Dimension
papers.abstract: We give exactly uniform samplers for linear codes with prescribed hull dimension, for the Euclidean, Hermitian, and symplectic inner products and over finite fields of every characteristic. Except for the Euclidean form over fields of odd characteristic, these are the first uniform samplers for arbitrary prescribed hull dimension. Each sample costs an expected $O(k^2 N + k \log q)$ field operations for codes of dimension $k$ in a space of dimension $N$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ or $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$.
papers.comments: 38 pages. v2: adds Appendix A with self-contained proofs of the results on the pseudo-symplectic group and its orbits; cites the implementation (Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.24517642)

papers.title: On bordism classes of symmetric products of surfaces
papers.abstract: We explicitly determine the complex bordism class of the $n$-th symmetric product of a complex curve of genus $g$. In particular, we provide an explicit formula expressing this class as an integral linear combination of bordism classes of products of complex projective spaces. Similarly, we determine the unoriented bordism class of the $n$-th symmetric product of a non-orientable surface of genus $g$ (i.e., $\#_{i=1}^{g+1}\mathbb R P^2$). It turns out that these classes are also expressed as a $\mathbb Z_2$-linear combination of bordism classes of products of even-dimensional real projective spaces. We also give an affirmative answer to a non-orientable version of the Blagojević--Grujić--Živaljević conjecture stating that the topological type of any symmetric product of a noncompact surface of finite type determines the topological type of the surface itself.

papers.title: The enigma of locally Toeplitz matrices. I. Discrete Schrödinger operators with complex potential
papers.abstract: Freezing the coefficients of a banded locally Toeplitz matrix gives a family of Toeplitz eigenvalue measures. Their average can fill a region of the complex plane even when the eigenvalues of the original matrices appear to follow curves. We conjecture that, when the above average has a sufficiently regular planar density, the limiting eigenvalue measure is its mother body. We prove it for a class of finite Dirichlet discrete Schrödinger operators with complex potential $V$ and a common real coefficient $α>0$ on the two adjacent diagonals. When $(\Im V)'>0$ and $V$ admits a suitable holomorphic extension, the limiting measure is supported on finitely many analytic arcs. Its logarithmic potential falls below that of the averaged measure by twice the least of four explicit actions. We obtain these actions from a four-term asymptotic expansion of the Dirichlet determinant. When $\Im V$ is not monotone, an exact transfer recursion gives a conditional extension. For a circular potential arc we verify the geometric switching condition, leaving non-resonance as the remaining hypothesis.

papers.title: Polyhedral Geometry of Degree-Bounded Characteristic Imset Polytopes
papers.abstract: Characteristic imset polytopes are convex hulls of a collection of characteristic imset vectors, which are 0/1 vectors that encode the Markov equivalence class of a directed acyclic graph. These polytopes are the feasible region of linear programs which correspond to causal discovery problems. We introduce a new family of these polytopes whose vertices correspond to directed acyclic graphs with in-degree bounded by $k$. This yields a polytope whose dimension is only polynomial in the number of nodes of the underlying graphs instead of exponential. We show that when $k = 1$, this polytope is a matroid independence polytope. For $k = 2$ we provide several large families of facet-defining inequalities, which give a complete $\mathcal{H}$-representation of the polytope on four nodes.

papers.title: Smooth local isometric embeddings in dimension four
papers.abstract: Every smooth four-dimensional Riemannian metric admits a local isometric embedding into $\mathbb{R}^{10}$, the optimal universal dimension. A fixed-domain Nash-Moser argument prescribes any Gauss-compatible rank-six second fundamental form with regular characteristic data. For $n\ge4$, product-weighted cube evaluations give polynomial Gram lifts of algebraic curvature tensors that are uniformly positive on a fixed $n(n-1)/2$-dimensional support. In dimension four the support can have a nonsingular complex characteristic quartic. With linear tangential control, the transverse square-root estimate near affine embeddings is sharp in $H^\ell$ for $\ell\ge1$.
papers.comments: 9 pages, including three appendices. Revised proof with exact second-jet prescription for smooth metrics, fixed-support Gram lifts, and a self-contained finite-field proof of characteristic regularity

papers.title: Controlled Riemannian rigidity
papers.abstract: Given a compact Lie group acting smoothly and freely on a compact connected manifold, we prove that the space of invariant Riemannian metrics whose symmetry group is precisely the group in question is open dense in that of all invariant metrics provided the orbit space is at least 2-dimensional. This strengthens the author's prior results to their optimal dimension bound and recovers Ebin's non-equivariant analogue to the effect that trivial-symmetry Riemannian metrics constitute an open dense set. In the process, the discussion also addresses a number of apparent gaps in said sources, pertaining to the rigidity results in question.
papers.comments: v2 adds Theorems 1.11 and 1.12, improves the dimensional bound in Theorem 0.1 to its optimal minimal value, and makes a number of other minor changes; 11 pages + references

papers.title: On the connected zero forcing polynomial of finite trees
papers.abstract: Given a graph $Γ$ with vertex set $V(Γ)$ and a set of colored vertices S, the zero forcing rule is an iterative graph coloring process which states that a colored vertex with exactly one uncolored neighbor forces that neighbor to become colored. If repeated application of this rule eventually colors every vertex of $Γ$, the set $S$ is called a \emph{zero forcing set}. Now, if the induced subgraph $Γ\vert_S$ is connected, then $S$ is called a \textit{connected zero forcing set}. The minimum cardinality of such a set is the \emph{connected zero forcing number} $Z_C(Γ)$. A \emph{connected zero forcing polynomial} of a finite graph $Γ$ is a monic polynomial $Z_C^Γ(x) \;=\; \sum_{k} a_k x^k$, where $a_k$ counts the number of connected zero forcing sets of $Γ$ of size $k$, which we denote by $Z_C(Γ,k)$. In this paper, we find the connected zero forcing polynomial of any finite tree $T$, and show that they are log-concave. We then establish sharp lower bounds for each coefficient of the connected zero forcing polynomial, over all trees on $n$ vertices with $p$ many pendant vertices. We also identify a family of trees, which we call uniform trees, and we prove that for any tree on $n$ vertices and $p$ many pendant vertices, there exists a uniform tree on $n$ vertices and $p$ many pendant vertices, whose connected zero forcing polynomial bounds as an upper bound, the connected zero forcing polynomial of the tree coefficient wise. Again for $2\leq p\leq 4$, we establish a sharp upper bound for each coefficient of the connected zero forcing polynomial, over all trees on $n$ vertices with $p$ many pendant vertices.

papers.title: Concave shifts and the complete Nevanlinna--Pick property
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a non-zero reproducing kernel Hilbert space of holomorphic functions on the unit disc, and assume $\mathcal{H}$ is invariant under the forward and backward shifts. We show that if the forward shift on $\mathcal{H}$ is concave, then $\mathcal{H}$ is a complete Nevanlinna--Pick (CNP) space. This answers a question by Shimorin, and greatly extends his result that any space of Dirichlet type is CNP. As a byproduct of our investigation, we also show that if the forward shift on $\mathcal{H}$ is concave, then any multiplier of $\mathcal{H}$ is the SOT limit of its Cesàro means. As applications, we prove a commutant lifting theorem for concave cyclic analytic operators, and several results about shift-invariant subspaces in de~Branges--Rovnyak spaces.

papers.title: Brown Measures and Spectral Convergence for Arbitrary GUE Polynomials
papers.abstract: We prove that, for every noncommutative polynomial in independent GUE matrices, the empirical eigenvalue distribution converges almost surely to the Brown measure of the same polynomial in free semicircular variables. This is the Gaussian case of a conjecture of Belinschi, Śniady and Speicher. We also prove that the spectrum converges almost surely in Hausdorff distance to the spectrum of the limiting operator, so that the spectral radius converges as well; deviations have probability smaller than every inverse power of the matrix size. For this we show that the support of the Brown measure of every polynomial in free semicircular variables is its whole spectrum, a statement about operators that involves no random matrices. We also give an algorithm, with a convergence guarantee, that computes the limiting Brown measure from matrices whose size depends only on the polynomial. A holomorphic rotation introduces an independent Ginibre component and yields the almost-sure limit without a least-singular-value bound for the original GUE polynomial. We also give a second-moment criterion for weak convergence of Brown measures. On free probability side, we use the Dyson equation of a linear pencil to show that harmonicity of its logarithmic potential forces invertibility.

papers.title: Stabilization of zero forcing numbers of finite quotients of periodic graphs
papers.abstract: We give a method for determining the zero forcing number of a graph by passing to an infinite cover. When the quotient map is a covering map, forcing commutes with taking preimages. If, in addition, the closure of every small set in the cover touches none of its translates, then no small set is a zero forcing set of the quotient. For covers that are periodic, this condition reduces to a property of the cover alone, and it gives an explicit threshold beyond which the zero forcing number of the quotient equals that of the cover. We apply the method to the generalized Petersen graphs: $Z(P(n,k))=2k+2$ for all $k\ge 1$ and $n\ge 2k^2+k+1$. We also show that the circulant $C_n(1,a)$ has zero forcing number $2a$ for all $n\ge 2a^2-a+1$.

papers.title: Virtual Two-Step Nilpotency of the Fundamental Groups of Special Quasi-Projective Varieties
papers.abstract: We prove that the fundamental group of every smooth connected complex quasi-projective variety that is special in the sense of Campana is virtually nilpotent of class at most two. This establishes the two-step nilpotency conjecture of Cao--Deng--Hacon--Păun, a quasi-projective analogue of Campana's almost abelian conjecture for special compact Kähler manifolds. Examples of Cadorel--Deng--Yamanoi show that the step bound is sharp. On a suitable finite etale cover, we construct a canonical second Albanese map to a torus torsor over an abelian variety. The proof reduces to showing that the kernel of the induced map on fundamental groups is finite. Using good minimal models and meridian groups of projective pairs, we show that an infinite kernel would yield a saturated rank-one subsheaf of logarithmic differentials whose Iitaka dimension contradicts specialness.

papers.title: $G_2'$-Slodowy Slices II: Anosov Representations
papers.abstract: We find many exotic connected components of Anosov representations of surface groups in the split real group $G_2'$ that are neither $ι$-Fuchsian deformations nor higher rank Teichmüller spaces. These representations are found through the non-abelian Hodge correspondence via $G_2'$-Higgs bundles that we call $α$-bundles and $β$-bundles, which are particular cyclic Higgs bundles in the Slodowy slices of the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-triples associated to the simple roots $α$ and $β$ of $\mathfrak{g}_2^{\mathbb{C}}$. We first prove that (most) $β$-bundles that are also Hodge bundles are $P_β$-Anosov and $α$-bundles are $P_α$-Anosov. The strategy employed is new, geometric, and general. For $σ\in \{α, β\}$, we then show the locally homogeneous $(G_2', G_2'/P_σ)$-manifold $\mathscr{M}_σ(ρ)$ recently described in arXiv:2510.12757, for the representation $ρ:π_1S\rightarrow \mathsf{G}_2'$ associated to a $σ$-bundle, coincides up to finite cover with the corresponding geometric structure for $ρ$ defined via domains of discontinuity by Guichard-Wienhard and Kapovich-Leeb-Porti. Consequently, we find that $π_1({\mathscr{M}}_σ(ρ))$ is an invariant for the connected component of $ρ$ in the space of $P_σ$-Anosov representations. After verifying the folklore result that the $G_2'$-character variety has exactly three connected components, we conclude lower bounds for the number of connected components of $P_σ$-Anosov representations in the two non-Hitchin components, most of which are exotic. These are the first higher rank examples of connected components of a character variety containing multiple (in fact, arbitrarily many) exotic components of Anosov representations.
papers.comments: 55 pages, 8 figures, 1 table. No AI proof assistance. Expositional improvements to the introduction from v1

papers.title: A nonfinitely based additively idempotent semiring with finitely based matrix semirings
papers.abstract: We establish that the matrix semiring $\mathbf{M}_n(SR_6)$ over the six-element nonfinitely based additively idempotent semiring $SR_6$ is finitely based for every $n \geq 2$. This provides the first known example of an additively idempotent semiring $S$ that is nonfinitely based, while the matrix semirings $\mathbf{M}_n(S)$ are finitely based. Moreover, we show that the interval $[\mathsf{V}(SR_6), \mathsf{V}(\mathbf{M}_2(SR_6))]$ in the lattice of additively idempotent semiring varieties has the cardinality of the continuum.

papers.title: $L^p$ Integrability and Spectral Complexity of Manifolds with Higher Codimension
papers.abstract: We investigate the relationship between the $L^p$ integrability of functions and the curvature geometry of their Fourier support. We prove that if $M\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is a $C^n$ manifold of dimension $d$ and $n>2d$, then every $u\in L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ with $\operatorname{supp}\widehat u\subseteq M$ vanishes whenever \[ 2\le p\le\frac{6n-4}{3d-1}. \] This strictly improves the classical threshold $2n/d$ throughout the range $n>2d$. More generally, we obtain a family of dimension-dependent improvements in higher codimension. As a consequence, we obtain a strict quantitative improvement in the necessary conditions for Fourier restriction when $n>2d$, resolving a conjecture of Mockenhaupt \cite{Mockenhaupt96}. This further establishes the nonexistence of quadratic manifolds satisfying the Christ--Mockenhaupt condition when $n>2d$, answering the question of \cite{CLMP}. For quadratic manifolds, we obtain spectral synthesis bounds from joint sublevel estimates for the eigenvalues of the normal Hessian pencil. In codimension two, we determine the exact critical exponent from the ranks and eigenvalue vanishing orders, including nonexistence at the critical endpoint. We also obtain integrability bounds for manifolds with constant relative nullity, extending Guo's hypersurface results \cite{Guo93} to higher codimension. Finally, we use the Fourier ratio as a measure of the geometric complexity of individual strata of the characteristic set to establish $L^p$ uniqueness criteria for homogeneous constant-coefficient PDEs.
papers.comments: Rectified typos and made minor revisions to a few arguments for better exposition. Main results unchanged

papers.title: Matrix ultraproducts have trivial fundamental group
papers.abstract: We prove that every tracial ultraproduct $\prod_{\mathcal{U}} M_n(\mathbb{C})$ of matrix algebras has trivial fundamental group. In particular, this establishes that there are uncountably many nonisomorphic matrix ultraproducts, answering a question of Sorin Popa. We actually prove the stronger result that every matrix ultraproduct has trivial first-order fundamental group and thus our techniques are model-theoretic in nature.
papers.comments: 50 pages; version 2; errors corrected and more consequences of the main results spelled out; comments welcome!

papers.title: Self-adjoint boundary conditions for equation-free multiscale modelling
papers.abstract: Equation-free modelling is a computation multiscale modelling scheme for the simulation of complex dynamical systems. Efficient computations are achieved by solving the given microscale model in small, well-separated `patches' spread across the space-time domain, with each patch providing a data point for the macroscale simulation. Patch coupling bridges the unsimulated space between patches and supports the macroscale dynamics. Accurate simulations require coupling conditions that preserve underlying symmetries of the microscale equation. Failing to preserve such symmetries may result in an unphysical macroscale simulation that does not satisfy required conservation laws. Here we develop equation-free modelling that preserves self-adjoint symmetry for microscale models defined by a compact self-adjoint operator on a bounded domain with fixed boundary conditions. This new design for equation-free modelling greatly increases the range of systems for which equation-free modelling is applicable.

papers.title: On two-dimensional affine Springer fibres
papers.abstract: We extend results of Spaltenstein on irreducible components of two-dimensional usual Springer fibres in reductive groups of simply lace type to the case of two-dimensional affine Springer fibres associated to loop groups. One of our methods is to relate these affine Springer fibres with certain subsets of the affine Weyl group.

papers.title: Gaussian mass inequalities for lattices
papers.abstract: The Gaussian mass of a lattice is the evaluation of its theta series at a real nome and is relevant to lattice coding for the wiretap Gaussian channel. The ratio of the Gaussian mass of stable lattices to the Gaussian mass of the integer lattice was conjectured to be $\le 1$ (Regev et al., 2024). Kominers proved this bound recently for lattices obtained by Construction~A from binary self-dual codes. Building on Kominers' bound, we establish corresponding inequalities on average for Construction~$A_4$ lattices obtained from free self-dual quaternary codes and for Construction~$A_6$ lattices obtained from self-dual senary codes. We also prove the strict Gaussian-mass inequality for extremal unimodular lattices of both Type~II and Type~I. The Type~I result uses the Rains--Sloane definition of extremality. Its proof combines a universal theta truncation with an exact inversion of the shadow coefficients, and a Gaussian inequality for translated lattices. In addition, we obtain an averaging bound over the genus of Type~II lattices, and extend the binary Construction~A inequality to Siegel theta series of arbitrary genus, with further quaternary results under conditions on the residue code.

papers.title: Douglas--Rachford Algorithm with Relaxed Resolvents
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the convergence of a generalization of the Douglas--Rachford algorithm for finding a zero of the sum of two maximally monotone operators, where reflected resolvents are extended to relaxed resolvents. This extension allows for different step sizes in the resolvents under cocoercivity. We show that the resulting method converges weakly when its parameters lie in a range determined by the cocoercivity constants, which reduces to the classical algorithm when these constants vanish. Our main results concern the cocoercive case when one of the operators is in addition strongly monotone, in which the composition is a strict contraction. For both monotone inclusions and convex minimization, we compute the contraction factor and its optimal parameters in closed form, and show that the resulting rates are tight. Whenever the second operator is cocoercive, the optimal rates are strictly smaller than the corresponding rates of forward-backward splitting and of the classical Peaceman--Rachford and Douglas--Rachford algorithms and, in convex minimization, than those of FISTA. All theoretical rates are corroborated by the numerical worst cases obtained via performance estimation.

papers.title: Golomb rulers with real marks: the real and integer optima agree up to ten marks
papers.abstract: A Golomb ruler is a set of integer marks whose pairwise differences are distinct. We let the marks be real numbers and ask that every difference be at least 1 and that any two differences be at least 1 apart. Every integer Golomb ruler satisfies these conditions, so the least length $G_R(n)$ of such a real ruler with $n$ marks is at most the optimal Golomb length $G_Z(n)$. Fixing the order of all differences splits the real problem into finitely many polyhedral chambers. A branch-and-bound over these chambers, with an exact rational certificate at every leaf, proves $G_R(n) = G_Z(n)$ for $n \le 10$. Each proof takes under a minute and is verified by an independent checker that uses only exact arithmetic. An exhaustive exact enumeration of all chamber vertices confirms the result for $n \le 7$, and shows that there the shortest real rulers are exactly the optimal integer rulers and their mirror images. For every $n$ we have $n(\sqrt{n}-1)^2 \le G_R(n) \le G_Z(n)$, essentially a bound of Erdős and of Cilleruelo and Ruzsa, so that $G_R(n) \sim G_Z(n) \sim n^2$. Non-integral chamber vertices first appear at $n = 7$: there are 84, all half-integral. Already there, 80 of them are shortest points of their chambers, 40 of them the only one, although the global optimum is integral; a twelve-mark example of the same kind comes from Singer's construction. On the other hand, every Singer ruler with at most 104 marks, cut at the largest gap, is the only shortest point of its own chamber; we conjectured this for all prime powers, and Ma and Zhang have since proved it.
papers.comments: 11 pages, 5 tables. v2: credits Erdos (1997; Erdos Problem 670) and Cilleruelo and Ruzsa (2004) for earlier work on the extremal problem, including essentially the lower bound of Theorem 3; note added on answers to the open questions; other results unchanged. Programs, proof files and exact checkers: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23843508

papers.title: Preserving Ramsey ultrafilters with tree forcings
papers.abstract: We define a wide class of tree forcings that we call $\textit{normed-tree forcings}$ and prove that they can preserve Ramsey ultrafilters. These include $\textit{fat-tree forcings}$ as particular cases. As an application, we prove the consistency with $\mathsf{ZFC}$ of $\mathfrak{d}=\mathfrak{u}=\aleph_1 < \mathsf{minLc}=\mathfrak{c}=\aleph_2$, where $\mathfrak{d}$ denotes the dominating number, $\mathfrak{u}$ the ultrafilter number, and $\mathsf{minLc}$ the minimum localization cardinal. This solves some open questions about pairs of classical cardinal characteristics, such as the consistency of both $\mathfrak{e}_{\mathsf{ubd}}$ and its dual strictly larger than $\mathfrak{u}$.
papers.comments: v2: Added Remark 3.23 about limsup tree forcings and expanded acknowledgements

papers.title: Local energy decay for small radial solutions of the two-dimensional Hamiltonian $abcd$ Boussinesq system
papers.abstract: We consider the $abcd$ Boussinesq system in two space dimensions, a four-parameter family of models for the two-way propagation of small-amplitude long surface waves, in the generic regime $a,c<0$, $b,d>0$. We first revisit the local well-posedness theory in Sobolev spaces in dimensions $2\le n\le4$ and show that for the Hamiltonian case $b=d$ the Cauchy problem is globally well-posed for small data in the energy space $\mathbb{H}^1(\mathbb R^n)$. Then we consider the asymptotic behavior of these global solutions in the $n=2$ case. Under the condition $-a,-c>b/9$, we prove that every small solution with radial symmetry exhibits local energy decay. As a consequence, there are no small radial time-periodic (in particular, stationary) solutions. Decay also holds, along sequences of times, on balls whose radius grows almost linearly in time. The proof is based on new virial identities adapted to the radial structure of the system. In the proof we introduce two correction functionals such that the resulting quadratic form is coercive precisely when $-a,-c>b/9$, a threshold which is sharp for the functional. To our knowledge this is the first result describing the long-time dynamics of $abcd$ systems in dimension two.
papers.comments: 71 pages, some references, and an AI declaration statement added. All comments are welcome

papers.title: Generic vanishing and singularities of theta divisors
papers.abstract: We study the connection between the generic vanishing conjecture for subvarieties of principally polarized abelian varieties and various predictions about the singularities of theta divisors. We deduce new cases of a conjecture on the multiplicities of points on irreducible theta divisors, as well as Beauville's conjecture characterizing Jacobians by the size of their theta singularity loci.
papers.comments: 15 pages; a few improvements, including the statement of Thm.D and the results in \S10; comments still welcome

papers.title: Rademacher and Enflo types in Banach spaces: sharp comparison and orthogonality
papers.abstract: Let \(1<p\le2\). We prove that the ratio of the Enflo to the Rademacher type \(p\) constant has supremum \(p\), already over finite-dimensional real or complex Banach spaces. This settles the sharpness question of Areshidze~\cite{aresh}, who improved the bound \(π/\sqrt{2}\) of Ivanisvili et al.~\cite{ivv} to \(p\). We also study orthogonal families in a real Banach space \(X\). \begin{list}{}{\setlength{\leftmargin}{\dimexpr24pt+1.8em\relax}\setlength{\rightmargin}{24pt}\setlength{\labelwidth}{1.4em}\setlength{\labelsep}{0.4em}\setlength{\topsep}{2pt}\setlength{\itemsep}{0pt}} \item[(a)] If \(p<2\), \(X\) has Enflo type \(p\) if and only if the Rademacher type \(p\) inequality holds uniformly over ordered families \((v_i)\) satisfying \[ v_i\perp_B v_j \qquad \text{for all } i<j, \] where \(\perp_B\) denotes Birkhoff--James orthogonality (that is, \(\|v_i+t v_j\|\ge\|v_i\|\) for every \(t\in\mathbb R\)). \item[(b)] Uniform validity of the Rademacher type \(p\) inequality on pairwise isosceles orthogonal families implies that \(X\) has Enflo type \(s\) for every \(1\le s<p\), with a quadratic bound in the restricted type constant at \(s=2p/(p+1)\). \end{list} We also record the subcritical type implication for Pythagorean orthogonality and the sharp factor \(p\) for Roberts orthogonality. {For the exponents in (a), as the modulus of roundness \(ν_X(p)\) approaches \(2\), the ratio of the Enflo to the Rademacher type \(p\) constant tends uniformly to \(1\) over real Banach spaces of Rademacher type \(p\). The same limit holds for the ratio of the two constants restricted by mutual Birkhoff--James orthogonality.}

papers.title: Relative Entropy under Ordered Chi-Squared Constraints: Sharp Bounds and Extremizers
papers.abstract: We derive a sharp upper bound on the relative entropy $D(P\|Q)$ in terms of the two ordered chi-squared divergences $χ^2(P\|Q)$ and $χ^2(Q\|P)$. For any $A,B>0$, the constraints $χ^2(P\|Q)\leq A$ and $χ^2(Q\|P)\leq B$ yield upper bounds on $D(P\|Q)$ and $D(Q\|P)$. Two pairs of Bernoulli distributions each attain both bounds simultaneously. As a consequence, for sequences of probability mass functions $\{P_n\}$ and $\{Q_n\}$ on a common finite or countably infinite alphabet, both $D(P_n\|Q_n)$ and $D(Q_n\|P_n)$ tend to zero whenever one of the two ordered chi-squared divergences tends to zero and the other remains uniformly bounded. Without this boundedness assumption, $D(P_n\|Q_n)$ can fail to converge to zero even when $χ^2(Q_n\|P_n)\to 0$. Finally, in contrast to the attainable upper bounds, on any finite or countably infinite alphabet containing at least three elements, the infimum of $D(P\|Q)$ under the exact constraints $χ^2(P\|Q)=A$ and $χ^2(Q\|P)=B$ is zero and is not attained. As an application to lossless source coding, we consider the product measures $P^n$ and $Q^n$ induced by $P$ and $Q$, respectively, on blocks of length $n$. We bound the expected saving in ideal codelength under $P^n$ when the encoder replaces $Q^n$ with the mixture $λP^n+(1-λ)Q^n$. The lower bound depends on the sources only through $D(P\|Q)$, and the upper bound depends on them only through the two ordered chi-squared divergences between $P$ and $Q$. For every fixed $n$, the upper bound agrees with the expected saving to first order as $λ\to 0^+$.
papers.comments: Section 4 is new, together with revisions

papers.title: List packing for graphs with small arboricity
papers.abstract: We prove that every graph $G$ whose edge set is the union of $r$ forests has list packing number at most $2^r$. This means that for all $k\ge 2^r$ and every list-assignment $L$ with lists of size $k$, the graph $G$ admits $k$ disjoint proper $L$-colourings. While for large $r$ this bound is far from optimal, for $r\in\{1,2\}$ it is sharp. As a direct corollary of the case $r=2$, we obtain that every triangle-free planar graph has list packing number at most $4$, thus improving upon a result of Dvořák, Masařík, Musílek and Pangrác and providing the optimal answer to a question of Dvořák, Postle and Norin on (weighted) $ε$-flexibility of such graphs. As a corollary of the case $r=3$, we obtain a short alternative proof that every $K_5$-minor-free (and hence every planar) graph has list-packing number at most $8$, matching the state of the art. All results above also hold for the stronger notion of correspondence packing.
papers.comments: 10 pages (of which 2 for the main proofs). v2: fixed typos

papers.title: A Generalized Lefschetz Degree with applications to Fixed Point Theory
papers.abstract: We introduce and study a class of spaces, named Lefschetz admissible, where the identity maps on compacts can be approximated by certain maps with values in Lefschetz spaces in a suitable sense. For maps defined on these spaces, we introduce a generalized Lefschetz degree obtained as the set of accumulation points of usual Lefschetz degrees for the approximant maps in a certain compactification. We show that when the degree is nonempty, fixed point results hold. We consider both the situation of spaces embedded in topological vector spaces (TVSs) as global and as neighborhood retracts. As two consequences, we obtain a generalization of a fixed point result due to Browder, and a no-retraction criterion for compact subsets of locally convex TVSs.
papers.comments: 20 pages. Comments are very welcome. v2: Various typos have been fixed, some things have been reworded for clarity, and a direct consequence of a result has been added to the applications

papers.title: Persistent Bass and Lyubeznik Numbers of Stanley Reisner Rings
papers.abstract: We define persistent Lyubeznik numbers and persistent Bass numbers of Stanley--Reisner rings along a simplicial filtration. For Lyubeznik numbers we show that the complex of Àlvarez Montaner and Vahidi computing $λ_{p,q}(\kk[Δ])$ is natural for inclusions of simplicial complexes, so that persistent Lyubeznik numbers are ranks of maps on its cohomology. We give an equivalent costar complex, whose terms are reduced homology groups of links of faces and whose differentials are induced by quotient maps; it requires neither Alexander duals nor free resolutions. For Bass numbers at coordinate primes we prove that the Hochster-type formula is natural for inclusions, which identifies the persistent Bass numbers with the persistent graded Betti numbers of Suwayyid and Wei for filtered links. Both families have finite barcodes and satisfy bottleneck stability. Examples, including two isomers with the same persistent homology, exhibit Lyubeznik bars that persistent homology does not detect.

papers.title: Global Critical $L^3$ Well-Posedness for the Stochastic Tamed Navier--Stokes Equations on $\mathbb R^3$ with Wiener and Jump Noise
papers.abstract: We study the global well-posedness for the three dimensional stochastic tamed Navier--Stokes equations on $\mathbb R^3$ with multiplicative Wiener and compensated Poisson noise. When noise coefficients are globally Lipschitz on $L^3_σ(\mathbb R^3)$ and satisfy spatial $H^1_σ(\mathbb R^3)$ regularity assumptions, the system admits a pathwise unique global, probabilistically strong, critical mild solution for any initial datum $u_0 \in L^0(Ω, \mathcal F_0; L^3_σ(\mathbb R^3)) $. Neither smallness nor moment or finite kinetic energy assumptions on $u_0$ are required. We also establish that the global solution depends continuously in probability on the initial datum in uniform-in-time $L^3$ and space-time $L^5$ norms on every finite time interval.
papers.comments: 72 Pages, The minor compilation error due to \cref has been fixed. No changes in proofs and results

papers.title: Incidence Correspondences and Chow Motives in the Symplectic (Z/2Z)4-K3 Locus
papers.abstract: We establish a Chow-motivic framework for projective K3 surfaces with a symplectic (Z/2Z)^4-action. For the universal Heisenberg-invariant quartic family, we show that the generically defined codimension-two cycles on the relative square are generated by three ambient classes and sixteen automorphism graphs, and that these nineteen classes are cohomologically independent. Combining this square-Franchetta property with a finite-cover trace construction and the Kuga-Satake correspondence, we prove that every smooth Heisenberg-invariant quartic K3 surface has a Chow motive of abelian type. We also consider the diagonal complete-intersection family of three quadrics and establish stability of the Heisenberg result under rational Hodge isogenies. For arbitrary projective K3 surfaces with a faithful symplectic (Z/2Z)^4-action, we obtain a motivic reduction to the minimal resolution of the fifteen-node quotient. Applying a rational Kuga-Satake criterion, we establish abelianity of Chow motives for explicit infinite arithmetic subfamilies of all three Garbagnati-Sarti lattice types, including their Picard-rank specializations. Finally, we prove a square-Franchetta theorem for the ten-dimensional family of double-cubic K3 surfaces.
papers.comments: Needs substantial edit before being readable

papers.title: The Tate Conjecture in Positive Characteristic
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{Z}(n)$ be Bloch's cycle complex and $\mathbb{Z}(n)^c$ be the complex that compute continuous étale cohomology. Kahn observed that the Tate conjecture for a finite field is equivalent to the map $\mathcal{Z}(n)\otimes\mathbb{Z}(0)^c\to\mathbb{Z}(n)^c$ being isomorphism. Later, Kahn found that the Tate conjecture for a finite field is equivalent to $Ω_\ell(\mathbb{Z}_\ell)\in DM^{\text{eff}}_{\text{ét}}(k)$, where $Ω_\ell$ is the right adjoint of the $\ell$-adic realisation functor. In this note, using the Dwyer-Greenlees equivalence between $\ell$-completed objects and $\ell$-torsion objects, we prove that $Ω_\ell(\mathbb{Z}_\ell)\in DM^{\text{eff}}_{\text{ét}}(k)$, and consequently, based on Kahn's early work, the Tate conjecture at positive characteristics.

papers.title: A unipotent witness: vanishing orders of word maps on SU(2) and lengths in the lower central series
papers.abstract: Let $n\ge2$, $k\ge2$ and $1\ne w\inγ_k(F_n)$, the $k$-th term of the lower central series of the free group of rank $n$. We prove that a cyclically reduced conjugate of $w$ has at least $2k$ cyclic syllables, so $w$ has word length at least $2k$; the previous linear bound, due to Malestein and Putman, is $k$. For $1\ne w\in[F_n,F_n]$ we also prove that the word map of $w$ on $SU(2)$ or $SO(3)$ vanishes at the identity to order at most $T/2$, where $T$ is the number of cyclic syllables of a cyclically reduced conjugate of $w$, with equality for $[x_1,x_2]$ and for words with six and eight syllables. Both proofs evaluate $w$ at unipotent matrices $I+tN_i$, with $N_i$ nilpotent of rank one, and compare the degree of the trace of the resulting matrix $M(t)\in SL_2(\mathbb{Z}[t])$ with the order of vanishing of $M(t)-I$ at $t=0$.
papers.comments: 7 pages, v2: example for k=4, references added, minor corrections

papers.title: Superintegrable Systems and the Tractor Connection
papers.abstract: Quadratic constants of motion for natural pseudo-Riemannian Hamiltonians with potential correspond to conformal Killing tensors admitting multiple Killing scales. Taking this correspondence further, we develop a dimension-independent ($n\ge 3$) framework for studying second-order superintegrable systems using conformal tractor calculus, and invariant BGG prolongation of the rank two conformal Killing equation. We apply this framework to classify second-order maximally superintegrable systems within certain natural families of Hamiltonians generated by pairs of conformally related Einstein metrics in arbitrary dimensions. We recover the second-order analogue of Bertrand's theorem as a special case.

papers.title: Invariant subspaces and nest algebras in left-right operator splitting
papers.abstract: The left--right (L-R) splitting method for boundary integral equations in rough-surface scattering writes the integral operator as the sum of its lower- and strictly upper- triangular parts. This note examines the operator algebra formed by the lower-triangular ($L$-type) parts.Their weak closure is a nest algebra; second-kind $L$-type operators with Hilbert--Schmidt kernels have $L$-type inverses; and Arveson's distance formula expresses the error of the best possible forward-only approximation in terms of the backward coupling across a single cut. Bounds and numerical results for the 2D double-layer kernel suggest that truncation is close to optimal, and that the worst-case input field is a predominantly left-going grazing wave rather than backscatter of a right-going incident field. For a hard surface the inverse $L$-operator is given, up to a second-order correction, by four times the $L$-operator of the mirror-image surface, and several open questions are posed.
papers.comments: 17 pages, Minor revisions for clarity, streamlined open questions, and an additional reference

papers.title: Automorphism groups of Severi--Brauer varieties of odd prime degree over $\mathbb{Q}$
papers.abstract: We prove that the only non-trivial finite subgroup of automorphism group of non-trivial Severi--Brauer variety of odd prime degree $p$ over the field of rational numbers is $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}.$

papers.title: Killing Scales for Conformal Killing Tensors of Rank Two and Higher
papers.abstract: We study which metrics in a conformal class admit a Killing tensor with prescribed conformal Killing trace-free part. We call such metrics Killing scales. We also consider whether a given conformal Killing tensor is itself a Killing tensor for some metric in the conformal class, as well as the analogous problem for conformal Killing-Yano forms. Our approach to this problem uses conformal and projective tractors, and the prolongations provided by the BGG splitting operators of the projective and conformal Killing operators. For rank two conformal Killing tensors, we characterise local Killing scales for arbitrary scales on arbitrary conformal manifolds, extending recent results that were restricted to Einstein scales on conformally flat manifolds. The criterion is expressed in terms of the scale tractor and the BGG prolongation of the conformal Killing tensor. We also obtain Killing scale criteria for higher-rank conformal Killing tensors and conformal Killing-Yano forms, under additional hypotheses involving Einstein scales and normal solutions. We describe the tractor geometry of special Einstein products, including Ricci-flat products, and use these constructions to give examples beyond the conformally flat setting.

papers.title: A note on approximate projection onto the semidefinite complementarity set
papers.abstract: The proximal slack update in an augmented Lagrangian method for semidefinite complementarity constraints requires a joint matrix projection. Given real symmetric matrices $A$ and $B$, we seek the nearest pair $(X,Z)$ with $X$ positive semidefinite, $Z$ negative semidefinite, and $XZ=0$. Hou, Peng and Ding obtain a squared-loss factor of $2$ by fitting the pair in an eigenbasis of $A+B$. To improve this bound, we replace the orthogonal projector onto the subspace allowed for $X$ by a symmetric matrix $T$ with eigenvalues in $[0,1]$. From an optimal solution of the resulting semidefinite program, we form candidate subspaces by starting at the zero subspace and adding the eigenspaces of $T$ in decreasing order of eigenvalue. For each candidate, we compress $A$ to that subspace and $B$ to its orthogonal complement. We keep the positive eigenvalues of the first compression and the negative eigenvalues of the second. The best pair has squared loss at most $1.189$ times the minimum for arbitrary inputs and at most $1.15487$ times the minimum when $A$ is positive semidefinite and $B$ is negative semidefinite. For arbitrary inputs the factor improves to $1.18$ if $T$ has at most two distinct eigenvalues in $(0,1)$. The threshold-rounding proofs average over a uniform spectral threshold and use computer-assisted bounds for the resulting scalar inequalities.

papers.title: Numerical simulations of CCP-2D GEC with sGMRES
papers.abstract: Fluid models provide an efficient means of simulating the low-temperature gas discharges, which are important in semiconductor manufacturing.
