This work presents, to the best of our knowledge, the first systematic numerical framework for the Gaseous Electronics Conference (GEC) reference cell of the 2D capacitively coupled plasma (CCP). The framework employs a structured, nonuniform cylindrical mesh to resolve the spatial gradients. A semi-implicit Scharfetter-Gummel (SG) scheme is used for the Poisson's equation, while the implicit SG schemes are applied to the continuity equations and the electron energy equation. Both the explicit and and the implicit formulations based on the conventional drift-diffusion terms are also investigated. To solve the resulting large-scale linear systems, we introduce an incomplete LU (ILU)-preconditioned sketched GMRES (sGMRES) method as the solver. As far as we know, this work is the first to apply the randomized sGMRES to the practical simulations in the engineering. By reducing the cost of the global orthogonalization, ILU-sGMRES achieves greater computational efficiency than ILU-GMRES while maintaining the accuracy, particularly at relatively large values of the restart. Specifically, numerical tests demonstrate that ILU-sGMRES can reduce the end-to-end wall-clock time by up to 25.38\% on a single machine and up to 11.71\% in a three-node benchmark compared with the conventional ILU-GMRES, while maintaining a maximum relative difference across plasma fields of only 0.194\%. Numerical experiments compare the performance of different numerical schemes and solvers, demonstrating the robustness of ILU-sGMRES in the real simulation.
papers.comments: This paper has been withdrawn because it was submitted without the full consent of all co-authors and contains critical methodological errors as well as unresolved academic compliance issues

papers.title: A local-in-time quadratic functional for scalar conservation laws
papers.abstract: We construct a Glimm-type functional for scalar conservation laws, which is quadratic (w.r.t. the total variation of the initial datum), it controls the change of wavefront speed across interactions, and, differently than functionals with similar properties already present in the literature, it is purely local in time, meaning that it depends only on the present profile of the (approximate) solution (and not on its past or future evolution).
papers.comments: 34 pages, 15 figures; added the arXiv identifier to reference [2]

papers.title: The cost functional for hyperbolic systems of conservation laws
papers.abstract: For hyperbolic systems of conservation laws (without any genuine nonlinearity of linear degeneracy assumption on the flux) we construct a quadratic interaction functional, which controls the change of wavefront speed across interactions and it is local in time. This extends the analysis of arXiv:2611.30663 from scalar conservation laws to $n \times n$ systems.
papers.comments: 45 pages, 14 figures; added the arXiv identifier to the reference [3] and updated the corresponding citation in the abstract

papers.title: Arithmetic Winding Curves in $\mathbb{F}_1$ Geometry
papers.abstract: We construct arithmetic winding curves from cyclic covers and the completions of a number field $K$. Transfers between cyclic periods give the primitive cyclotomic relations. Selected factors of the equivariant endomorphism rings of their derived intersections are finite fields in odd residue characteristic and length-two Witt rings in residue characteristic two. Valuation covers carry these periods on the curve $Y_K$. Their normal coordinates realize deck shifts as Schwartz operators in Meyer's arithmetic trace formula, and their puncture differentials give the finite Euler factors of $ζ_K$. We construct a sheaf on $Y_K$ for which the middle Fourier--Poisson representation embeds as a $C_K$-module in ordinary first sheaf cohomology. The Dedekind-zeta component is an equivariant direct summand. The injection uses valuation monodromy at the finite places and adelic Poisson summation on the archimedean charts. The cup product of two image classes vanishes with tensor-product coefficients, also after conjugating one factor. On the section side, tensor degree and integral jets give multiplicative lattices, explicit duality quotients, and relative theta identities. A principal cyclotomic twist with determinant one on truncated jets yields a quadratic lower bound for the logarithmic index in a family of increasing rank. The fixed-weight Poisson quotients preserve finite collections of Mellin derivatives at Hecke zeros of orders below their respective multiplicities.
papers.comments: 56 pages, v2: Corrected the closed-range argument in the proof of Proposition 10.3. Results unchanged

papers.title: The Kao-Lai-Osting Conjecture for the Second Laplace Eigenvalue on Riemannian Two-Tori
papers.abstract: We prove the $k=2$ case of the Kao-Lai-Osting conjecture for the area-normalized Laplace spectrum of Riemannian two-tori: $\sup_g λ_2(T^2,g)\,\mathrm{Area}(T^2,g) = 8π^2/\sqrt{3} + 8π$, where the supremum is taken over smooth Riemannian metrics. No smooth metric attains this value. It is approached by a sequence in the equilateral conformal class developing a round spherical bubble, and the equilateral class is the only conformal class whose conformal supremum equals the global one. The upper bound follows from spherical folding and a sharp truncated conformal-area inequality for fundamental embeddings into $S^5$. Normal-curvature and normal-chord estimates yield high-cap area control, with exact elementary estimates on nested high-centre strips. The proof is partly computer-assisted. Rational polynomial inequalities handle the low-weight cap range and the entire residual high-cap region, the latter through exact Bernstein certificates on rational boxes, which are also checked independently in ball arithmetic. The residual product inequality is established by rigorous upper quadratures, with two independent reproducible certificates, in ball and in interval arithmetic, and exact domain-coverage checks.
papers.comments: 72 pages, 1 figure. The computational supplement (verification programs, certificates, reference logs) is included as ancillary files (see also Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24473074). v2: editorial corrections (explicit constant in the main theorem, notation and terminology, a few proof steps made explicit); results, numbering and ancillary files unchanged

papers.title: On the computation of Green's function in layered elastic media
papers.abstract: We develop a recursive scheme for the computation of Green's function for time-harmonic elastic wave in three-dimensional layered media, based on a matrix basis representation in the Fourier domain and a classic interface reaction-transmission theory. With transversal rotational symmetry preserved, the scheme decouples the Green's function into SH waves and P-SV waves using five scalar functions, which are recursively solved at linear cost with respect to the number of total layers, regardless of the layers the source and target particles locate in. The resulting scheme leads to a stable numerical method ready for Hankel transform evaluation in the spatial domain, constituting a foundation for the analysis and efficient numerical simulation of elastic wave scattering in layered media.

papers.title: Needlepoints in Quasi-Normed Orlicz Spaces and a Question of Kalton and Peck
papers.abstract: We prove that the approachable points and the needlepoints coincide in every quasi-normed Orlicz function space on the probability interval. Their common set is either $\{0\}$ or $E_Φ$. The proof gives a characterization by finite probability laws and also applies to Orlicz function spaces with the modular topology, without assuming $Δ_2$. We then construct a separable real quasi-Banach space whose approachable points form a line and whose only needlepoint is zero. Every compact convex subset of this space is relatively locally convex. The construction gives a negative answer to the question of Kalton and Peck for general quasi-Banach spaces.

papers.title: The polygonal Weinstock inequality and quantitative stability
papers.abstract: For every integer $N \ge 3$, the regular $N$-gon $R_N$ uniquely maximizes the perimeter-normalized first positive Steklov eigenvalue $J(P) = |\partial P|σ_1(P)$ among all simple planar polygons $P$ with at most $N$ sides, up to similarity. More generally, if $P$ has $p$ strictly convex vertices and $q$ reflex vertices after merging consecutive collinear sides, then $J(P) \le J(R_{p+\min(q,2)})$, with equality if and only if $q = 0$ and $P$ is similar to $R_p$. Among polygons with at most $N$ sides, restricting to those that are nonconvex or have fewer than $N$ genuine sides lowers the supremum of $J$ by $12πζ(3)N^{-4} + O(N^{-5})$ as $N \to \infty$, with a positive gap for every $N \ge 4$. For convex $p$-gons, the spectral deficit $J(R_p) - J(P)$ controls the normalized squared deviations of support heights, midpoint offsets, and side lengths with weights $1$, $p^{-2}$, and $p^{-3}$, as well as $p^{-3}$ times the sum of squared exterior-angle deviations from $2π/p$; the length weight $p^{-3}$ is sharp. For triangles, the deficit is instead comparable to the square root of the relative area deficit at fixed perimeter, or equivalently to $1 - r$, where $r$ is the singular-value ratio of an affine map from an equilateral triangle. Independently of the number of reflex vertices, a boundary phase identity in arc-length balanced disk coordinates yields the sharp fourth-order bound $2π/J(P) - 1 \ge 2ζ(3)p^{-3} + 8ζ(4)p^{-4} + O(p^{-5})$. For fixed $p$, a degree-$p$ Blaschke transport links this identity to $H^{1/p}$ coercivity for the regularized square root of the conformal derivative, perimeter-concentration rigidity at equally spaced convex prevertices, and quadratic Hausdorff stability for $p \ge 4$.
papers.comments: 62 pages. Major revision: replaces the computer-assisted verification of v1 with a purely analytic proof for all N >= 3, and adds the sharp convex-vertex comparison, the N^(-4) spectral gap for nonconvex and fewer-sided polygons, sharp quantitative stability for convex polygons, and Blaschke-transported rigidity and Hausdorff stability. Ancillary files removed

papers.title: Hochschild operations and other invariants of stable equivalences of Morita type
papers.abstract: We study stable equivalences defined by bimodule tensor identities over a commutative ring $R$. For the $R$-split exact structure, these identities preserve positive Hochschild homology and positive Hochschild cohomology with its cup product, Gerstenhaber bracket and, in prime characteristic, restricted power. A triangular comparison also identifies the relative singular Hochschild cochain complexes as $B_\infty$-algebras. For reduced pairs of finite-dimensional Frobenius algebras over an algebraically closed field, with diagonalizable Nakayama automorphisms, we construct compatible Frobenius functionals and compare the Tate--Hochschild BV operators in all degrees. For flat algebras over $R$ we give a Hochschild-cohomological criterion for comparing marked associative deformations. It applies to biadjoint Morita-type pairs and, by reduction, to all stable equivalences of Morita type between finite-dimensional algebras over any field. We compare the Bezrukavnikov--Ginzburg maps in characteristic zero by using a common triangular deformation or by lifting a two-sided tilting complex. We also compare marked module deformations over local Artin rings and their augmented universal rings. Further applications concern connected outer automorphism group schemes over perfect fields, the kernels of the quotient maps on ordinary algebraic $K$-theory, and the nonconnective $K$-theory of enhanced relative singularity categories. We construct biadjoint representatives over Henselian Noetherian local rings and relative stable tensor functors for almost $ν$-stable derived equivalences. We also answer a question of Abe and Hoshino about preservation of the Gorenstein condition in a fixed codimension.

papers.title: Hadwigerś Covering Conjecture in Three Dimensions
papers.abstract: Let $K \subset \R^3$ be an arbitrary convex body, that is, a compact convex subset of $\R^3$ with nonempty interior. We prove unconditionally that $K$ can be covered by eight smaller positive homothetic copies of itself: there exist a scalar $λ\in (0, 1)$ and translation vectors $v_1, \dots, v_8 \in \R^3$ such that \[ K \subseteq \bigcup_{i=1}^{8} (λK + v_i). \] This resolves Hadwiger's covering conjecture in three dimensions. The proof works in Boltyanski's equivalent boundary illumination formulation and is completely self-contained. Parallelepipeds are covered directly by eight translates of $\frac{2}{3} K$. For any convex body $K$ that is not a parallelepiped, we place its centrally symmetric halved difference body $S = \frac{1}{2}(K - K)$ in John's position ($B^3 \subseteq S$) and show that the spherical average of its support function satisfies $8 \int_{S^2} h_S \, d\sigmatilde < 12$, with equality only for orthogonal cubes. Using outer polyhedral approximations together with Cauchy's planar perimeter formula, the full spherical measure of directions not parallel to any boundary segment of $K$, and lower semicontinuity of curve variation, we find a unit vector $w_* \in S^2$ whose shadow boundary $\Shad{K}{w_*}$ on $K$ itself is a continuous closed curve of $S$-length strictly less than $12$. Splitting $\Shad{K}{w_*}$ into six contiguous arcs of $S$-length strictly less than $2$ and applying Helly's theorem in $\R^3$ illuminates each arc with one direction, while $\pm w_*$ illuminate the remainder of $\partial K$. The proof was discovered using an experimental harness on top of Gemini~4 Carbon and formally verified in Lean~4.

papers.title: Boundedness and Kawamata-Viehweg vanishing for threefolds of Fano type in large characteristics
papers.abstract: We study threefolds over algebraically closed fields of large positive characteristic. Let $(X,B)$ be a projective log canonical pair with $X$ of Fano type, $-(K_X+B)$ nef and coefficients of $B$ in a fixed hyperstandard set. We obtain a monotonic complement of bounded index. For exceptional pairs the complement is Kawamata log terminal. We prove that all $ε$-log canonical weak log Fano threefolds are arithmetically bounded above a characteristic threshold independent of $ε$. We also prove Kawamata--Viehweg vanishing for integral $\Q$-Cartier Weil divisors on projective threefolds of Fano type above an absolute characteristic threshold.
papers.comments: Clarify the credit distributions in this version. 97 pages, comments are welcome!

papers.title: Notes for a seminar on vortex layer cascades
papers.abstract: After the seminars I recently gave at New York University, the University of Chicago, Princeton University and the University of Bonn and after having been asked by some people to publish these notes, I decided to upload them to arXiv. In recent years, the method of vortex layer cascades has successfully been applied to construct finite-time singularities in multiple fluid equations (3D Euler, Boussinesq, IPM, g-SQG...). In this talk, I will motivate and describe the method and sketch how it can be applied to the 2D Boussinesq and 2D non-homogeneous Euler equations. In both systems, the growth of the vorticity is driven by an accumulated hysteresis effect triggered by the cyclic deformation of the density layers, whose dynamics is governed by an infinite chain of degenerate pendula. Our work also settles the previously open question about global existence of classical solutions of the (forced) 2D non-homogeneous Euler equations.

papers.title: Dobrowolski-type lower bounds for canonical heights of polynomials of Frobenius type
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a number field and let $f\in\OK[x]$ be a monic polynomial of degree $d=p^r$ with $f\equiv x^d+c\pmod p$, such as $x^2+c$. We prove that every $α\in\Kbar$ of degree $D$ over $K$ with infinite orbit under $f$ satisfies $$\hh_f(α)\ \ge\ \frac{c_1}{D\log3D}\exp\bigl(-c_2\sqrt{\log3D}\bigr),$$ where $c_1,c_2>0$ depend only on $f$ and $K$. This implies $\hh_f(α)\ge D^{-1-o(1)}$, making progress towards the dynamical Lehmer conjecture. The polynomial $f$ need not be postcritically finite. For such polynomials, for instance $x^2+1$, no lower bound of polynomial decay in $D$ was previously known. For postcritically finite polynomials such as $x^2-1$, it improves the recent quadratic bound of Habegger and Schmidt. The method is motivated by Dobrowolski's proof on Lehmer's problem.

papers.title: An elliptic Lehmer bound of exponent one at a supersingular prime
papers.abstract: Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over a number field $K$ with good supersingular reduction at a prime $\p$. We prove that the Néron--Tate height of every non-torsion $P\in E(\Kbar)$ satisfies $\hh_E(P)\ge c\,D^{-1}(\log3D)^{-1}\exp(-c'\sqrt{\log3D})$, where $D=[K(x(P)):K]$ and $c,c'>0$ depend only on $E$, $K$ and $\p$; so $\hh_E(P)\ge D^{-1-o(1)}$. By a result of Elkies this applies to every elliptic curve over $\QQ$, and it improves the exponents of Masser and of Hindry and Silverman.

papers.title: Practical limitations on robustness and scalability of quantum Internet
papers.abstract: The realization of a desirably functional quantum Internet is hindered by fundamental and practical challenges such as high loss during transmission of quantum systems, decoherence due to interaction with the environment, fragility of quantum states under measurement, etc. We study the implications of these constraints by analyzing the limitations on the scaling and robustness of the quantum Internet. Considering quantum networks, we present practical bottlenecks for secure communication, delegated computing, and resource distribution among end nodes. In particular, we show that the device-independent quantum key distribution (DI-QKD) network of isotropic states with parameter $p$ has a finite diameter depending on $p$. Motivated by the power of abstraction in graph theory (in association with quantum information theory), that allows us to consider the topology of a network of users spatially separated over long distances around the globe or separated as nodes within the small space over a processor or circuit within a same framework, we consider graph-theoretic quantifiers to assess network robustness and provide critical values of communication lines for viable communication over quantum Internet. We consider some quantum networks of practical interest, ranging from satellite-based networks connecting far-off spatial locations to currently available quantum processor architectures within computers, and analyze their robustness to perform quantum information processing tasks. Some of these tasks form primitives for delegated quantum computing, e.g., entanglement distribution and quantum teleportation, that are desirable for all scale of quantum networks, be it quantum processors or quantum Internet.
papers.comments: Happy about the successful soft landing of Chandrayaan-3 on the moon by ISRO. 37 pages, 37 figures. Revised version

papers.title: Asymptotic Properties of the Maximum Likelihood Estimator for Markov-Switching Observation-Driven Models
papers.abstract: A Markov-switching observation-driven model is a stochastic process $((S_t,Y_t))_{t \in \mathbb{Z}}$ where $(S_t)_{t \in \mathbb{Z}}$ is an unobserved Markov chain with finite state space and $(Y_t)_{t \in \mathbb{Z}}$ is an observed stochastic process such that the conditional distribution of $Y_t$ given $(Y_τ)_{τ\leq t-1}$ and $(S_τ)_{τ\leq t}$ depends only on $(Y_τ)_{τ\leq t-1}$, through time-varying parameters, and $S_t$. In this paper, we prove consistency and asymptotic normality of the maximum likelihood estimator for such a model. As a special case, we also give conditions under which the maximum likelihood estimator for the widely applied Markov-switching generalised autoregressive conditional heteroscedasticity model introduced by Haas, Mittnik, and Paolella (2004b) is consistent and asymptotically normal.

papers.title: Propositional Dynamic Logic has Craig Interpolation: a tableau-based proof
papers.abstract: We show that Propositional Dynamic Logic (PDL) has the Craig Interpolation Property. This question has been open for many years. Three proof attempts were published, but later criticized in the literature or retracted. Our proof is based on the main ideas from Borzechowski (1988, master thesis). We define a cyclic tableau system for PDL with a loading mechanism to recognize successful repeats. For this system, we show soundness and completeness via a game. To show interpolation, we modify Maehara's method to work for tableaux with repeats: we first define pre-interpolants at each node, and then use a quasi-tableau to define interpolants for clusters (strongly connected components). In different terms, our method solves the fixpoint equations that characterize the desired interpolants, and the method ensures that the solutions to these equations can be expressed within PDL. The proof is constructive and we show how to compute interpolants. We make available a Haskell implementation of the proof system that provides interpolants, and a formal verification of our proof in the interactive theorem prover Lean. Lastly, we discuss several questions for future work.

papers.title: Hadrons in group expansion
papers.abstract: We develop a general framework for describing symmetry-breaking responses in physical systems with approximate symmetries. Hadronic systems provide a particularly rich setting for investigating such symmetries. For example, the flavor $SU(4)$ symmetry involving the $u$, $d$, $s$, and $c$ quarks is severely broken, the flavor $SU(3)$ symmetry involving the $u$, $d$, and $s$ quarks is moderately broken, and the isospin $SU(2)$ symmetry involving the $u$ and $d$ quarks is only slightly broken. An important question is how a physical system responds to further symmetry breaking when its symmetry has already been partially broken. Motivated by the observed mass nonadditivity of vector mesons, we formulate this framework in terms of the group expansion, in which higher-order responses may modify the coefficients within the inherited response space or unlock additional independent response directions outside this space. We refer to these two effects as coefficient evolution and response unlocking, respectively, and develop a differential description connecting the interaction flow, mass flow, and state flow. We apply this framework to $J^P=1^-$ vector mesons and $J^P=3/2^+$ and $1/2^+$ baryons within flavor $SU(4)$ and $SU(5)$ reference spaces. These analyses illustrate how the internal structure and dynamics of a physical system, together with additional symmetries, can shape and constrain its symmetry-breaking responses. The group expansion thus provides a unified framework for organizing the evolution, correlations, and constraints of symmetry-breaking responses, with potential applications beyond hadronic systems.
papers.comments: 55 pages, 5 figures, 14 tables; major revision with an expanded theoretical framework and new applications to baryons

papers.title: Quantitative Quantum Soundness for Bipartite Compiled Bell Games via the Sequential NPA Hierarchy
papers.abstract: Compiling Bell games under cryptographic assumptions replaces the need for physical separation, allowing nonlocality to be probed with a single untrusted device. While Kalai et al. (STOC'23) showed that this compilation preserves quantum advantages, its quantitative quantum soundness has remained an open problem. We address this gap with two primary contributions. First, we establish the first quantitative quantum soundness bounds for all bipartite compiled Bell games via a newly formalized convergent sequential Navascués-Pironio-Acín (NPA) hierarchy: any polynomial-time prover's score is controlled by a finite-level hierarchy value, and finite-level convergence gives a negligible gap to the commuting quantum value, or to the tensor-product quantum value under flat optimality. Second, we develop the sequential NPA hierarchy as a computational tool of independent interest, establishing its convergence and a stopping criterion based on flatness, and identifying its conic dual as a sparse SOS hierarchy.
papers.comments: 43 pages, 1 figure. Accepted for publication in Quantum. See Section 4 of v2 for a discussion of whether the NPA convergence rate is necessary. For independent parallel work, see Cui, Falor, Natarajan and Zhang (arXiv:2507.17581)

papers.title: Derivative Estimation from Coarse, Irregular, Noisy Samples: An MLE-Spline Approach
papers.abstract: We address numerical differentiation under coarse, non-uniform sampling and Gaussian noise. A maximum-likelihood estimator with $L_2$-norm constraint on a higher-order derivative is obtained, yielding spline-based solution. We introduce a non-standard parameterization of quadratic splines and develop recursive online algorithms. Two formulations---quadratic and zero-order---offer tradeoff between smoothness and computational speed. Simulations demonstrate superior performance over high-gain observers and super-twisting differentiators under coarse sampling and high noise, benefiting systems where higher sampling rates are impractical.

papers.title: An elementary proof that linking problems are hard
papers.abstract: We give a new, elementary proof of what we believe is the simplest known example of a "natural" problem in computational 3-dimensional topology that is NP-hard---namely, the Trivial Sublink Problem: given a diagram $L$ of a link in $S^3$ and a positive integer $k$, decide if $L$ contains a $k$ component sublink that is trivial. This problem was previously shown to be NP-hard in independent works of Koenig-Tsvietkova and de Mesmay-Rieck-Sedgwick-Tancer, both of which used reductions from 3SAT. The reduction we describe instead starts with the Independent Set Problem, and allows us to avoid the use of Brunnian links such as the Borromean rings. On the technical level, this entails a new conceptual insight: the Trivial Sublink Problem is hard entirely due to mod 2 pairwise linking, with no need for integral or higher order linking. On the pedagogical level, the reduction we describe is entirely elementary, and thus suitable for introducing undergraduates and non-experts to complexity-theoretic low-dimensional topology. To drive this point home, in this work we assume no familiarity with low-dimensional topology, and---other than Reidemeister's Theorem and Karp's result that the Clique Problem is NP-hard---we provide more-or-less complete definitions and proofs. We have also constructed a web app that accompanies this work and allows a user to visualize the new reduction interactively.
papers.comments: V2 has many more figures and expanded exposition. See URL on page 9 for accompanying web app. Many thanks to Martin Tancer and Yo'av Rieck. To appear in Involve - a journal of mathematics

papers.title: Fixed Points and Envelope Dynamics on Credal Hyperspaces
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a compact metric space and consider the hyperspace $\mathscr C_X$ of nonempty weakly closed convex sets of Borel probability measures on $X$, called credal sets. These sets represent uncertainty about which probability law governs the phenomenon of interest. We equip $\mathscr C_X$ with the Hausdorff metric induced by a metric for weak convergence. Credal order intervals $[\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B}] = \{ \mathcal{P}\in\mathscr C_X: \mathcal{A}\subseteq\mathcal{P}\subseteq\mathcal{B} \}$ are complete lattices, and every inclusion-monotone, Hausdorff-continuous self map of such an interval has least and greatest fixed points obtained as limits of iteration from $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{B}$. For families of inclusion-monotone updates that may vary with time, we construct lower and upper envelope maps that bound every admissible trajectory. When these envelope maps are Hausdorff-continuous, the distance of every trajectory from a limiting credal interval vanishes uniformly over all switching sequences and initial credal sets. Coalescence of the limiting interval endpoints yields convergence to a common credal limit. We then construct the credal evolution induced by a time consistent Nisio semigroup. Uniform $W_1$ contraction of the underlying Markov semigroups induces Hausdorff-Wasserstein contraction of the credal evolution, yielding a unique common invariant credal set, exponential convergence from every initial credal set, and a support functional equal to the robust ergodic limit. We also derive perturbation bounds from finite time Nisio discrepancies and one step kernel set discrepancies, and characterize the countable sequences of support coordinates that represent credal sets, providing an explicit reconstruction formula.

papers.title: Debiased Inference via Posterior Corrections for High-Dimensional Regression
papers.abstract: There has been significant progress in Bayesian inference based on sparsity-inducing priors, such as spike-and-slab and horseshoe priors, for high-dimensional regression. The resulting posteriors, however, in general do not possess desirable frequentist properties, and the credible sets thus cannot serve as valid confidence sets even asymptotically. We introduce a novel debiasing approach that corrects the bias for the entire (possibly approximate) Bayesian posterior distribution. We establish new Bernstein-von Mises theorems that guarantee the frequentist validity of the debiased law. We demonstrate the practical performance of our proposal through Monte Carlo simulations and two empirical applications in economics.

papers.title: Multi-UAV Trajectory Optimization for Bearing-Only Localization in GPS Denied Environments
papers.abstract: Accurate localization of maritime targets by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) remains challenging in GPS-denied environments. UAVs equipped with gimballed electro-optical sensors are typically used to localize targets; however, reliance on these sensors increases mechanical complexity, cost, and susceptibility to single-point failures, limiting scalability and robustness in multi-UAV operations. This work presents a new trajectory optimization framework that enables cooperative target localization using UAVs with fixed, non-gimballed cameras operating in coordination with a surface vessel. This estimation-aware optimization generates dynamically feasible trajectories that explicitly account for mission constraints, platform dynamics, and out-of-frame events. Estimation-aware trajectories outperform heuristic paths by reducing localization error by more than a factor of two, motivating their use in cooperative operations. Results further demonstrate that coordinated UAVs with fixed, non-gimballed cameras achieve localization accuracy that meets or exceeds that of single gimballed systems, while substantially lowering system complexity and cost, enabling scalability, and enhancing mission resilience.
papers.comments: Published open access in the Journal of Guidance, Control, and Dynamics. 41 pages, 8 figure, and 6 tables

papers.title: Biologically Inspired Coordination of Parameter Selection and Update Strength for Language Model Adaptation
papers.abstract: Adapting a source-trained language model to a target task requires deciding which parameters to update and how strongly when learning signals are uncertain. We introduce Synapse Consolidation (SyCo), a biologically inspired framework that coordinates these two controls. Rac1-associated forgetting and memory-trace redistribution motivate retaining selected source-derived low-rank components while resetting others for target adaptation. MAPK-associated signal processing motivates combining multiple prediction-based indicators over time to regulate update strength. SyCo combines these controls with a structured consistency objective and a small, fixed buffer of labelled source examples. Target labels are not used during adaptation. We evaluate the framework in Multi-source Open-set Adaptation (MOA), using source-initialized target learners for tasks absent from source training and for perturbed held-out inputs from source tasks. Across 18 natural-language-processing datasets, SyCo reaches 78.01% average accuracy on unseen-task adaptation and 85.37% under unseen-data shifts, outperforming the strongest evaluated hybrid baselines. Ablations support complementary contributions from selective plasticity, evidence-guided update control and structured consistency. These results show how coordinated control of update location and strength can improve target adaptation under uncertain learning signals.

papers.title: Relaxed magnetohydrodynamics with cross-field flow
papers.abstract: The phase-space Lagrangian model of Dewar et al. (Phys. Plasmas 27, 062507, 2020) provides a framework for incorporating cross-field flow into relaxed equilibria while retaining ideal magnetohydrodynamics force balance. Here, we characterize the steady-state solution space and identify a solvability condition that couples the prescribed constrained flow to the geometry through the metric tensor. Using this condition, we construct equilibria in slab, cylindrical, and toroidal geometries. In toroidal geometry, the cross-field flow strongly correlates with magnetic-island structure: varying the rotation frequency modifies the dominant Fourier harmonic of the radial component of the magnetic field and can drive a transition from a primary (m = 1) island to secondary (m = 2) islands. In slab and cylindrical geometries, flow parameters weakly affect island width but strongly modify equilibrium profiles.

papers.title: An Implicit Compact-Kernel Material Point Method for Computational Solid Mechanics
papers.abstract: The numerical performance of the material point method (MPM) is strongly governed by the particle-grid kernel, which controls the trade-off among smoothness, locality, numerical diffusion, contact accuracy, and computational cost. Although wide-support smooth kernels can effectively suppress cell-crossing instability, they often introduce increased numerical diffusion, artificial contact gaps, and higher transfer cost. In contrast, the suitability of compact-kernel designs for implicit computational solid mechanics remains unclear. In this work, we develop an implicit formulation of the Compact-Kernel Material Point Method (CK-MPM) building on the framework of Liu et al. [2025], and assess its performance through benchmark problems in linear and nonlinear solid mechanics. Numerical assessment comprises cantilever bending, Hertzian contact, narrow-clearance free fall, and colliding hyperelastic rings, supplemented by a transfer-only diffusion test and spatial and temporal refinement studies. Implicit CK-MPM mitigates the cell-crossing stress noise and numerical energy loss observed in linear MPM, while retaining bending and energy responses comparable to those of quadratic B-spline MPM. Meanwhile, its more localized transfers improve contact-pressure accuracy and reduce the artificial contact gaps and early-contact artifacts associated with the wider-support quadratic kernel. These results demonstrate that the developed implicit formulation retains CK-MPM's favorable balance between smoothness and transfer locality in static and dynamic solid-mechanics analysis.

papers.title: Anisotropy in Fourier space optical memory effect correlations
papers.abstract: We investigate anisotropy in Fourier-domain speckle correlations associated with the optical memory effect in disordered scattering media. Within a single scattering framework, we show that while the conventional memory effect constrains transverse wavevector shifts, the correlation strength also depends non-trivially on differences in the axial wavevector components. Our theory is supported by numerical simulations of a three-dimensional, single scattering medium, which show excellent agreement with theory. We extend the analysis to pseudo-correlations, demonstrating that analogous anisotropic behavior arises in the conjugate memory effect. Our results highlight the often overlooked role of axial disorder in scattered field correlations.

papers.title: Vote-Left: A Deterministic Coordination Strategy for the Faithful in The Traitors
papers.abstract: The Traitors is a social deduction game in which an informed minority of Traitors face an uninformed majority of Faithful, and the recurring question facing the Faithful is how to vote. Eliminating a player chosen uniformly at random is optimal for the Faithful when it can be guaranteed, but when votes are cast individually a random vote is indistinguishable from a strategic one, leaving the Faithful exposed to coordinated Traitor collusion. We introduce the Vote-Left protocol, a deterministic rule under which every player votes for the next surviving player in a fixed cyclic ordering. It reproduces the banishment distribution of random voting, yet any deviation from it is immediately identifiable. Combined with a simple punishment rule, Vote-Left punishes every deviation in the main phase of the game that does not end it at once, whether by a single player or by the Traitors acting together. In the final rounds punishment arrives too late, and the Faithful should return to random voting there. Under this switching protocol no player gains by departing from Vote-Left in the main phase, and with a single Traitor it is a Perfect Bayesian Equilibrium of the whole game. Across the televised configurations, it raises the Faithful's winning probability by a factor of approximately four over random voting under collusion with three Traitors, and by a factor of 62 to 84 with four.

papers.title: Variational approach to droplet motion on uneven solid surfaces, including contact line dynamics and evaporation
papers.abstract: We show how dynamical equations for liquid films and drops on uneven surfaces, including contact line dynamics and evaporation/condensation effects, may be formulated as a variational dynamics, generated via Onsager's variational principle. The theory applies in the isothermal overdamped-dynamics limit. We apply this general approach to obtain several well-known results on contact line dynamics and to study drops pinning and sliding on inclined corrugated surfaces. This approach constructs the dynamical equations starting from the free energy of the system and therefore has the advantage that it naturally incorporates the correct equilibrium properties.

papers.title: Global linear convergence of entropy-regularized softmax policy gradient beyond tabular MDPs
papers.abstract: We study the global convergence of policy gradient for infinite-horizon entropy-regularized Markov decision processes (MDPs) with continuous state and action spaces. We consider log-linear softmax policies with linear function approximation, which extend the tabular softmax parameterization while retaining a tractable policy class. Under $Q^π_τ$-realizability up to a state-dependent baseline for the regularized state-action value function, we establish a non-uniform Polyak-Lojasiewicz (PL) inequality for two different feature regimes. The non-uniformity arises through degeneracy of the state-averaged Fisher information matrix in the first feature regime and the uncentered feature second-moment matrix in the second. In both regimes we prove that these non-uniform constants can be bounded uniformly from below along the gradient flow. For full-affine-span features, we prove radial unboundedness of the KL regularizer and show that the state averaged smallest eigenvalue of the Fisher information matrix remains bounded below by an initialization-dependent positive constant. For simplex-valued features, we prove an analogous radial unboundedness result in the subspace orthogonal to the one vector and obtain an initialization dependent lower bound for the state averaged smallest eigenvalue of the uncentered second-moment matrix. These results imply global linear convergence of the regularized objective along the gradient flow, i.e., suboptimality decaying as $\mathcal{O}(e^{-Ct})$ for some $C>0$. Our analysis complements the global convergence theory of entropy-regularized softmax policy gradient beyond the tabular setting of Agarwal et al. (2020); Bhandari and Russo (2024); Mei et al. (2020).

papers.title: Weyl conformal geometry vs Riemannian geometry of Weyl gauge invariant (dressed) metric
papers.abstract: Weyl conformal geometry is the natural underlying geometry of gauge theories of Weyl group (of dilatations and Poincaré symmetry), such as Weyl quadratic gravity and its generalisation, Weyl-Dirac-Born-Infeld action (WDBI). These are local, Weyl-anomaly free (quantum) gauge theories of gravity. We describe Weyl gauge symmetry from a more familiar Riemannian view of Weyl gauge invariant dressed fields by the Wilson line of dilatations. Weyl geometry can then be seen as Riemannian geometry of non-local dressed metric ($g_{μν}^*$), at the "cost" of (gauge-induced) non-commutativity in the UV, due to Wilson line. Then Weyl quadratic gravity and WDBI actions of Weyl geometry, which are Weyl gauge invariant in $d$ dimensions, have the same expression in Riemannian geometry defined by $g^*_{μν}$. This is a non-local map and dual description of the two geometries and actions in the symmetric phase. Unlike for the metric, the equation of motion of Weyl gauge field ($ω_μ$) does not commute with the dressing of the metric. Quantum non-locality, in particular entanglement, and non-commutativity are (gauge-invariant) physical artefacts of "translating" (local) Weyl geometry and Weyl gauge covariance into our real-world Riemannian geometry of Weyl gauge invariant observables, and they are evidence of Weyl gauge symmetry. At lower energies, $ω_μ$ becomes massive, can decouple and Einstein-Hilbert action and commutativity are recovered. The case of a light $ω_μ$ is also discussed.

papers.title: Norms, overlaps and Yangian descendants for the Haldane-Shastry spin chain
papers.abstract: The Haldane-Shastry spin chain is a prototypical integrable model with long-range interactions, notable for hosting quasiparticles with fractional statistics and serving as a discrete analogue of a conformal field theory. Its remarkable simplicity is closely tied to a full Yangian spin symmetry. While the highest-weight states for this symmetry are known explicitly, a systematic treatment of the descendant states, needed for the computation of various physical quantities, has remained incomplete. In this work, we provide a detailed construction of these descendants in terms of the algebraic Bethe ansatz following recent work of Ferrando et al. In the limit of extreme twist, it includes the Gelfand-Tsetlin basis. As an application, we derive product and determinant formulae for norms and overlaps of these states.

papers.title: Adaptive Volumetric Parameterization of Simply Connected 3-Manifolds with Applications
papers.abstract: Volumetric parameterization, the process of mapping a 3-manifold onto a simplified volumetric domain, is important for many tasks in computer graphics and imaging science. However, most prior volumetric parameterization approaches have only utilized standardized domains such as a solid ball regardless of the overall shape of the given 3-manifolds, which introduces significant geometric distortion and affects the subsequent shape processing and analysis tasks. To overcome this issue, in this work we propose a novel volumetric parameterization framework for simply connected 3-manifolds. Specifically, the proposed framework jointly controls local shape and mass distortions, while adapting the target domain during the optimization process. It enables three progressively more flexible target-domain settings for the parameterization: a prescribed solid ellipsoid, a volume-normalized adaptive ellipsoid with variable radii, and a sea-embedded free-boundary domain. For each setting, the parameterization algorithm consists of a 3D quasi-conformality shape update, a diffusion-based density-equalizing update, and a geometric correction procedure for removing element foldings, thereby allowing for volumetric parameterizations with different desired effects. Experimental results are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed framework. Moreover, our framework can be easily applied to multiresolution and localized adaptive volumetric remeshing, volumetric registration, and volumetric morphing. Altogether, our work provides a new way for the representation, processing, and analysis of 3-manifolds.

papers.title: Mathematical inverse problem for the world data inference of the parton distribution functions of the proton
papers.abstract: We show that the inference problem of constraining the parton distribution functions of the proton from deeply inelastic scattering data can be formulated as a linear tensor reconstruction inverse problem. This means that instead of fitting model parameters to the world data, a reconstructive approach to solve a system of coupled linear functional integral equations can be formulated. We leverage the mathematical structures of the integral equations defined by perturbative QCD and global analysis to pose the problem of global analysis as a coupled system of linear integral equations, and construct a proof-of-principle methodology to solve it. To formulate this approach concretely, we review all next-to-leading order accuracy results for inclusive virtual photon, neutral current, charged current, heavy flavor production, and neutrino deep-inelastic lepton--proton scattering. This mathematical methodology of inference opens a path towards a parametrization-bias-free extraction of the proton PDFs from the world data of deeply inelastic scattering in the spirit of indirect measurement employed in mathematical inverse problems, including robust estimation of uncertainties with reduced bias from model parametrization, while closely adhering to the established paradigm of perturbative QCD and global analysis.
papers.comments: 124 pages, 1 figure; v2 matches the published version

papers.title: Parallel Policy-Gradient Methods for Parameter Optimization of Nonlinear Feedback Controllers
papers.abstract: Structured feedback controllers provide stability guarantees, but their performance depends on manually tuned parameters. Policy-gradient methods offer a systematic way to tune these parameters, but evaluating the gradient is computationally expensive because it requires a sequential forward rollout of the state dynamics followed by a backward rollout of the costate dynamics. This letter develops a time-parallel policy-gradient framework for discrete-time nonlinear control-affine systems. We evaluate the policy gradient by formulating the forward state and backward costate rollouts as residual-minimization problems and solving them with Gauss-Newton (GN) iterations that use parallel associative scans. We show that global asymptotic stability and local exponential stability of the closed loop guarantee convergence of the parallel state solver without requiring bounds on Jacobian products throughout the state space. Near the exact trajectory, GN iterations converge quadratically in a neighborhood whose size is independent of the horizon T. When initialized at the equilibrium trajectory, a clipped variant converges at a linear rate that is also independent of T. We also quantify how horizon truncation and solver tolerance affect the accuracy of the policy gradient. Experiments on an LQR problem and a lossless Lorenz-96 system with saturated passivity-based control demonstrate improved closed-loop performance and computational benefits.

papers.title: Separation of variables for non-diagonalisable models: XXX with twisted boundary conditions
papers.abstract: We study the Heisenberg XXX spin chain with twisted periodic boundary conditions with a defective twist matrix. Using quantum separation of variables, we show that the generalised eigenvectors of this system can be characterised in terms of a modified TQ equation that we have named "Jordanian TQ equation". We also show that the wavefunction in the separated basis is only separable for true eigenvectors, while the wavefunction for generalised eigenvectors of higher rank is given instead by a sum over weak compositions.
papers.comments: 24 pages. v2, Typos corrected, references updated. v3, Typos corrected

papers.title: Simultaneous Reduction of Observables and Measured Qudits in Entanglement-Assisted Quantum Local Recovery
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be the finite field with $q$ elements, $q$ being a prime power. For an entanglement-assisted or unassisted stabilizer code defined by an $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear space $C\subseteq\mathbb{F}_q^{2n}$, a set of erasures and an associated repair group, we propose a procedure to compute a reduced set of observables and a reduced repair group of codeword qudits for correcting the given erasures. The computed set of observables has the smallest possible size for correcting the given erasures, within the stabilizer measurement model. The repair group is reduced by eliminating qudits that need not be measured. In classical local recovery, such symbols can be found by Gaussian elimination, although the resulting repair group need not be a smallest one. In the quantum case we eliminate an admissible set of qudits. Finding a largest admissible set is a linear matroid parity problem, and for Calderbank--Shor--Steane (CSS) codes defined by two linear codes it is a linear matroid intersection problem. Both problems are solvable in deterministic polynomial time. We give closed-form upper bounds on the size of reduced repair groups for general codes and for codes from Euclidean and Hermitian orthogonality, and, for two-code CSS codes, a sharper bound with a min--max formula. Based on these bounds, we propose quantum counterparts of the concept of dimension locality of classical local recovery.
papers.comments: The new authors extended and improved the results from v1 by using matroid theory. This is a continuation of arXiv:2608.04403

papers.title: Even Sharper Bounds for Transductive Learning and Its Applications
papers.abstract: We introduce Sharper Transductive Local Complexity (STLC) as a new tool for improving current transductive bounds. Although Local Rademacher Complexity (LRC) has been used to obtain sharp inductive generalization bounds and local-complexity-based transductive bounds, it has remained open whether a localized Rademacher-complexity framework can achieve the same fixed-point and confidence structure as its inductive counterpart. STLC provides an affirmative answer to this question. STLC is constructed by first deriving a new Bernstein-type concentration inequality for the test-train process, under uniform sampling without replacement. The proof uses a new two-parameter entropy argument based on the modified log-Sobolev inequality for the swap walk. A subsequent peeling strategy with a surrogate localization functional yields transductive excess-risk bounds that match the fixed-point and confidence structure of the classical LRC-based inductive bounds without the additional logarithmic confidence gap in existing works. We further advance transductive learning through two applications. First, for realizable transductive learning over a binary-valued class of VC dimension $2\le d <\infty$ with $u\ge m\ge d$, where $u$ and $m$ are the test and training sizes, STLC gives the upper bound $O(d\log(me/d)/m}$. This rate matches the classical LRC-based, standard ERM-style inductive upper bound. It remains a logarithmic factor $\log(me/d)$ above both the optimal realizable inductive PAC rate and the transductive minimax lower bound, which are of order $d/m$. Our prior work achieves the excess risk of $O(d/m)$ in a transductive setup by randomized learning. Second, STLC gives a sharper, spectrum-adaptive excess-risk bound for transductive kernel learning than the prior local-complexity-based result.

papers.title: Twisted Cohomology of D-Brane Disk Integrals
papers.abstract: Disk-level scattering amplitudes involving one Ramond--Ramond and two NSNS states on a D-brane obey nontrivial identities among scalar world-sheet integrals imposed by gauge and T-duality Ward identities. We investigate the cohomological organization of these relations using twisted de Rham cohomology and show that the Ward identities admit twisted-exact representatives. In the $I/J$ sector, the unique generic linear dependence among the Ward identities is realized one degree lower in the same twisted de Rham complex, revealing a common cohomological origin for the identities and their syzygy. We also identify independent pointwise algebraic relations among the integrands. An independent cohomological rank computation then establishes that the physically selected $I/J$ family spans a five-dimensional subspace of the top twisted cohomology at generic complexified kinematics. Extending the construction to the $K$-family, including the exceptional double-pole representative $K_3$, introduces no additional cohomology direction. For a D1-brane amplitude, we exhibit a physical polarization component in which six scalar periods reduce to one at special kinematics.
papers.comments: Substantially revised and expanded version, with additional derivations, appendices, and references; 30 pages

papers.title: Policy Iteration Is Not Polynomial for Deterministic Markov Decision Processes: The Price of Algorithmic Anarchy
papers.abstract: We establish exponential iteration lower bounds in the number of states for Howard's policy iteration on deterministic discounted and average-reward Markov decision processes (MDPs), with a constant number of actions per state. This rules out polynomial-time complexity of Howard's policy iteration in both settings. We further prove that a Dantzig counterpart of Howard's policy iteration runs in strongly polynomial time on deterministic average-reward MDPs. Together with the known strongly polynomial bound for Dantzig's rule on deterministic discounted MDPs, these results establish an exponential separation between the two algorithms in both settings. This separation between Howard's decentralized and simultaneous selfish improvements and Dantzig's coordinated selection of a single action with the largest improvement across all states reveals a "price" of algorithmic anarchy.

papers.title: Realizing Braided Fusion 2-Categories as (3+1)D Mixed-State Topological Orders
papers.abstract: We construct large families of mixed-state topological orders in (3+1)D, including intrinsically mixed-state topological orders. We realize these theories by relating the data parameterizing braided fusion 2-categories to the strong higher-form symmetries and their anomalies that characterize mixed-state topological order. We focus here on bosonic theories, which include theories which admit an emergent fermion in the spectrum of line operators. Our general framework is exemplified on the lattice, where we present concrete models and identify how the data of braided fusion 2-categories are physically encoded. We then formalize this data and show that every braided fusion 2-category arises from a general construction (decoherence followed by strong and weak gauging) as the category of topological operators of a (3+1)D mixed state, with intrinsically mixed-state topological orders distinguished by the presence of strong higher-form symmetries whose anomalies cannot be realized in any (3+1)D gapped ground state. Notably, we show that (3+1)D admits a new mechanism with no (2+1)D counterpart: intrinsically mixed-state order whose topological operators braid non-degenerately, but which carries a gravitational anomaly.

papers.title: Minimax estimation of the pseudo-spectral gap of continuous Markov chains, with applications to empirical concentration bounds
papers.abstract: We study the minimax estimation of the pseudo-spectral gap $γ_{ps}$ of a Markov chain from the observation of a single trajectory. Extending earlier works on finite-state space chains by Wolfer and Kontorovich (2024), we provide an estimator in the case of a compact, continuous state-space. Our estimator appears to be minimax-optimal on the class of chains with a transition operator with Lipschitz density, up to logarithmic terms. Our estimator, combined with Paulin's version of Bernstein inequality, allows to derive empirical concentration inequalities for Markov chains. This unlocks many applications, from confidence intervals, to active learning and generalization bounds. In particular, for rested bandits with Markov rewards, we provide a version of UCB with a regret bound similar to the one in the iid case, without assuming any knowledge on the pseudo-spectral gap of the chains.

papers.title: Undirected Multiple-Unicast Network Coding and Faster External-Memory Integer Sorting
papers.abstract: In undirected multiple-unicast networks, where independent messages are sent between specified source-destination pairs, network coding allows intermediate nodes to combine messages, whereas fractional routing splits and forwards individual messages along paths without mixing them. Proposed in 2004 by Li and Li and independently by Harvey, Kleinberg, and Lehman, the multiple-unicast conjecture---long a central open problem in network coding with deep connections to computational complexity---asserts that network coding and fractional routing have the same achievable rate region. We construct a counterexample refuting this conjecture and use it to reduce block transfers in external-memory data rearrangement, thereby accelerating external-memory integer sorting and answering in the affirmative the longstanding question of Aggarwal and Vitter (1988) on whether integer operations can beat the comparison-sorting input/output (I/O) bound. Specifically, we give a deterministic sorting algorithm: for $N$ integers of $Θ(\log N)$ bits, a memory holding $M$ integers, and block transfers of $B$ integers, where $2B\le M\le N$, the number of block transfers is $$O\!\left(\frac{N}{B}\left[1+\frac{\log N}{(\log(M/B))^{1-\varepsilon}(\log M)^\varepsilon}\right]\right),$$ where $\varepsilon=1.5\times10^{-5}$ is an absolute constant. This bound asymptotically improves on the classical $Θ\!\left(\frac{N}{B}\left[1+\frac{\log(N/M)}{\log(M/B)}\right]\right)$ comparison-sorting bound in certain parameter regimes. Under the external-memory model specified in this paper, we have formally verified the algorithm's correctness and I/O complexity bound in Lean 4. Our reduction is independent of the address-field interchange construction. Using the one from recent work on multitape integer multiplication gives the bound for every fixed $0<\varepsilon<1/2$, with an $\varepsilon$-dependent constant.
papers.comments: 45 pages, 4 figures, 1 table. New in v4: Appendix E extends the sorting bound to every fixed $0<\varepsilon<1/2$. Lean 4 code: https://github.com/rtyu-1/coded-sorting-lean

papers.title: High-Order Gaussian Approximation of Besov Functions on Manifolds
papers.abstract: We study high-order Gaussian approximation for Besov functions $f\in B^α_{2,\infty}(X)$ with $α>0$ on a compact smooth embedded manifold $X$ without boundary. For $r<α$, a suitable signed combination of Gaussian integral operators at different bandwidths gives an $H^r(X)$ error bounded by $Cγ^{α-r}\|f\|_{B^α_{2,\infty}(X)}$. The squared Gaussian RKHS norm of the approximant is bounded by $Cγ^{-\varrho}\|f\|_{L_2(X)}^2$, where $\varrho$ is the intrinsic dimension of $X$. We apply these approximation results to two statistical learning problems. For regularized Gaussian logistic classification, we combine the approximation bounds with a localized oracle inequality. For a potentially unbounded Bayes function in $B^α_{2,\infty}(X)$ and a marginal density in $L_p(X)$, the excess logistic risk has upper bounds of order $((\log n)^{\varrho+1}/n)^{2β/(2β+3\varrho)}$ for the unclipped predictor and $((\log n)^{\varrho+2}/n)^{β/(β+\varrho)}$ for clipped predictions with suitably selected parameters, where $β=2α(1-1/p)$. Under bounded marginal densities, our excess misclassification risk bound matches, up to logarithmic factors, the classical Hölder-class exponent. For elliptic operator learning, we assemble a Gaussian Galerkin solution operator from random manifold samples. Its error in the operator norm from $B^α_{2,\infty}(X)$ to $H^1(X)$ is bounded with high probability by two terms. The trial-space term has a decay exponent in the number of Gaussian centers that can approach $(α+1)/\varrho$. The bias and sampling term is of order $n^{-2N/(4N+\varrho)}$ for a fixed trial space, where $n$ is the number of sample pairs and $N$ is the number of Gaussian scales used for matrix assembly. The convergence rates for both problems depend on the intrinsic dimension $\varrho$ and are independent of the ambient dimension $d$.

papers.title: 5D Runge-Lenz Vector from Symplectic Reduction of 8D Harmonic Oscillator
papers.abstract: We investigate the origin of the Runge-Lenz vector of the five-dimensional Kepler problem in the SU(8) dynamical symmetry of the eight-dimensional harmonic oscillator acting on its phase space. Using a complete basis of real $8\times 8$ matrices constructed from five-dimensional gamma matrices and the $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ generators associated with the symplectic reduction, we decompose the conserved quantities of the harmonic oscillator into representations of $\mathrm{SO}(5) \times \mathrm{SU}(2)$ and identify the SU(2)-singlet sector. We show that the corresponding conserved quantities generate an SO(6) subgroup of the SU(8) dynamical symmetry. We then perform the Hurwitz transformation and symplectic reduction with respect to SU(2), obtaining the five-dimensional Kepler Hamiltonian. We explicitly show that the SO(6) moment map reduces to the angular momentum and the suitably normalized Runge-Lenz vector of the five-dimensional Kepler problem on a fixed negative-energy surface. This establishes the origin of the Runge-Lenz vector in the dynamical symmetry of the eight-dimensional harmonic oscillator.
papers.comments: improvements to discussions, references added, author affiliation corrected

papers.title: Researcher-in-the-Loop Evolutionary Discovery of Entanglement-Assisted Quantum Code Families
papers.abstract: LLM-guided program evolution can produce mathematical constructions, but validity, generality, and reproducibility require distinct evidence. In this paper, we develop a researcher-in-the-loop discovery pipeline combining program evolution, exact evaluation, mathematical generalization, and independent verification. We apply it to entanglement-assisted quantum error-correcting codes (EAQECCs). Evolved programs produced finite qubit constructions from specifications that supplied no family formula. Researcher-directed analysis with a language model led to a general construction and proof drafts, which the researchers revised and checked. The resulting family $[[n,1,n-1;n-q-1]]_q$ exists for prime powers $q\ge3$ at $n\ge2q+1$ and for $q=2$ at odd $n\ge5$; Lean checks its formalized algebraic core. With entanglement lifting, it closes 54 listed table gaps. The evidence includes 115 verified code records, ten DRAT-checked nonexistence results, family implementations and preserved search programs. Controlled studies test how research proposals interact with program generation. Under a mutation-and-restart proposal, iterative evolution improves normalized success-curve area in all ten paired runs and raises success at excluded lengths $n=13,15$ from 13.4% to 62.5% and from 0.9% to 33.4%, respectively. The benefit depends on the proposal. Selected programs combine the proposed moves with objective and restart-counter changes. The pipeline connects finite computational discoveries to a proved family and independently checkable constructions.
papers.comments: 35 pages, 11 figures. Code, data and Lean proofs: https://github.com/LeGenAI/llm_guided_EAQECC_search

papers.title: A new toric ALF gravitational instanton
papers.abstract: We construct a new explicit toric ALF gravitational instanton. The instanton has Euler characteristic $χ= 4$ and Hirzebruch signature $τ= -1$. The topology at infinity is a lens space $L(3,1)$. The solution depends on one parameter and is constructed from the Belinski--Zakharov four-soliton solution. We prove that the instanton is smooth and positive definite on and away from the axis. This is the first example of a non-Hermitian ALF (not AF) gravitational instanton.
papers.comments: 8 pages. v2: Fixed orientation consistency issues and typos

papers.title: Karhunen-Loève Transforms of Autoregressive Windows Based on Matched Symmetry Groups
papers.abstract: The Karhunen-Loève transform of a window of a stationary autoregressive process of any order $p$ is described through its poles, extending the Algebraic Diversity framework, which selects a transform by the matched group. For simple roots every basis vector is a sum of at most $p$ sinusoids, at the frequencies where the spectrum equals the eigenvalue, plus modes decaying from the ends. The window covariance differs from a member of the class diagonalized by the type-II discrete cosine transform by a closed-form matrix of rank $2p$, exactly when no pole is zero, so the eigenvalues interlace spectrum samples on the cosine grid, and the coding-gain loss of the cosine transform is an exact function of that matrix, below 1.2 percent for the $8\times8$ Markov block at pole $0.95$. By Kronecker's theorem the rank is at most $2\max(p,q)$ for rational spectra. A moving-average window departs in its Hankel corners, and an integrated (ARIMA) window departs by low rank from the type-VII sine class, exactly for the random walk. The exact symmetry is generically the reflection and contains a wreath product for interleaved windows. The dihedral group of the even extension is matched approximately, the dominant pole's sign choosing cosine or sine. The two groups give the transform a fast form: a parity fold, half-length cosine cores and a cascade of at most $p$ first-order Cauchy stages, exactly $p$ for a minimal AR($p$) model. The first-order case recovers results obtained by other means. This version adds complex data on the cyclic group with a border departure of rank exactly $2p$, the mixed and integrated classes, odd-length cores, and a released implementation whose kernel evaluation counts are flat in $M\log_2(M/n_{\mathrm{leaf}})$ to 5.3 percent. Experiments on recorded acoustic-array, radar and vibration data state where the transform helps and where existing methods match it.
papers.comments: v1: 38 pages, 7 figures; v2: 71 pages, 11 figures, 38 tables. Extended version with all proofs, adding a reference implementation, experiments on recorded data, and applications

papers.title: Extending indoor airborne infection risk modelling to 3D, with local surface deposition
papers.abstract: Mathematical models of indoor disease transmission often rely on simplifying assumptions to reduce computational cost. In particular, in the Viral Infection Risk Indoor Simulator (VIRIS)[13], which combines architectural layout, people movement and airborne viral transmission, aerosol concentrations are assumed uniform across room height, allowing a two-dimensional (2D) formulation. Also, particle deposition on surfaces is represented by a first-order removal term acting throughout the computational domain. Here, we extend VIRIS to the VIRIS-3D-L framework to investigate how these two assumptions affect the predicted infection risk. In VIRIS-3D-L, we solve the reaction-diffusion equation in three dimensions (3D), and aerosol deposition is represented by local surface removal through a Robin boundary condition. We compare VIRIS with VIRIS-3D-L across three indoor settings of increasing architectural and people-movement complexity: a courtroom, a care home, and a supermarket. For the courtroom, care home, and supermarket, respectively, at the end of the simulation, the original 2D formulation with global removal predicts average infection risks across individuals of 44%, 78%, and 25%, while VIRIS-3D-L predicts risks of 51%, 85%, and 28%. Thus, VIRIS significantly underestimates infection risk in all three settings. The predictions of VIRIS-3D-L also show agreement with a documented courtroom outbreak that was used to validate VIRIS. Although computation time increases by approximately a factor of four on average, simulations remain feasible on a standard laptop, taking between eight minutes and just under 1.5 hours. These findings suggest that VIRIS-3D-L offers a more physically realistic framework for assessing indoor airborne infection risk in indoor spaces without prohibitive computational costs.

papers.title: Littlestone Dimension and Its Dual
papers.abstract: The dual Littlestone dimension of a concept class $\mathcal{H}\subseteq\{0,1\}^{\mathcal{X}}$, $\operatorname{Ldim}^*(\mathcal{H}):=\operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal{H}^*)$, is the Littlestone dimension of the dual class $\mathcal{H}^*$, obtained by exchanging the roles of domain points and hypotheses. A classical result of Shelah implies that $\operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal{H})$ and $\operatorname{Ldim}^*(\mathcal{H})$ are finite simultaneously, and quantitative results of Hodges [Mathematika, 1981] imply the doubly exponential bound $\operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal{H})\le 2^{2^{O(\operatorname{Ldim}^*(\mathcal{H}))}}$. Malliaris and Moran [Trans. Amer. Math. Soc., 2024] asked whether this bound is optimal. We answer this by proving the bound \[ \operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal{H})\le 2^{O(\operatorname{Ldim}^*(\mathcal{H}))}, \] which is tight up to the constant in the exponent, as witnessed by the class of all binary hypotheses on a finite domain.
papers.comments: 10 pages, 2 figures, main theorem bound improved

papers.title: Symplectic Matroids, Stabilizer Codes, and Quantum Secret-Sharing
papers.abstract: An $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear $[[n,k]]_q$ stabilizer code is represented by a totally isotropic subspace of $\mathbb{F}_q^{2n}$ of dimension $n-k$, whose full-rank generator matrix has nonzero maximal minors on admissible column sets forming the bases of a representable symplectic matroid. Sarvepalli asked whether graphical symplectic matroids introduced by Chow give stabilizer codes with good parameters, when a Lagrangian matroid induces a quantum access structure, which code realizes it, and which polynomial carries the weight enumerator. We answer these questions. For a $3$-connected simple graph, every representation of a graphical symplectic matroid, over any field, gives a stabilizer code of distance exactly $2$, so the girth is not a lower bound. For a represented Lagrangian matroid and a dealer, we construct the dealer-shortened stabilizer code, its logical operators, an encoding isometry and explicit recovery maps, and we show that this is the code implemented by the stabilizer state through teleportation. A set of players recovers the secret, learns nothing, or learns part of it according to a rank formula on pairs of columns, which equals its mutual information with the dealer; for graph states it becomes a cut-rank condition. Over $\F_2$ a symplectic matroid of any rank has only one representation, so the code, its access structure and its weight enumerators depend on the matroid alone; for $q\ge3$ even the enumerator does not. Circuit-induced authorized sets always reconstruct when the matroid is self-dual, but not in general, and a six-qubit graph state shows that the two access structures can differ even then. Finally, a polynomial in the ranks of column pairs determines both weight enumerators.

papers.title: Full-chip constrained quantum annealing via self-calibrating spin-susceptibility control
papers.abstract: Discrete optimization in finance, power grids, and logistics requires minimizing Ising Hamiltonians under coupled linear constraints. However, quadratic-penalty formulations superimpose dense cliques that exhaust the minor-embedding capacity of sparse superconducting processors at 128-176 spins, and first-order dual subgradient schemes diverge or stall under constraint coupling. Accordingly, this study proposes a hardware-native quantum-classical closed-loop primal-dual workflow, designated as Self-Calibrating Quantum Susceptibility Quasi-Newton (SelfCal-QSQN), in which linear constraints are encoded in longitudinal fields with zero auxiliary quadratic penalty couplings and dual curvature is reconstructed from single-shot spin-fluctuation covariances. This workflow requires no slack qubits or perturbation queries. Evaluated over 891 runs on D-Wave Advantage (5,612 qubits) and Advantage2 (4,560 qubits), SelfCal-QSQN drives the pre-polish trajectory-minimum raw QPU sample violation to $0.108 \pm 0.017$ at 4,560 qubits (83.3% exact feasibility after a deterministic 1-bit polish with best-incumbent tracking, reaching 47.3% of the continuous linear-programming relaxation bound), reduces high-constraint error by 6.1- to 20.1-fold over K-scaled first-order updates, attains 5.35-fold deeper feasible energies than linear programming with the identical 1-bit polish within a 4.10-s compute-only budget at 256 spins, and achieves 95.0%-96.7% feasibility on non-native and inequality benchmarks. Moreover, the workflow is robust toward shot noise and freeze-out drift.
papers.comments: 14 pages, 5 figures, 3 tables. v2: expanded classical baseline comparisons, runtime breakdowns, and full-chip LP lower-bound verification

papers.title: Sampling with graph wavelet kernels: optimality and adaptivity to regularity and geometry
papers.abstract: We construct wavelet-based determinantal samplers on manifolds and geometric graphs whose approximation rates adapt to the regularity of the observable. On a Riemannian manifold of dimension $m$, our wavelet DPPs satisfy variance reduction of order $n^{1-2s/m}$ for linear statistics of both $s$-Hölder and $H^s$ observables, where $0<s\le1$. Using these samplers, we further construct unbiased quadrature rules with root mean square error $O(n^{-1/2-s/m})$ using at most $3n/2$ function evaluations, matching the classical optimal randomized integration exponent. For point clouds sampled from an $m$-dimensional manifold, we develop corresponding determinantal samplers on two standard classes of geometric random graphs: $\varepsilon$-graphs and symmetric $k$-nearest-neighbour graphs. These samplers satisfy the same variance reduction for linear statistics of $s$-Hölder observables and yield conditionally unbiased estimators of empirical averages with root mean square error $O(n^{-1/2-s/m})$, using at most $2n$ function evaluations. In both settings, the rates are governed by the intrinsic dimension $m$ and the regularity $s$ of the observable.

papers.title: Physics-Constrained Neural ODEs for Learning Traffic Dynamics and Trajectories from Road Entry/Exit Times
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of learning microscopic traffic dynamics and reconstructing vehicle trajectories from section entry/exit timestamps (EET) recorded by cameras and from the positions of a probe vehicle leading the platoon. The dynamics are difficult to recover as each vehicle's position is measured only at two points, and its trajectory between them is unknown. By combining Neural ODEs with a local density approximation, we learn a follow-the-leader model whose speed--density relation is a neural network. With such sparse data, an unconstrained network may learn physically unrealistic relations, such as negative speeds or non-zero speeds on a fully congested road. We therefore introduce a normalization that, applied to a monotone neural network with a learned regime change, enforces the endpoint conditions, guaranteeing an admissible speed--density relation while provably retaining the ability to approximate any admissible one. We validate the method on first- and second-order simulations, recovering the speed--density relation of the first-order model and reconstructing the trajectories of both models, with mean maximum position errors of 2.50~m and 2.51~m, respectively, on a 125~m road segment. On real-world ring-road data, the proposed model still yields an admissible relation, whereas both baselines violate the constraints; the large spread in the data, however, highlights the limitations of a first-order model with homogeneous driver behaviors.

papers.title: Tensionless M5-brane in light-cone gauge. The spinor moving frame method is wanted
papers.abstract: We perform the complete light--cone gauge fixing for the tensionless limit of the M-theory 5-brane the action for which was recently obtained in [1]. The problem of gauge fixing of local fermionic $κ$--symmetry becomes quite nontrivial because the projector of that is constructed from the gauge field strength which is required to be nonvanishing and nontrivial in this limit for its consistency. To resolve this problem the spinor moving frame method has been adapted. The corresponding moving frame is constructed on a vector quadratic in the gauge field strength, which is required to be nonvanishing and nondegenerate in the tensionless limit, and the derivative of the PST (Pasti-Sorokin-Tonin) scalar. The symmetries of the gauge fixed action and equations of motion are briefly discussed. To make a comparison with the case of usual tensionless p-branes (null-p-branes), those which do not carry worldvolume gauge fields, we also elaborate their spinor moving frame formulation.
papers.comments: 26 pages. V2: A few misprints corrected. RevTex style, 19 pages

papers.title: Morphogenic necking of surfaces
papers.abstract: Surface morphogenesis occurs across biological scales, from subcellular vesicles and cells to visceral organs, tissue organoids, and whole organisms. Since morphogenesis often involves changes in topology, a natural question is that of appropriate mathematical descriptions that provide an approach to topological transitions of thin surfaces. Here, we suggest a general intrinsic framework coupling morphogen organization to surface geometry. We propose a minimal geometric model in which smoothing competes with morphogen-induced deformation to regulate shape, while loss of this balance can bring a surface toward a topological transition via neck constriction. A simple dynamical model coupling a scalar field to the surface metric reveals two mechanisms: gradient-driven constriction at steep morphogen transitions and curvature-driven constriction near localized morphogen peaks. For frozen morphogen profiles in simple axisymmetric examples, the gradient-driven route gives exact algebraic contraction, while the curvature-driven route gives local exponential contraction.

papers.title: A Fused Gaussian Process Bandit Framework for Multi-Fidelity Bayesian Optimization
papers.abstract: Bayesian optimization (BO) is widely used to maximize expensive black-box functions when direct evaluation is costly. In many real-world applications, the high-fidelity objective can be approximated by a series of lower-fidelity models that provide partial but informative signals at substantially reduced cost. Multi-fidelity BO (MFBO) algorithms aim to strategically combine these information sources to achieve an optimal trade-off between accuracy and evaluation cost. However, existing MFBO methods often oversimplify the complex dependencies between fidelity levels or rely on heuristic acquisition functions that lack theoretical performance guarantees. To address these limitations, we introduce a new formulation of the MFBO problem as a fused Gaussian Process bandit and develop a corresponding Fused Gaussian Process Upper Confidence Bound (FGP-UCB) algorithm. Our approach accurately predicts the high-fidelity function by fusing multi-fidelity observations through an autoregressive Gaussian Process model and explicitly quantifies the uncertainty arising from parameter estimation across fidelity levels. The proposed method also provides theoretical simple-regret guarantees, overcoming a key limitation of existing MFBO algorithms that lack provable performance bounds. Effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated via both theoretical analysis and empirical studies.
